summary: Deep low-level analysis + roofline micro-analysis + brutal-critiqued extreme-TDD implementation plan to make WaaV Infer beat vLLM-Omni across all models/stages/quant/hardware
logs: Fanning out 10 deep-dive+design agents, each followed by a 2-hawk brutal critique panel.

9/10 gap dossiers survived analysis+critique. Synthesizing master plan.

plan.thesis: WaaV already OUT-DESIGNS vLLM-Omni in machinery but loses on DELIVERY: the recurring failure across all 9 gaps is the design-vs-wired trap (decode_committed_prefix seam wired but zero prod model overrides — CONFIRMED only arstep.rs:615 default + serve.rs:3416 test-double; StepBuckets/CascadeDag/LayeredAdmit/KvFirewall built+byte-tested with zero live serve-path callers; SDP AttnKernel::{Flash,Cudnn} collapse to FusedAuto). To BEAT vLLM-Omni we do NOT chase attention kernels (measured 1.5-5% of every model — a <1% net lever by ridge-433.5 physics) or fabricate throughput. We attack the ON-BOX MEASURED truth: B=1 decode is launch/CPU-bound (dia2 gpu_busy 0.06, ~380K tiny launches, ~12.3s GPU-idle), and TTFA == whole-utterance is the #1 realized-latency gap. The winning spine is four ordered moves, each byte-identical-by-default or an explicit WER/MOS-gated opt-in: (1) a WIRED-LEDGER discipline that makes dormancy a CI red-bar so every capability proves a LIVE serve-path caller; (2) kill the 12 per-frame GPU->CPU sync round-trips + stream first-audio early + extend byte-identical CUDA-graph coverage into the batched path — the launch/sync/latency levers that actually move GB10; (3) in-process multi-stage DAG (beats their 22GB per-process bug) + byte-identical cross-request flow batching + measure-gated width, all labeled THROUGHPUT/capacity not single-stream RTF and gated on measured fill; (4) quant/hardware coverage as an honest COVERAGE win with explicit projection-only exclusions. Governing law throughout: the invariant hierarchy byte-identity > state-safety > lockstep > OOM-floor > perf-levers; any lever that would violate a higher tier is refused at construction or routed to a stamped WER/MOS path, never silently. Every projection is re-derived from profiling/perf_equations.py against gb10_calibration.json (198.5 GB/s, 86.04 TFLOP/s, ridge 433.5) — and the datasheet 273e9 constant that poisons every duty projection (LIVE at engine.rs:1889) is corrected in Wave 0.

waves.wave: Wave 0 — Anti-dormancy discipline, roofline-honesty, and the empirical decision-gates that settle whole design families
waves.rationale: Nothing else ships durable value until four cheap, high-leverage, zero-accuracy-risk foundations exist: (a) the design-vs-wired trap becomes a CI red-bar (the ONE structural cause behind every gap); (b) the roofline math stops lying (the LIVE 273e9 datasheet bandwidth over-admits ~37.5% vs the 198.5 GB/s calibration — CONFIRMED at engine.rs:1889 + codec_ar_admission.rs:314, and admit_bandwidth is a perpetual no-op without a profiler-fed duty); (c) two empirical gates run FIRST because their outcome decides entire downstream families — the multinomial Philox category-count-invariance test (decides on-device sync-free sampling) and the shared stamp type surface (decides quant+native-precision+EP admission). These are prerequisites, not features.

waves.wave: Wave 1 — The measured single-stream bottleneck: sync elimination, first-audio streaming, and byte-identical graph coverage (the levers that actually beat vLLM-Omni on GB10)

waves.wave: Wave 2 — Throughput/concurrency capacity + in-process multi-stage (beat their 22GB per-process bug), byte-identical-first and measure-gated
waves.rationale: Where WaaV structurally beats vLLM-Omni: in-process single-CUDA-context multi-stage DAG (their 3x0.90-mem-fraction port would request ~351GB against GB10's 130.6GB shared pool and CRASH), and cross-request flow batching that stays byte-identical (their reassociation would flip our discrete codes). Every number here is labeled THROUGHPUT/per-GPU-capacity — NOT single-stream RTF (an isolated call has no co-resident to batch with) — and gated on MEASURED bucket-fill and per-model B64 records, never extrapolation past B24.

plan.conflict_resolutions:
INVARIANT HIERARCHY (highest wins; a lower-tier lever that would violate a higher tier is REFUSED at construction — typed CfgBatchRefusal / CausalDecoder sub-trait / MaskedCell — or routed to an EXPLICIT WER/MOS-gated opt-in, NEVER silently relaxed):
1. Byte-identity-by-default (accuracy + reproducibility golden gate) — arstep.rs:551-561, cfg_batch.rs:177.
2. Per-slot isolation + masked!=absent state-safety (privacy/correctness) — ring_kv MaskedCell append_where, ChannelId.
3. Lockstep 1-stride/tick (the batching contract) — Driver::tick.
4. Unified-pool OOM-safety (hard box-crash floor) — codec_ar_admission MIN_FREE_BYTES=28GiB (> the 21.7GiB S3Gen transient), the twice-crashed 170GB scar.
5. Perf levers (CUDA-graph, ragged/flow batch, quant, streaming, width) — LOWEST; each gated by 1-4.

CROSS-GAP CONFLICTS + RESOLUTIONS:
(C1) G1 streaming byte-identity vs the bit-law -> CAUSALITY-TYPED SPLIT decided by an EMPIRICAL test, not an assumption. Build the streaming-conv-STATE decoder (port the CONFIRMED-existing vibevoice SConv1d::forward_streaming into shared codec/mimi.rs) and RUN the pivotal byte-identity test against an INDEPENDENT whole-body golden (NEVER redefine decode_audio in terms of decode_streaming — the tautological-oracle trap). Branch A (byte-identical) ships golden-unchanged; Branch B (expected, given the length-dependent get_extra_padding_for_conv1d right-pad) is a one-time WER<0.005 re-baseline of the streaming golden; if neither holds -> WER/MOS relaxation or onboard a genuinely-causal codec (SNAC — CONFIRMED none shipped). CausalDecoder sub-trait makes a NonCausal model unable to fake incrementality.
(C2) G2 cross-request flow batch vs cfg_batch batch-2 refusal -> RESOLVED BY REGIME + by NOT folding CFG. Batch across REQUESTS (independent per-slot rows) while running each model's CFG as TWO batch-1 passes exactly like cfg_batch two_pass; NEVER fold CFG 2->2B. Byte-identical Design-B oracle (GB10-proven md==0.0 at B>=5) is the DEFAULT path; the WER/MOS Design-A path is used ONLY for oracle-FAIL / bf16/fp16 shapes, opt-in, per-precision stamped.
(C3) G1 streaming (latency, no coalescing) vs G2 flow-batch (throughput, ADDS a coalescing window) -> MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE per request: the flow-coalescer is DISABLED under any early-emit streaming path (enforced by test flow_coalescer_disabled_under_streaming). Latency path serves interactive; throughput path serves batch.
(C4) G3 sync-elimination 'unlocks graph -13.6%' vs graphable reality -> only dia2/csm graphable; qwen3/misotts/s2_pro/cosyvoice3 get the DIRECT sync win only (graph-compounding claim scoped to the graphable set). The multinomial category-count-invariance gate (W0.3) decides fully-on-device vs 1-scalar-D2H per model.
(C5) G4/G10 static-graph vs G2 ragged membership vs lockstep vs cfg_batch -> PER-SLOT B=1 CUDA-graph replay per ctx-bucket (NOT a shared padded batched grid — that puts the batch axis in a reducing GEMM AND padding perturbs active-row numerics). Capture mempool sized INSIDE VramAccountant + MIN_FREE_BYTES (the G4<->G5 OOM collision).
(C6) G5 multi-stage vs OOM vs ring-KV -> ONE process-wide VramAccountant summing per-stage weights+KV+transients inside MIN_FREE_BYTES; no full-engine-per-stage (reject vLLM's 22GB bug); CUDA-EVENT stream-ordered device-resident edges (not raw pointer handoff — the cross-thread race); per-slot ring-KV at native GQA g-heads.
(C7) G6 quant vs byte-identity -> quant/native-precision is a STATISTICAL-EQUIVALENCE (TOST/CI, not absolute-Δ<0.02 which refuses the dia2 0.0208 flagship) WER/MOS-stamped ADMISSION gate; byte-identity stays the default/verification mode. Fail-closed if no stamp and no fp32 sibling.
(C8) G9 width vs OOM vs byte-identity -> measure-gated per-model (no default>24 without a B64 codes-identical record) + MANDATORY load-time admission clamp fail-closed; quarantine the sync-heavy fleet until W1.1.
(C9) G5 DriftDetector (raw tick) vs G2/G9 batching (step-time legitimately grows with B) -> DriftDetector observes PER-ACTIVE-SLOT-NORMALIZED step time (batch-aware) so lockstep batch growth is not misread as drift and does not false-shed the streams W2.2/W2.3 batch.
(C10) G8 attention pin vs ridge physics -> attention is 1.5-5% of every model -> infra-only (ship the SDP shim, defer the levers behind a measured >15%-of-wall trigger); the is_causal encoder bug is fixed regardless.
(C11) Design-vs-wired (UNIVERSAL) -> the WIRED-LEDGER (W0.1) makes an empty live_callers() a CI red-bar and its exerciser drives the REAL serve.rs mux loop (not the #[cfg(test)] harness), so every capability across all waves proves a live serve-path caller exercised on the real loop; #[dormant] is permitted only with a milestone expiry.
STALE-SUMMARY CORRECTIONS FOLDED IN: DutyLedger IS wired live (engine.rs:1805 admit_bandwidth) — dynamic-IC and admit_layered are NEW consumers, not activations; the decode_committed_prefix LOOP-half is wired (serve.rs:999), the MODEL-half is the dead code (CONFIRMED zero prod overrides); F6_DECODE_CADENCE_FRAMES=8 actively gates serve.rs (not inert); the 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap is INFEASIBLE in tch (dropped, honest exclusion); GB10_PEAK_DRAM_BYTES_PER_S=273e9 IS a LIVE production constant (engine.rs:1889 + codec_ar_admission.rs:314), corrected to the 198.5 calibration in W0.2.
plan.coverage_attestation:
COVERAGE MATRIX (architecture x stage x quantization x hardware), with the wave that carries each cell and honest exclusions:

ARCHITECTURES:
- Codec-AR TTS (dia2/csm/qwen3/misotts/s2_pro/higgs/higgs_v2/neutts/vibevoice/indextts2/hibiki): sync-elimination (W1.1), causal streaming (W1.2 branch-decided per-codec), per-slot graph (W1.4, only dia2/csm graphable), width (W2.2), native precision (W3.2). ZONOS2 MoE expert-routing host reads EXCLUDED from W1.1 (not a sampler — a separate on-device grouped-expert dispatch gap).
- Continuous-flow TTS (cosyvoice3/dots/irodori): flow batching (W2.3, byte-identical on GB10-proven shapes, WER-gated for oracle-fail), sync-elimination on cosyvoice3 (W1.1, the #1 measured hotspot). OMNIVOICE discrete masked-diffusion backbone EXCLUDED from flow-fold (keeps two-batch-1 per cfg_batch).
- Enc-dec/CTC STT (whisper/moonshine/parakeet/cohere/canary/sensevoice/voxtral): quant admission (W3.1, dtype-seam largely already done), EP portability (W3.3), the Fish graph-capture-safe masked-ring decode is ALREADY LIVE (voxtral), bucketing added (W3.4).
STAGES: STT, AR/LLM backbone, flow/CFM, vocoder, codec-decode — all reachable; multi-stage cascade STT->LLM->TTS wired live (W2.4). Per-stage lockstep batching restricted to the AR ring family; flow/diffusion stay per-slot until W2.3 proves them (honest P1-PARTIAL preserved).
QUANTIZATIONS: fp32 + bf16 (Path-B native, W3.2 equivalence-stamped); fp16 + q4f16 (Path-A CUDA via the byte-identical exact-length ping-pong, W3.1); int8 (CPU via EpKind::Cpu stamp, W0.4/W3.3; int8-on-ORT-CUDA correctly rejected). Every lossy tier is WER/MOS-stamped, byte-identical stays default.
HARDWARE: GB10 CUDA sm_121 = primary, fully MEASURED (all Wave 1/2 wins). Path-A ORT CPU = proven today. XNNPACK/OpenVINO/ROCm/other EPs = wired-but-UNPROVEN-ON-SILICON until the arch-matched aarch64 CI dylib lands (W3.3 Step-0); all non-NVIDIA numbers are LABELED PROJECTION. Static1(NPU)->width 1 + reject-AR; Tens->[8,64]; Wide->[64,512] (W2.2, portable by DeviceCaps).

HONEST EXCLUSIONS (stated, not hidden):
1. 2nd-CUDA-stream mid-loop-decode overlap — INFEASIBLE in tch (no stream guard); dropped from W1.3.
2. Byte-identical streaming for the CURRENT Mimi fleet is DECISION-CONTINGENT (W1.2) — likely defers to a WER-gated re-baseline or a future SNAC onboarding; not asserted as shipped.
3. Non-causal S3Gen/chatterbox + cosyvoice3-CFM streaming — WER/MOS-gated opt-in only (may be ALL current codecs if Mimi proves non-causal).

plan.plan_red_team:
BRUTAL SELF-CRITIQUE OF THIS PLAN:
1. INHERITED-VERDICT RISK: I synthesized from dossiers + critics and spot-verified only ~6 load-bearing facts (decode_committed_prefix dead, forward_streaming exists, 273e9 live, StepBuckets/CascadeDag dormant, MIN_FREE_BYTES, sampling.rs primitives). I did NOT independently re-run the critic code-reads on e.g. whether whisper/moonshine dtype-seam is truly already-done, or whether admit_layered wiring regresses CodecArAdmission. The plan inherits any residual critic error. Mitigation: Wave-0 decision-gates ARE the empirical settlers, but W2.4/W3.1 carry unverified premises.
2. THE #1 WIN IS CONTINGENT: W1.2 (streaming) is the headline latency lever AND the direct vLLM-Omni-TTFP match, but the confirmed length-dependent Mimi right-pad makes the byte-identical branch UNLIKELY on the current fleet. If it falls to a WER-gated re-baseline, the 'byte-identical streaming' claim weakens to 'WER<0.005 streaming', and if WER regresses, first-audio for the causal fleet stalls entirely until a SNAC onboarding (scope creep not in this plan). The plan's marquee win is a coin-flip gated on one test.
3. THROUGHPUT WINS ARE SOFT: W2.2 (width>24) and W2.3 (flow batch) are measure-gated and fill-starved — on real ragged-T free-form voice at low concurrency (the actual realtime regime) both realize near-ZERO. The 'beat vLLM-Omni on throughput' story only materializes under high concurrent equal-T completion; I labeled it capacity-not-RTF, but a skeptic could say Wave 2 is largely defensive (byte-identity + OOM-safety + observability) rather than a speed win.
4. OVER-SCOPE: Wave 3 (G6 quant + G7 portability + G8 attention) is ~4 items for a COVERAGE win that does NOT move the GB10 vs-vLLM-Omni needle. G7 especially (CI dylib, CapabilityMatrix, new ORT load seam) is a large lift for projection-only silicon. A tighter plan might cut G7 to just the EpKind::Cpu type fix + honest matrix rows and defer the harness. I kept it for completeness but flag it as the first thing to cut under time pressure.
5. LEDGER BUREAUCRACY: W0.1 (WIRED-LEDGER) could ossify into process overhead that slows legitimate milestone staging; the linkme-gated-out-of-cfg(test) + call-graph reachability approach is asserted feasible but unproven — if reachability analysis is flaky, the gate becomes noise. And its own exerciser (drive the real serve loop) is non-trivial to build for every seam.
6. STREAMING-UNDER-LOAD REGRESSION: dropping the 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap means the mid-loop decode competes with the lockstep tick; under 24-slot concurrency the frame-deadline cap forces higher IC -> later first-audio exactly when it matters most. The plan mitigates but does not solve this; it is a real ceiling on the streaming win at scale.
7. CROSS-WAVE COUPLING UNDER-SPECIFIED: W2.4 DriftDetector-batch-awareness (C9) vs W2.2/W2.3 batch growth is a subtle co-design I flagged but did not fully sequence — if W2.4 lands before W2.2's normalization is proven, it will false-shed. I put W2.4 after W2.1 but the DriftDetector fix must co-land with W2.2/W2.3, which the linear wave ordering slightly obscures.
8. MISSING ADJACENT GAPS: zonos2 MoE on-device dispatch, the fully-speculative RAS path, and the dia2 sustained-RT (depformer TRT) are all excluded — a complete 'beat vLLM-Omni' claim on dia2 needs the sustained-RT gap that this plan explicitly punts. A reader could reasonably say dia2 is not actually realtime after all four waves.
9. NO EXPLICIT ROLLBACK/FLAG STRATEGY: every lever is gated, but I did not enumerate the env-flag/rollback matrix per item — production-readiness requires each new path be default-off-until-stamped with a named kill-switch, which I asserted in aggregate but did not itemize.
10. PROJECTION HONESTY vs SELLING: I re-labeled several dossier numbers (RTF->capacity, 27x->~0 launch-bound, 55x->host-restream-elim) per the critics — good — but the thesis still leads with 'BEAT vLLM-Omni', and the honest sum is: we MATCH their TTFP (contingent), BEAT their memory (W2.4, solid), MATCH their flow batching byte-identically (fill-limited), and BEAT their launch overhead (W1.1/W1.4, solid). The strongest, least-contingent wins are the memory (in-process DAG) and launch-elimination (graph+sync) axes; the plan should lead with those if the streaming test fails.

dossiers.current_state: TTFP == whole-utterance today, PROVEN by three live-path facts, not summary trust: (1) serve.rs:1003-1010 `drain_finished_stream` is the ONLY place PCM reaches the wire — it fires only when `s.accum.done`; (2) the mid-loop F6 seam serve.rs:991-1001 calls `stream_committed_prefix`→`model.decode_committed_prefix` (serve.rs:1051) but NO production model overrides it — grep across crates/ shows the only override is the test at serve.rs:3416 and cuda_torch_csm_streaming.rs asserts csm/dia2 INHERIT the default no-op; arstep.rs:615-624 default returns `(Vec::new(), committed_frames)` = commits nothing; (3) engine.rs `serve_codec_ar_stream` explicitly DROPS codec deltas from the audio wire — `EgressEvent::Delta(Frame::Codec(_)) => return true` (~line 2331) so only PCM (produced at drain) is ever sent. So F6_DECODE_CADENCE_FRAMES=8 (serve.rs:1039) and CHUNK_SAMPLES=480 (codec_ar_batcher.rs:52) are inert w.r.t. TTFP; CHUNK_SAMPLES only paces already-decoded whole-body PCM on the wire. The WS wire itself is ALREADY streaming (ws.rs:443-465 forwards each StreamItem::Chunk to the socket the instant it lands); only the REST path (lib.rs:957) drains to one buffer. So the gap is purely the RUNTIME producing zero early PCM — the wire is ready. MEASURED TTFP (== wall drain time, perf/path-b/*/record.json, ridge 433.5 FLOP/byte / 86.04 TFLOP/s bf16 / 198.5 GB/s calib): dia2 15349 ms (RTF 2.231, 6.88 s audio, Mimi 12.5 Hz→86 frames→178.5 ms/frame step, rtf_frame 2.23), hibiki 4062 ms (RTF 1.0156, 4.0 s, 50 frames→81.2 ms/frame, rtf_frame 1.015), cosyvoice3 3337 ms (RTF 0.670, 4.98 s, ~62 tok→53.8 ms/frame, rtf_frame 0.67). ttfa_ms is null in every record (no model streams). Codec causality (backend-torch/src/codec/): Mimi (mimi.rs:192 `decode(&self,codes)` — STATELESS, re-runs sliding-window-causal transformer over positions 0..seq + SEANet SConv/SConvTranspose each call) is used by dia2/csm/hibiki; conv.rs header confirms MimiConv is temporally causal (left-pad + `_get_extra_padding_for_conv1d` right-pad). CAUSAL family = Mimi/DAC/SNAC SEANet (left-pad convs). NON-CAUSAL = chatterbox S3Gen (chatterbox.rs:1986-2012: bidirectional UpsampleConformer + bidirectional CFM U-Net + overlap-add ISTFT) and cosyvoice3's CFM flow estimator (its HiFT vocoder is causal, cosyvoice3.rs:477 CausalHiFTGenerator, but the upstream CFM over the whole mel is non-causal → end-to-end non-causal). CRITICAL nuance the dead seam never distinguished: the current stateless `MimiDecoder::decode` makes a NAIVE prefix re-decode diverge (arstep.rs:608-610: differs at sample 0 in bf16 AND f32 — length-dependent right-pad + kernel-reduction-order non-associativity across shapes), but a proper streaming-conv-STATE decode (the moshi StreamingConv1d formulation that ALREADY EXISTS at vibevoice.rs:379-411 SConv1d::forward_streaming, whose header line 314 asserts 'streaming cache is irrelevant to the VALUES' = byte-equal to non-streaming) is NEVER used by the shared codec/mimi.rs. That is the unexploited byte-identical lever.
dossiers.root_cause: Two stacked root causes: (1) the decode_committed_prefix streaming seam (arstep.rs:615) is dead — no production model overrides it, so all PCM is produced only at drain (serve.rs:1003) and codec deltas are dropped from the wire (engine.rs ~2331); (2) the bit-identity law was over-generalized against a length-parameterized STATELESS Mimi decoder (mimi.rs:192, positions 0..seq + shape-dependent kernel reduction), so even causal codecs looked un-streamable — while the byte-identical streaming-conv primitive that fixes exactly this (vibevoice.rs SConv1d::forward_streaming, header line 314 'streaming cache is irrelevant to the values') was never wired into the shared codec decoder or the seam. For truly non-causal S3Gen/CFM the law is correctly binding, so first-audio there needs a consciously WER/MOS-gated relaxation that was never built.

designs.name: Design A — Engage decode_committed_prefix on CAUSAL Mimi via per-slot streaming-conv state (byte-identical first-audio; the honest win)
designs.mechanism: Give the shared Mimi decoder a stateful streaming twin and override the dead seam for the Mimi fleet (dia2/csm/hibiki). Step 1: add `MimiDecoder::decode_streaming(&mut self, codes_chunk, state: &mut MimiStreamState)` in codec/mimi.rs mirroring vibevoice.rs:379-411/440-454 forward_streaming — carry (a) the transformer ring-KV for the sliding-window-causal attention (mimi.rs:208 loop; reuse the per-slot ring the AR backbone already uses), (b) per-SConv1d left-context tensors and per-SConvTranspose1d input cache, (c) a running position counter so positions are absolute (chunk-local offset), NOT 0..seq. Step 2: override `decode_committed_prefix` (arstep.rs:615) on TorchDia2/Csm/Hibiki ArStepModel impls: given committed_frames C and body-so-far, feed frames [C..C_new_final) through decode_streaming where C_new_final = len - codec_right_context (Mimi SEANet receptive field on the RIGHT is 0 for the causal convs, so C_new_final == current body len; the only holdback is the transformer sliding-window edge, which is fully left-causal → holdback 0). Return (pcm_delta, C_new_final). The serve loop (serve.rs:991-999) already calls this every F6_DECODE_CADENCE_FRAMES=8 strides and ships the delta as Frame::Pcm through the persistent StreamEgress → ws.rs:443 forwards it live. Step 3 (the pivotal correctness pin): the streaming decode's reduction order must equal the whole-body decode's. Because that is NOT guaranteed across shapes, run each streaming chunk at a FIXED codec_chunk_frames shape and capture it as a CUDA-graph (nn/cuda_graph.rs already does byte-identical capture with Philox snapshot) so every chunk hits the SAME kernel/algorithm and the SAME rounding — then Σ chunks is byte-identical to a whole-body decode ALSO run through the same fixed-chunk streaming path. If the TDD gate proves the fixed-chunk streaming path is additionally byte-identical to the existing one-shot batch `decode_audio` golden, ship with the golden unchanged; if it diverges by ULPs, re-baseline the Mimi golden to the streaming decode (WER-neutral, one-time) and make decode_audio itself call decode_streaming with a single whole-body chunk so reference==streaming by construction.
designs.projected_win: TTFP collapses from whole-utterance to initial_codec_chunk_frames (IC) of AR steps + one chunk decode. Basis: B=1 AR step is memory/launch-bound (AI~1-2 << ridge 433.5 → per perf_equations roofline, step time is fixed launch+KV-bandwidth, independent of how much downstream body remains), so producing audio after IC frames instead of N frames is pure latency-to-first with no per-step penalty. hibiki (measured 81.2 ms/frame): IC=2 → 2×81.2 + ~12 ms Mimi chunk-decode ≈ 174 ms TTFP vs 4062 ms today = 23× earlier, emitting 160 ms of audio; IC=4 → ~337 ms. csm (Mimi 12.5 Hz, occ 0.97/gpu_busy 0.248 launch-bound, step ~80 ms order): IC=4 ≈ 330 ms. dia2 (measured 178.5 ms/frame): IC=4 → 4×178.5 + 12 ≈ 726 ms TTFP vs 15349 ms = 21× earlier — HONEST caveat: dia2 rtf_frame=2.23 so after first audio the stream underruns until the committed graph/TRT work (memory: dia2 best 1.86) lands; first-audio is real, sustained-RT is a separate gap. Chunk-decode floor ~10-20 ms (Mimi decode is itself launch-bound, many tiny convs) argues IC≥2 to amortize the decode launch overhead across the 8-stride cadence.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST (byte-identical, deterministic): (1) `mimi_streaming_conv_state_decode_is_bit_identical_to_whole_body` on REAL dia2/csm Mimi weights — build a body, decode via decode_streaming in fixed IC-frame chunks carrying MimiStreamState, assert concat == MimiDecoder::decode(whole) byte-for-byte (max|Δ|=0). THIS TEST DECIDES the design: if it passes at fixed chunk shape, ship golden-unchanged; if it fails, it quantifies the ULP gap and forces the re-baseline branch (then the gate becomes Σstreaming==whole-body-streaming, and a separate WER(streaming vs old-golden)<0.005 gate proves the re-baseline is quality-neutral). (2) `dia2_decode_committed_prefix_concat_equals_decode_audio` — drive the serve.rs mid-loop path across cadence probes, assert Σ pcm_delta + drain-tail == decode_audio(full_body) byte-for-byte (the arstep.rs:598-604 law, reusing the existing serve.rs:2248 default-seam harness pattern). (3) reuse cuda_torch_csm_streaming.rs but FLIP its expectation: csm/dia2 now emit multiple genuine segments (assert ≥2 segments, first_visible_body_len << full). PERF gate: `ttfa_ms` populated in record.json and TTFP < 400 ms for IC≤4 on hibiki/csm; a regression gate that whole-utterance WER/byte-output is unchanged (no accuracy cost).
designs.coverage: Applies to the CAUSAL codec family: every Mimi-decoder model (dia2, csm, hibiki) + generalizes to DAC/SNAC SEANet (same left-pad causal conv structure) with a per-decoder StreamState. Made universal by putting decode_streaming on the SHARED codec/mimi.rs decoder + a shared MimiStreamState so any Mimi model inherits it for free (same pattern that de-duplicated the decoder across dia2/csm). Quantization: orthogonal — the streaming path is dtype-agnostic (bf16/f32/q4f16); the fixed-chunk CUDA-graph pins reduction order per dtype so byte-identity holds per precision. Hardware: Path-B (tch/CUDA) only for the graph pin; Path-A (ORT) models can use the same seam without the graph (accept the whole-body reference as decode_streaming(whole)). Scoped OUT: non-causal S3Gen/CFM (Design B).
designs.risks_conflicts: (1) Byte-identity risk is REAL and gated, not assumed: the fixed-chunk-shape requirement is because cross-shape cuDNN reduction order differs (the exact reason the naive seam was retired); if even fixed-chunk streaming can't match the one-shot batch golden, Design A must re-baseline the golden — an explicit, WER-gated, one-time change, never silent. (2) ring-KV: reuses the per-slot ring (GQA-native, arstep invariant) for the codec transformer — must allocate a SECOND ring for the codec-decoder attention distinct from the AR backbone ring (ChannelId/MaskedCell keeps them state-safe). (3) lockstep 1-stride/tick: the mid-loop decode runs on the cadence (every 8 strides) so it does not violate one-step-per-tick, but a heavy chunk decode inside the shared tick stalls ALL slots — mitigated by Design C's 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap. (4) cfg_batch: unaffected — codec decode is post-sampling, single-batch, no CFG GEMM. (5) design-vs-wired: this DOES wire into the live path (serve.rs:991 already calls the seam; ws.rs:443 already ships PCM deltas) — the override is the only missing link; REST (lib.rs:957) still drains to one buffer so REST TTFP is unchanged until Design C's chunked-transfer.

designs.name: Design B — WER/MOS-gated left-context streaming for NON-causal vocoders (S3Gen / CFM): the one conscious bit-law relaxation
designs.mechanism: For chatterbox S3Gen and cosyvoice3 CFM — where arstep.rs:557-561 correctly proves no byte-identical prefix exists — add an OPT-IN streaming decode path that is WER/MOS-gated, default stays whole-body byte-identical. Port the vLLM-Omni chunk-knob taxonomy as explicit fields on the model: initial_codec_chunk_frames IC, codec_left_context_frames L, codec_right_holdback_frames R, ref_code_on_first_chunk. Override `decode_committed_prefix` on ChatterboxTts (currently inherits the honest whole-body default at chatterbox.rs:2002) ONLY when a `streaming_relaxed` flag is set: on probe k, decode the window body[C-L .. C_new] where C_new = current_len - R, run the S3Gen conditional_decoder (chatterbox.rs:1328) over [C-L..C_new], then EMIT only samples corresponding to frames [C..C_new] (drop the L-frame left-context warmup and hold back R frames whose output still depends on not-yet-arrived future frames). ref_code_on_first_chunk: on the first chunk prepend the reference speech codes so the conformer/CFM sees speaker context (kills first-chunk timbre drift). For cosyvoice3, the CFM estimator runs its N flow-steps over the [C-L..C_new] mel window with left-context latents carried; HiFT (causal, cosyvoice3.rs:477) then decodes byte-cleanly on top. The drain flush still decodes the WHOLE body via decode_audio for the final tail, but under streaming_relaxed the committed prefix samples are the streamed (approximate) ones — so the stream is NOT Σ==whole-body; the accuracy contract shifts from byte-identity to WER/MOS.
designs.projected_win: cosyvoice3 (measured RTF 0.670, 53.8 ms/frame, keeps up): IC=4, L=8, R=2 → first flow+HiFT chunk decode over ~14 frames ≈ (4×53.8 AR) + ~60-100 ms chunked-CFM+HiFT ≈ 275-320 ms TTFP vs 3337 ms today = ~11× earlier, sustained (rtf_frame 0.67 leaves headroom for the L-context recompute overhead — the CFM redoes L frames each chunk, a ~ (L+C)/C ≈ 3× flow-decode multiplier that 0.67 RTF absorbs up to ~IC=4/L=8). chatterbox S3Gen: TTFP ~few hundred ms depending on IC/R; win is qualitative (whole-utterance → sub-400 ms) and MUST be MOS-verified because bidirectional CFM/conformer over a truncated window changes the waveform. Basis: left-context recompute cost is the trade — projected via perf_equations frame_budget with the (L+C)/C recompute multiplier against measured per-frame step.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST — accuracy gate is WER/MOS, NOT byte-identical (the conscious relaxation): (1) `chatterbox_streaming_relaxed_wer_within_gate` — synth a fixed corpus (LibriSpeech-derived prompts) via (a) whole-body decode_audio and (b) streaming_relaxed IC/L/R path; transcribe both with a fixed ASR (reuse the voxtral/whisper gate harness) and assert WER(streaming) - WER(whole) < 0.01 AND a MOS proxy (mel-cepstral distortion or the existing supertonic-style maxΔ-on-mel) below a pinned threshold. Sweep L∈{4,8,16}, R∈{0,2,4} to find the smallest L/R meeting the gate. (2) `chatterbox_default_is_still_byte_identical` — with streaming_relaxed OFF, assert decode_committed_prefix commits nothing and drain == decode_audio byte-for-byte (the default MUST NOT regress; reuse chatterbox.rs:3323 existing test). (3) A REFUSAL test: streaming_relaxed requires an explicit config/flag; assert it is never enabled silently (mirrors the quant-admission accuracy-stamp gate). PERF gate: cosyvoice3 TTFP < 350 ms, sustained rtf_frame < 1 with L-recompute.
designs.coverage: Scoped to non-causal vocoders: chatterbox S3Gen + cosyvoice3 CFM, generalizes to any bidirectional-CFM/BigVGAN-overlap-add TTS (the family arstep.rs:558 enumerates). Universal within that family via the shared IC/L/R knob struct + a `NonCausalStreamDecode` trait method any such model implements. Quantization: orthogonal (WER gate re-run per precision — a q4f16 streaming path needs its OWN WER stamp, per the quant-admission invariant). Hardware: Path-B; Path-A CFM models could adopt but each needs its own WER stamp. Honestly SCOPED (not universal to Mimi models — those take the byte-identical Design A instead; applying B to a causal codec would needlessly relax a codec that can be byte-exact).
designs.risks_conflicts: (1) DIRECTLY bends the byte-identity law — this is the ONE sanctioned place, and it MUST be (a) opt-in behind an explicit flag, (b) WER/MOS-stamped before admit, (c) default-off so the shipped default stays byte-identical. Any silent enablement is a defect. (2) cfg_batch (cfg_batch.rs:177): chatterbox/cosyvoice3 CFG runs the estimator batch-2; a chunked CFG flow over a left-context window may hit the SAME batch-2 reassociation refusal (maxΔ 3.9e-4 TF32) — the streaming path must run CFG the SAME way as whole-body (or accept it inside the WER gate, which it can since we're already WER-not-byte here). (3) lockstep/ring-KV: S3Gen decode is not the AR ring — it's a separate vocoder call; the L-context recompute must not corrupt the AR slot's ring state (isolate vocoder state per slot). (4) design-vs-wired: wires into serve.rs:991 seam like A, but gated by the flag; REST path needs Design C. (5) Risk that MOS regresses audibly at aggressive IC/R — the gate is the backstop; if no (L,R) meets it, the model stays whole-body (honest fallback, not a silent degrade).

designs.name: Design C — The wire+schedule substrate: load-adaptive dynamic-IC, 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap, ship codec deltas, real chunked REST
designs.mechanism: The substrate BOTH A and B ride on — closes the design-vs-wired trap and ports the remaining vLLM-Omni knobs. (1) Un-drop codec deltas: engine.rs (~2331) currently returns early on `Frame::Codec` — add an opt-in codec-passthrough wire mode (for consumers that decode client-side) so codec deltas can ship too; keep PCM-decode default. (2) Load-adaptive dynamic-IC: replace the inert const F6_DECODE_CADENCE_FRAMES=8 (serve.rs:1039) with a per-slot adaptive cadence driven by the live cohort width — under low load use IC=2 (min TTFP), as active slots approach MAX_SLOTS=24 (codec_ar_batcher.rs) raise IC (fewer mid-loop decode calls competing for the shared lockstep tick), exactly vLLM-Omni's dynamic initial_codec_chunk. Compute the schedule from the admission ledger (admission.rs DutyLedger is BUILT but unwired — wire it here as the load signal). (3) 2nd CUDA stream overlap: run the mid-loop codec decode (stream_committed_prefix, serve.rs:1049) on a SECOND CUDA stream so chunk-k decode overlaps AR tick-(k+1) on the main stream — the AR step is launch/memory-bound with 60%+ GPU idle (dia2 gpu_busy 0.525, cosyvoice3 0.278) so the decode fits in the idle shadow at ~zero added wall. Use a per-slot event to keep the decode's read of committed body race-free vs the ring writer. (4) Real chunked REST: lib.rs:957 drains to one buffer — add SSE/chunked-transfer so /v1/audio/speech streams PCM chunks as they land (WS already does via ws.rs:443). (5) Port the graph-safe knobs: LRU graph cache + RNG-buffer-refill-before-replay + scalar-placeholder runtime controls (cfg/sigma/temp tunable without recapture) into nn/cuda_graph.rs so the fixed-chunk streaming graphs (Design A) and CFM step counts (Design B) don't thrash-recapture (dots.rs re-capture-on-total-change is the anti-pattern to avoid).
designs.projected_win: Overlap: hides the 10-20 ms/chunk Mimi decode inside the AR idle shadow → removes it from TTFP and from per-tick stall; on dia2 (52.5% GPU idle) the decode is fully shadowed → TTFP stays ~IC×step with no decode adder (Design A hibiki IC=2: 162 ms instead of 174 ms) and the shared cohort tick is not stalled by mid-loop decode (protects the other ≤24 slots). Dynamic-IC: bounds the mid-loop decode frequency so at 24 concurrent slots the aggregate decode load stays a small fraction of the tick (keeps the measured 55×@64 batching win intact). Chunked REST: brings REST TTFP to parity with WS (today REST TTFP == whole-utterance regardless of A/B). Basis: gpu_busy fractions from records + the launch-bound AR classification (AI<<ridge).
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `codec_delta_passthrough_roundtrip` — with codec-passthrough on, Σ shipped codec deltas == whole body codes byte-for-byte (extends egress.rs Σ-deltas==full invariant to the codec wire). (2) `second_stream_decode_is_bit_identical_and_race_free` — run the mid-loop decode on stream 2 under a torture loop of concurrent ring writes; assert the emitted PCM == single-stream decode byte-for-byte (the 2nd stream must not read a half-written frame) — deterministic gate. (3) `dynamic_ic_never_starves_cohort` — 24 concurrent slots, assert per-tick wall stays within the frame budget (perf_equations frame_budget keeps_up=true) as IC adapts, and that Σ output per slot is unchanged (byte-identical) regardless of the IC schedule chosen (IC is a latency knob, MUST NOT change bytes). (4) `rest_chunked_transfer_streams_before_drain` — assert first REST chunk arrives at t < whole-utterance. PERF gate: overlap removes the decode adder from measured TTFP; 24-slot aggregate throughput unchanged vs pre-C baseline.
designs.coverage: UNIVERSAL substrate — applies to every codec-AR model (causal via A, non-causal via B) and both wire surfaces (WS + REST). Dynamic-IC + overlap are model-agnostic (operate at the serve-loop/CUDA-stream layer, not the model). LRU-graph-cache/scalar-placeholder benefits all 4 graphable models (dia2/csm/omnivoice/dots) + the new streaming graphs. Quantization/hardware-agnostic (scheduling + streams are below the dtype layer; Path-A gets chunked-REST + codec-passthrough but not the 2nd-stream overlap, which is CUDA-only).
designs.risks_conflicts: (1) 2nd CUDA stream is the sharpest risk: reading the still-growing ring body from a concurrent stream can race the AR writer → MUST use per-slot events + read only up to committed_frames (never the in-flight frame); the race test is the gate. This touches ChannelId/MaskedCell state-safety — the committed-frames boundary is the safe read horizon. (2) Dynamic-IC must be a pure latency knob: byte output MUST be independent of the IC schedule (gate 3) — else two runs of the same request differ, breaking reproducibility. (3) lockstep: dynamic-IC changes decode FREQUENCY not stride cadence — one AR step per tick is preserved. (4) cfg_batch: untouched (scheduling layer). (5) design-vs-wired: this IS the wiring fix — it activates the DutyLedger (admission.rs, built-but-unwired) as the load signal and turns the inert F6 cadence const into a live control; without C, A and B stall the shared cohort tick and leave REST non-streaming.

dossiers.recommended: Ship A + C together as the primary deliverable; B as the fast follow. Design A is the highest-value, lowest-risk win: it is BYTE-IDENTICAL (zero philosophy change, the gap's stated goal-a), covers the largest fleet (every Mimi model: dia2/csm/hibiki + trivially DAC/SNAC), and resurrects genuinely-dead machinery (decode_committed_prefix + the already-present vibevoice streaming-conv primitive). Its projected win is a clean 21-23× earlier first-audio (hibiki 4062→~174 ms, csm ~330 ms) with no accuracy cost — GATED by the one pivotal test (mimi_streaming_conv_state_decode_is_bit_identical_to_whole_body) that honestly decides golden-unchanged vs a WER-neutral one-time re-baseline. A is inert on the live path without C (the mid-loop decode would stall the shared 24-slot cohort tick and REST would still drain-buffer), so C is a hard co-requisite, not optional — C is also where the built-but-unwired DutyLedger/admission machinery finally gets a live driver. Design B is essential for the non-causal fleet (chatterbox/cosyvoice3, ~40% of the flagship TTS models) and is the ONLY place the byte-law is consciously relaxed, but it carries real MOS risk and a per-precision WER-stamp burden, so it should land second behind the byte-identical A+C once its WER/MOS gate is proven. Net: A+C makes the causal fleet stream first-audio in a few hundred ms with the byte-identity law fully intact; B extends it to the non-causal fleet under an explicit, gated, opt-in relaxation — together matching vLLM-Omni's TTFP while preserving WaaV's byte-identical-by-default invariant everywhere it is physically achievable.
dossiers.other_gaps_found: (1) The 12 sync-round-tripping models (cosyvoice3.rs:331 full Vec<f64> D2H/step; s2_pro/csm/misotts/qwen3_tts) flush the pipeline per frame — this interacts with G1: the mid-loop decode probe competes with these per-frame D2H stalls on the shared lockstep tick, so streaming TTFP for those models will be gated by the sync stall until on-device sample_token is wired (the primitives exist but aren't called). (2) DutyLedger/DriftDetector/LayeredAdmit (admission.rs) and the step-bucket flow batcher (cohort.rs/subbucket.rs) are built + byte-tested but have ZERO live driver — Design C is the natural place to finally wire the DutyLedger as the dynamic-IC load signal. (3) dia2 rtf_frame=2.23 means streaming gives early first-audio but then UNDERRUNS — G1 (TTFP) and the sustained-RT gap (memory: dia2 depformer TRT, task #133) are orthogonal and both needed for a usable dia2 stream; do not let a TTFP win mask that dia2 still isn't real-time. (4) cosyvoice3's Kernel2 (30%/862 ms, launch-bound BinaryElementWise, worst sync hotspot) is on the CFM/vocoder path that Design B chunks — chunking it repeatedly (L-context recompute) could amplify that launch-bound cost; the frame_budget gate must include the recompute multiplier. (5) nn/cuda_graph.rs has NO shape bucketing (exact-shape B=1) — Design A's fixed-chunk streaming graphs and Design C's LRU cache must add bucketing without the dots.rs recapture-thrash anti-pattern.

per_design.design_name: Design A — Engage decode_committed_prefix on CAUSAL Mimi via per-slot streaming-conv state
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The design's central premise cites vibevoice.rs:314 as proof that a streaming-conv decode is 'byte-equal to non-streaming' ('streaming cache is irrelevant to the VALUES'). This is a MISREAD and I verified it in code: the header says the cache is irrelevant *because vibevoice runs the NON-streaming path* — it is NOT a byte-equality proof for forward_streaming vs forward. Concretely SConv1d::forward (vibevoice.rs:326-335) adds a length-dependent RIGHT pad via get_extra_padding_for_conv1d that forward_streaming (line 411) omits, and Mimi's own decoder (mimi.rs:192-215) runs positions 0..seq (relative, not absolute) — so a chunked streaming decode is NOT trivially the same graph. Worse, there is a LIVE non-determinism scar the design underweights: vibevoice.rs:322-368 documents that cuDNN picks an atomicAdd (run-to-run non-deterministic) conv algorithm for VAE conv shapes, which forced the with_deterministic_conv thread-local pin — so even at a FIXED chunk shape the streaming decode is NOT byte-stable run-to-run unless deterministic conv is explicitly enabled; a CUDA-graph replay freezes ONE captured launch but the whole-body reference decode (different shape) may still use the atomicAdd algo, so the 'ship golden-unchanged' branch is unlikely to hold. The re-baseline fallback also contains a logical gap: the design says decode_audio should call decode_streaming with 'a single whole-body chunk' so reference==streaming — but Σ(fixed-IC-frame chunks) has a DIFFERENT per-call conv shape than one whole-body chunk, so their reduction orders differ and Σ(IC-chunks) != decode_streaming(whole). The byte-identity gate as written cannot pass. The dia2 projection is HONESTLY caveated (rtf_frame 2.23 → underrun after first audio) and the roofline basis (B=1 AR step launch/memory-bound, per-step cost independent of remaining body, AI<<433.5) is sound, so the TTFP-first claim itself is real. Nothing here breaks lockstep, cfg_batch (codec decode is post-sampling, single-batch), or ChannelId state-safety.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Drop the vibevoice:314 'byte-equal' claim as a premise — treat RED test #1 as the sole decider, which the design already does; but FIX the re-baseline branch: define decode_audio == Σ over the SAME fixed IC-frame streaming chunks (a fixed conv reduction unit), NOT decode_streaming(one whole-body chunk); only then is Σ(streaming)==reference byte-identical by construction. (2) Wrap the streaming decode in with_deterministic_conv (the existing pin) — otherwise the atomicAdd cuDNN scar makes the SEANet convs run-to-run non-byte-stable and the whole gate is meaningless. (3) Allocate a SECOND per-slot ring for the Mimi decode transformer (distinct from the AR backbone ring) with absolute positions carried in MimiStreamState (mimi.rs currently uses relative 0..seq). (4) Add the WER(streaming vs old-golden)<0.005 gate on the re-baseline branch as stated, and land a per-tick-stall guard (heavy chunk decode inside the shared lockstep tick stalls all ≤24 slots — needs Design C overlap or an explicit budget cap).

per_design.design_name: Design B — WER/MOS-gated left-context streaming for NON-causal vocoders (S3Gen / CFM)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Structurally this is the correctly-scoped, sanctioned relaxation: default-off, opt-in flag, WER/MOS-stamped, the non-causal default (chatterbox S3Gen inherits the honest whole-body seam) stays byte-identical — and the arstep.rs law text explicitly blesses exactly this (non-causal decoders MUST NOT fake incrementality unless gated). It does NOT silently break byte-identity. The real flaws are in the accuracy GATE sufficiency, not the invariant: (a) The MOS proxy proposed (mel-cepstral distortion / maxΔ-on-mel + WER<0.01) is INSUFFICIENT to catch the specific artifact this design creates — a spectral/phase DISCONTINUITY at the seam where the streamed approximate committed prefix meets the whole-body-decoded exact tail (the design itself states 'the stream is NOT Σ==whole-body', so a boundary click is possible). WER on ASR tokens and averaged MCD both routinely pass through an audible click. (b) cfg_batch conflict is acknowledged but the resolution is hand-waved: chatterbox/cosyvoice3 CFG runs the estimator batch-2 and cfg_batch.rs:177 REFUSES the batch-2-GEMM (verified: BatchAxisReducedInGemm, flips codes maxΔ 3.9e-4 TF32). The design says 'run CFG the same way as whole-body OR accept it inside the WER gate' — but a chunked CFG flow over a left-context window is a NEW batch/shape configuration whose reassociation is not the same as whole-body, so 'run it the same way' is not automatically available; this needs to be pinned, not deferred to the WER gate. (c) The cosyvoice3 sustained-RT projection leans on the (L+C)/C≈3x flow recompute multiplier being absorbed by RTF 0.67 — plausible but the 3x is only for L=8/C=4; larger L breaks keep-up, and the projection doesn't bound the CFM N-step count which dominates flow cost.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Add a seam/discontinuity detector to the gate (spectral-flux or phase-continuity at chunk boundaries, or crossfade the approximate-prefix→exact-tail join) — WER+MCD alone must not be the sole admit stamp. (2) Pin the chunked CFG to run cond/uncond as two batch-1 passes exactly like cfg_batch::two_pass mandates (backbone as two batch-1 forwards, fused work per-position) so the left-context CFG never enters a batch-axis reduction; don't rely on the WER gate to paper over a batch-2 reassociation. (3) Re-run the WER/MOS stamp per precision (q4f16 needs its own stamp — the design says this, keep it hard). (4) Bound the CFM N-step recompute in the sustained-RT projection and add the honest fallback (if no (L,R) meets the gate, stay whole-body) as an enforced code path, not just prose.

per_design.design_name: Design C — wire+schedule substrate: load-adaptive dynamic-IC, 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap, ship codec deltas, chunked REST
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: SHARPEST FLAW — a cross-design contradiction that makes gate #3 UNWRITABLE as stated: Design A's byte-identity depends on a FIXED conv chunk shape (reduction order is cuDNN-shape-dependent, the exact reason the naive seam was retired and the reason A needs a fixed-chunk CUDA-graph). Design C's dynamic-IC VARIES the chunk-frame count under load. Varying IC → varying conv input length → varying cuDNN algo/reduction order → the emitted PCM bytes CHANGE with the IC schedule. So test #3 ('Σ output per slot is byte-identical regardless of the IC schedule chosen') cannot be made to pass on top of the real conv streaming decode — it is a test that cannot be written. This also breaks the reproducibility invariant (two runs of the same request under different load emit different bytes). SECOND real flaw: the 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap runs the codec decode concurrently, but the byte-identity of that decode requires the DETERMINISTIC_CONV thread-local (vibevoice.rs:337, verified) to be SET on whatever thread/stream drives the decode; a thread-local flag does NOT propagate to a second stream driven from another thread, so the overlapped decode silently reverts to the atomicAdd non-deterministic conv algo and diverges — test #2 ('2nd-stream decode is bit-identical') would fail for a reason the design doesn't name. The race-horizon reasoning (read only up to committed_frames, per-slot event) is correct and does respect the ChannelId/MaskedCell committed boundary. Codec-passthrough Σ==whole-body-codes is trivially true (codes are post-sampling, already byte-exact). Chunked REST and DutyLedger-as-load-signal are sound and don't touch accuracy.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) DECOUPLE the load-adaptive EMISSION cadence from the byte-determining conv reduction unit: dynamic-IC may only change HOW OFTEN decode_committed_prefix is called / how many fixed-size conv windows are batched per call — the internal conv must always step a FIXED window granularity so Σ is shape-stable and IC is a pure latency knob. Only then can gate #3 be written to pass. Without this, dynamic-IC is incompatible with Design A and must be dropped to a constant. (2) Propagate deterministic-conv onto the overlap stream/thread (call with_deterministic_conv inside the decode closure that runs on stream 2), else the overlapped decode is not byte-identical — make test #2 the gate for this. (3) Keep the committed_frames read-horizon + per-slot event (correct as specified). (4) Codec-passthrough must be labeled opt-in/non-default (it is) and must not be the audio wire for PCM consumers.

per_design.design_name: Design A — Engage decode_committed_prefix on CAUSAL Mimi via per-slot streaming-conv state
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Core diagnosis is CORRECT and verified: mimi.rs:192 decode is stateless-whole-sequence, and the arstep.rs docstring's own empirical note ('differs at sample 0 in both bf16 and f32') is a SHAPE-dependent cuDNN/SDPA reduction-order artifact (shorter seq -> different mask shape -> different algo), NOT a causality violation — so a fixed-chunk-shape + graph-pinned streaming-state decode over the causal Mimi (sliding_window causal mask, left-pad SEANet) CAN be byte-identical. Wiring claim is TRUE (serve.rs:997 calls seam; ws.rs ships PCM deltas). Perf projection is honest (B=1 AR is launch/memory-bound at AI<<433.5, so IC-frames-to-first is pure latency-to-first; dia2 rtf_frame=2.23 sustained-underrun is explicitly caveated). FLAWS: (1) The extra-right-pad divergence is not merely ULP: SConv1d.forward adds get_extra_padding_for_conv1d (length-dependent RIGHT pad) that forward_streaming omits (vibevoice.rs:400-408), so Sigma-streaming will NOT equal the EXISTING one-shot decode_audio golden at chunk boundaries — the re-baseline branch is the EXPECTED path, not the exception, and it re-baselines dia2 (608 byte-identical tests) + csm (4000) + hibiki goldens = large blast radius on a heavily-verified surface. (2) The proposed 'make decode_audio itself call decode_streaming with a single whole-body chunk so reference==streaming by construction' DESTROYS the independent oracle — it makes the byte-identity test tautological/vacuous (a bug in decode_streaming is inherited by the reference and passes silently), directly violating the force-solo independent-reference discipline that caught the 8 cross-runtime bugs. (3) Mimi transformer is h==kvh (no GQA, mimi.rs:123) so it CANNOT reuse the GQA-native AR backbone ring as implied; needs a separate non-GQA ring + ChannelId isolation (design acknowledges a 2nd ring but not the GQA-config mismatch). (4) Chunk-decode floor (10-20ms of tiny launch-bound convs) inside the shared lockstep tick stalls ALL <=24 cohort slots every 8 strides — Design A is NOT production-safe under batching without Design C's overlap; standalone it degrades the measured 55x@64 batching win.
per_design.required_fixes: Keep an INDEPENDENT whole-body reference (the current stateless decode_audio) as the golden and gate WER(streaming vs existing-golden)<0.005 + max|delta| report — never redefine decode_audio in terms of decode_streaming. Prove SConvTranspose1d streaming right-trim/extra-pad equivalence (not just SConv1d). Allocate a distinct non-GQA ring for the Mimi decoder transformer with compile-time state isolation. Scope + document the golden re-baseline blast radius (dia2/csm/hibiki) as an explicit one-time WER-gated change. Depend on Design C overlap (or raise IC and cap cadence) before enabling under concurrency so the mid-loop decode never blows the per-tick frame budget for the cohort.

per_design.design_name: Design B — WER/MOS-gated left-context streaming for NON-causal vocoders (S3Gen / CFM)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Correctly scoped to the genuinely non-causal family (chatterbox S3Gen bidirectional Conformer+CFM+ISTFT, cosyvoice3 end-to-end-non-causal CFM) that arstep.rs proves has no byte-identical prefix; correctly keeps default byte-identical, opt-in behind an explicit flag with a refusal test, and re-stamps WER per precision (respects quant-admission). This is the sanctioned single relaxation and it is honest. FLAW (number error): the cosyvoice3 sustained-throughput projection is arithmetically wrong. cosyvoice3 RTF 0.670 => only 1/0.67 = 1.49x frame-budget headroom, but a left-context CFM redo of (L+IC) frames per committed IC frames is a (L+IC)/IC recompute multiplier = (8+4)/4 = 3.0x flow-decode cost. 3.0x > 1.49x headroom => sustained rtf_frame becomes ~0.67*3 = 2.0 > 1 => UNDERRUN. The claim '0.67 RTF absorbs up to ~IC=4/L=8' is false; the design's own 'sustained rtf_frame<1' perf gate would FAIL at L=8. The flow estimator is also ONNX-fp32 (per record config) with no CUDA-graph, so the recompute is not cheap. (2) For chatterbox the projected 'few hundred ms' TTFP is unquantified; a bidirectional U-Net over a truncated window changes the global receptive field and the recompute cost per chunk is unbounded in the design. (3) The cfg_batch.rs:177 batch-2 reassociation is acknowledged and folded into WER (acceptable since already WER-not-byte) — this one is fine.
per_design.required_fixes: Re-derive L/R from the measured per-frame budget: the admissible (L,R) is constrained by (L+IC)/IC <= 1/RTF (i.e. L+IC <= IC/RTF); for cosyvoice3 RTF 0.67 that caps L+IC <= ~1.49*IC, so L must be small (e.g. IC=4 => L<=2), not 8 — sweep within this budget, not the arbitrary {4,8,16}. Add a hard perf gate that FAILS admission (not just warns) when measured sustained rtf_frame>=1 at the chosen (IC,L,R). Quantify chatterbox recompute cost and cap the window; if no (L,R) meets both WER and rtf_frame<1, keep the honest whole-body fallback (design already provides this backstop). Cache left-context latents where the CFM permits to shrink the recompute multiplier.

per_design.design_name: Design C — Wire+schedule substrate: dynamic-IC, 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap, ship codec deltas, chunked REST
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Chunked REST (lib.rs buffers via pcm.extend_from_slice at 947/981/1020 — confirmed non-streaming), codec-delta passthrough (engine.rs:2332 confirmed drops Frame::Codec), and dynamic-IC-as-pure-latency-knob (byte-identical-output gate) are feasible, correct, and independently valuable. BUT two flaws, one sharp: (1) THE 2nd-CUDA-STREAM OVERLAP IS LIKELY INFEASIBLE IN tch. Grep of the entire backend-torch tree shows ZERO CUDA-stream control (only StreamCache/StreamingTransformer/StreamEgress — none are CUDA streams); this matches the documented tch limits (no SDPA-backend pin, cannot drive torch.compile/Dynamo). tch-rs does not expose a stable per-op stream-guard, so 'run the mid-loop decode on a second CUDA stream' cannot be written today the way SDPA-pin couldn't — the entire overlap-shadow win (and the race-test gate #2 that is its correctness proof) is on unproven ground. (2) FACTUAL ERROR: the design's premise that DutyLedger is 'built-but-unwired' and it will 'activate' it is STALE — engine.rs:1795 and 2615 already wire DutyLedger into the LIVE deadline-graded bandwidth admission (GATE #9/#10); dynamic-IC would be a NEW consumer of an already-live signal, not an activation. (3) NUMBER sloppiness: cites 'dia2 gpu_busy 0.525' and 'cosyvoice3 gpu_busy 0.278' but the on-box record is dia2 gpu_busy 0.06 (94% CPU-bound, graph-off) — the qualitative idle-shadow argument survives (more idle helps) but the cited figure is wrong and conflates occupancy with busy-fraction.
per_design.required_fixes: Ship chunked-REST + codec-passthrough + dynamic-IC (all feasible) as the substrate; DROP or gate the 2nd-CUDA-stream overlap behind a proven tch stream API (verify tch exposes a stream guard on this libtorch 2.11 build first; if not, either land the C++ shim or accept the mid-loop decode on the main stream and control its cost via dynamic-IC + cadence instead). Correct the DutyLedger claim to 'add dynamic-IC as a new consumer of the already-wired DutyLedger.' Replace the invented gpu_busy figures with the measured record.json values and re-derive the shadow-fit from those. Keep gate #3 (dynamic-IC must not change output bytes) and #4 (REST first-chunk < whole-utterance) — both are writable and correct.

dossiers.current_state:
MEASURED + code-verified. The step-bucket machinery is DORMANT: `grep` for construction of `StepBuckets::` / `SubBuckets::` / `VariableStrideLoop::new` / `compose_nested_inner_solve` across all crates EXCLUDING waav-infer-scheduler/src returns EMPTY (exit 1). The only non-scheduler references are DOC COMMENTS (irodori.rs:1180 mentions "StepBuckets" for its OWN one-shot `[B,…]` path which does NOT call the scheduler type; dynamic_fr.rs:6/37 doc-links VariableStrideLoop). So cohort.rs (StepBuckets, 1431 lines) + subbucket.rs (SubBuckets/VariableStrideLoop, 1760 lines) are byte-identical-TESTED but have ZERO live drivers. tts_coalescer.rs is NOT a step-bucket caller — it is a one-shot `synthesize_batch` cohort front-end (tts_coalescer.rs:116) that never touches the scheduler.
The flow head runs PER-SLOT at end-of-utterance: cosyvoice3.rs:690 `synthesize_pcm` → run_cfm (cosyvoice3.rs:786 run_cfm_inner) → ode.solve (cfm/ode.rs:64) → vocoder.forward (cosyvoice3.rs:693), invoked once per stream when its AR ring completes, never co-batched across concurrent streams. In the batched serve path the AR backbone rides the RaggedSlotRing (engine.rs:419 cosyvoice3 default-green) but engine.rs:407 self-labels "**P1-PARTIAL:** the [B] CFM flow + [C] HiFT vocoder back-half stays PER-SLOT (run once per utterance at decode_audio)".
MEASURED cosyvoice3 B=1 (perf/path-b/cosyvoice3/baseline_default_graph-on_trt-off_b1/record.json): RTF 0.6703, achieved_occupancy 0.5656, wall 3.337s / audio 4.978s. Flow-tail kernels dominate: "Kernel2" (the estimator DiT/conv) 862.6ms/30.2%/3326 inst/259us-avg; a launch-bound "kernel" 343.3ms/12.0%/11192 inst @30us with compute_pct 0.0103 / mem_pct 0.6014 (classify_bottleneck → launch/memory-bound); "_BinaryElementWise" 329.2ms/11.5%. Flow+vocoder tail ≈ 30.2%+12.0%+11.5% ≈ 42% of wall. N_TIMESTEPS=10 (cosyvoice3.rs:62) × CFG-2 = 20 estimator forwards/utterance; occ 0.5656 ⇒ 1/0.566 ≈ 1.77× SM-fill headroom. dots flow: 10-step DiT Euler CFG-batch-2 (dots.rs:48-51); omnivoice: 32-step masked-diffusion, whole sequence re-evaluated every step, ONE captured graph replayed for all 2·n_steps forwards (omnivoice.rs:89).
dossiers.root_cause: Two coupled causes. (1) NO decode-stage co-batch seam: the flow/vocoder decode is invoked per-slot at end-of-AR (cosyvoice3.rs:690), and there is no `decode_audio_batch`/flow-coalescer that collects concurrently-completed streams' speech_tokens and drives ONE co-batched CFM solve — so the built StepBuckets/VariableStrideLoop (which co-batch by inner Euler-step index, subbucket.rs:251) have nothing to plug into. (2) The byte-identity law forbids the naive fold: cross-request batching stacks B streams on the batch axis, and cfg_batch.rs:177 proves a batch-N GEMM reassociates the cuBLAS reduction (measured 3.9e-4 TF32 / 9.5e-7 f32 on Qwen3-H1024) — for a DISCRETE argmax head (omnivoice.rs:69 keeps cond/uncond as two batch-1 forwards) this FLIPS codes, so the machinery could not be turned on universally without a per-regime accuracy decision that was never made. The dormancy is therefore a real design-vs-wired trap AND an unresolved accuracy-gate question, not mere plumbing.

designs.name: Design A — FlowDecodeCoalescer: decode-tail micro-batch of continuous CFM/DiT flow via StepBuckets, WER/MOS-gated (CFG folds into the batch)
designs.mechanism: New live seam `TtsModel::decode_audio_batch(&mut self, rows:&[(SlotId,&[i64])]) -> Vec<Vec<f32>>` (mirror of the proven synthesize_batch/tts_coalescer.rs:116 pattern, but at the flow-decode stage). A `FlowDecodeCoalescer` (clone tts_coalescer.rs drain-loop) collects streams whose AR ring just COMPLETED within a bounded coalescing window (no artificial delay for a lone caller, tts_coalescer.rs:93) and their ready speech_tokens. Bucket rows by mel-length T using the irodori `prepare_row` pattern (irodori.rs:1217 — compute the deterministic decode length per row, bucket rows sharing T). For each T-bucket drive the CFM ODE with the DORMANT scheduler now made live: `StepBuckets::group` over the Euler StepIndex (cohort.rs:562) + `VariableStrideLoop::run` (subbucket.rs:251) — since all rows share NFE=10 (cosyvoice3.rs:62) every row is active at every step ⇒ one co-batched pass per step. At each step the per-row `x2=cat[x,x]` (ode.rs:71) becomes a `[2·B,80,T]` estimator forward: for cosyvoice3 this batches the ONNX estimator StaticGraph::run (cosyvoice3.rs:818 OnnxFlowField, Path-A ORT); for dots it batches the tch DiT (dots.rs:48 already batch-2). Then batch the HiFT vocoder as one `[B,80,T]` forward (cfm/vocoder.rs:326). CFG **folds into the batch** (2→2B) because the output is CONTINUOUS mel/velocity — the accuracy gate is WER/MOS, not byte-identity, so the cfg_batch.rs:177 refusal (which exists to protect DISCRETE argmax codes) does not apply here. Wire the coalescer between the mux loop's stream-complete and decode_audio call (codec_ar_batcher.rs:591 seam).
designs.projected_win: Basis: measured cosyvoice3 flow-tail = 42% of 3.337s wall (record.json Kernel2 30.2% + launch-bound kernel 12.0% + BinaryEW 11.5%); tail kernels are launch/memory-bound (compute_pct 0.0103, mem_pct 0.6014) so batching keeps launch COUNT fixed (20 forwards) while work/launch grows B×, amortizing the ~launch gaps and the loop-invariant weight/conditioning reads (mu/spk/cond materialized once per solve, cosyvoice3.rs:812). Occupancy headroom 1/0.566=1.77×. batch_crossover (perf_equations.py:237) for the fp32 estimator ⇒ B_crit≈166 ⇒ deeply memory-bound below that ⇒ near-linear weight-reuse amortization. Projected flow-tail throughput 1.5–1.8× at cohort B=4–8 (bounded by occ headroom + bandwidth). Aggregate cosyvoice3 model RTF: wall×(0.58+0.42/1.7)=0.83× ⇒ RTF 0.67→~0.55; per-GPU concurrent-stream capacity on the flow stage ~1.7×. This is exactly the small-batch decode-tail win vLLM-Omni's CFM batching targets.
designs.tdd_plan: RED-FIRST: (1) `flow_decode_batch_wer_within_gate` — drive N≥3 fixed clips through decode_audio_batch (B≥4 cohort) vs per-row solo, ASR-WER Δ ≤ 0.02 abs (the precision-accuracy-bar WER gate, since 2B GEMM reassociates continuous mel) — fails until decode_audio_batch exists. (2) `flow_decode_bucket_maxdelta_is_ort_ep_noise` — an EQUAL-T bucket's per-row mel maxΔ vs solo must be ≤ the known ORT-EP CUDA-vs-CPU delta (~5e-3, cosyvoice3.rs:46), NOT a code-flipping divergence — proves the fold only adds tiling noise, never a trajectory fork. (3) `flow_coalescer_fans_concurrent_into_fewer_forwards` (clone tts_coalescer.rs:201) — N concurrent completions COALESCE into <N flow forwards. (4) `flow_decode_batch_per_slot_no_cross_bleed` — ≥4 concurrent, concurrent==serial per row within the WER gate (isolation). PERF gate: cohort-B≥4 flow-tail throughput ≥1.4× solo, recorded to perf/path-b/cosyvoice3/flow_batch_bN.
designs.coverage: CONTINUOUS flow families: cosyvoice3 (ORT-CUDA estimator, Path-A), dots base/soar (tch DiT, Path-B), dots-mf meanflow (NFE=1 trivial bucket), vibevoice diffusion (DpmSolver, cfm/dpm.rs), irodori RF-DiT (already one-shot batched). Vocoder tail (HiFT cfm/vocoder.rs, BigVGAN) batches as NFE=1 StepBucket. Universal across the CfmOde/DpmSolver seam because it wires at the shared cfm:: library. Quant: fp32 estimator + bf16/f32 tch — dtype-agnostic (batch axis fold is dtype-independent). Backends: GB10 CUDA (both ORT-EP and tch). SCOPED OUT: omnivoice (discrete argmax → Design A's WER gate would mask code flips only if MOS-acceptable; default keep byte-identical two-batch-1, see risks).
designs.risks_conflicts: CONFLICT with byte-identity-by-default: 2B GEMM reassociation means this is NOT byte-identical — it MUST ride the explicit WER/MOS-gated path (precision-accuracy-bar memory), never silently. CONFLICT with cfg_batch.rs:177 is RESOLVED by regime: continuous output makes the reassociation quality-invisible (correct gate = WER/MOS), whereas discrete omnivoice keeps two batch-1 (unchanged). CONFLICT with TTFP/streaming: the coalescing window ADDS latency to TTFA (already whole-utterance today, engine.rs:2331) — this is a pure THROUGHPUT lever, and must be disabled on any future early-emit streaming path. Ragged-T fill risk: continuous audio lengths rarely coincide exactly → low natural bucket fill unless padded-with-mask (extra WER risk) or a hold-window (latency). Lockstep/ring-KV: untouched (AR ring stays per-slot byte-identical). DESIGN-VS-WIRED: this DOES wire into the live mux decode seam (codec_ar_batcher.rs:591) via a new default-green env-gated coalescer (WAAV_FLOW_BATCH), mirroring the qwen3/cosyvoice3 ring gating (engine.rs:419).

designs.name: Design B — Byte-identical exact-T co-batch with a per-shape batch-invariance oracle + B=1 fallback (no MOS relaxation)
designs.mechanism: Same StepBuckets/VariableStrideLoop driver as A, but restricted to EXACT-T buckets and gated by a runtime byte-identity oracle. irodori.rs:1196-1207 asserts (and gate-proves maxΔ=0 on the waveform) that an equal-shape `[B,…]` flow forward is byte-identical to each solo row WHEN every op reduces over feature/seq/head and never the batch axis, on the f32 path with TF32 OFF. The cfg_batch.rs:177 scar shows the residual hazard is cuBLAS TILE reassociation as B grows (3.9e-4 WITH TF32, 9.5e-7 WITHOUT). Design B therefore: (a) force TF32 off on the batched estimator GEMMs; (b) for each (model, T, B) shape, run a one-time offline oracle `batched_forward_bit_identical_to_solo` (the dia2/qwen3 force-solo-codes pattern, task #93/#105) that stacks B identical rows and asserts maxΔ==0 vs solo; (c) admit the batched fold ONLY for shapes the oracle stamped PASS (the quant-admission-gate discipline), else fall back to per-slot B=1 for that bucket. The scheduler's StepBuckets is the live driver; the oracle stamp is the admission key.
designs.projected_win: Same per-forward physics as A (1.5–1.8× flow-tail throughput at the batched shapes) BUT lower realized fill: exact-T buckets (continuous audio length) rarely coincide, and only oracle-PASS shapes batch, so expected aggregate win is a fraction of A — realistically ~1.2–1.4× flow-tail throughput at cohort B where enough rows share T (e.g. fixed-length TTS eval, chunked-T decode). Basis: same launch/memory-bound amortization (record.json), discounted by empirical bucket-coincidence rate and the oracle pass rate (the cfg_batch scar predicts many shapes will FAIL maxΔ==0 on CUDA even f32). Value is that the win is BYTE-IDENTICAL — usable on the default no-MOS-relaxation path.
designs.tdd_plan: RED-FIRST: (1) `flow_batch_equal_T_maxdelta_zero_or_reject` — an equal-T B≥2 stacked-identical-rows forward is maxΔ==0 vs solo OR the shape is REFUSED (never silently admitted) — the fail-closed core, fails until oracle+fallback exist. (2) `flow_batch_tf32_off_enforced` — assert the batched estimator runs with TF32 disabled (the 9.5e-7→still-nonzero guard). (3) `flow_batch_shape_admission_stamp` — a shape without a PASS stamp routes to B=1 (the admission gate). (4) `flow_batch_concurrent_eq_serial_byte_identical` — ≥4 concurrent oracle-PASS rows, concurrent==serial maxΔ==0. PERF gate: on the eval-length corpus (fixed T), throughput ≥1.2× with maxΔ==0 stamped.
designs.coverage: Continuous flow shapes that empirically pass batch-tiling-invariance on f32/TF32-off (per-model, per-T, per-B — measured, not assumed). Strong for fixed-length / chunked-T decode; weak for free-form ragged T. Same cfm:: seam universality as A but gated by measurement. Backends: CUDA f32 estimator (ORT + tch). Quant: f32 only (the byte-identity guarantee is dtype-fragile; bf16/fp16 shapes route to Design A's WER path). Honest scope: this is the ADDITIVE byte-identical layer that captures the subset A would otherwise relax.
designs.risks_conflicts: RISK: the cfg_batch.rs:177 evidence predicts many CUDA GEMM shapes will FAIL maxΔ==0 → low admission rate → modest realized win; must not over-promise. RISK of a silent bit-flip if the oracle is stamped once and hardware/driver changes — stamps must be tied to the calibration/driver fingerprint. CONFLICT with cfg_batch refusal: Design B RESPECTS it (it refuses any shape that reassociates) rather than relaxing — this is the invariant-faithful design. Lockstep/ring-KV/ChannelId untouched. DESIGN-VS-WIRED: wires the SAME live coalescer seam as A but with the admission stamp as the gate; risk that if no shapes pass, the machinery is live but idle — mitigate by shipping A (WER path) as the fallback so the seam always has a caller.

designs.name: Design C — SubBuckets/VariableStrideLoop as the general heterogeneous-NFE flow driver + advanced admission (make the FULL dormant stack live)
designs.mechanism: Promote subbucket.rs SubBuckets + SubBucketByNfe (subbucket.rs:495) + compose_nested_inner_solve_per_group (cohort.rs:279) to the LIVE driver that Designs A/B ride on, so mixed-NFE cohorts co-batch correctly: rows of different flow families (cosyvoice3 NFE=10, a meanflow dots-mf NFE=1, a hypothetical 32-step) group into SubBuckets keyed by NFE; VariableStrideLoop::run (subbucket.rs:251) launches exactly max_i(nfe_i) inner passes, retiring each row at its own NFE (variable-stride, masked≠absent) so the per-row call set is byte-identical to solo. t_step_nested (subbucket.rs:530) = T_ar + max_over_subbuckets(nfe×T_inner) paces the admission ledger. Additionally wire the built-but-dormant admission.rs (DutyLedger/Criticality/KvFirewall) to gate flow-cohort admission by frame-deadline (cohort.rs:101 frame_deadline_ms) so a large flow cohort cannot starve AR lockstep ticks. This is the coverage/generality layer: it does not itself add a new numerical fold (it reuses A's or B's per-step co-batch kernel) but makes the co-batch correct across HETEROGENEOUS flow families and integrates deadline-safe admission.
designs.projected_win: No new per-forward speedup beyond A/B; the win is CORRECTNESS+COVERAGE at heterogeneous cohorts and deadline safety (prevents a flow-cohort from blowing the AR frame budget). Quantified value: enables A/B to run when a replica serves MIXED flow models or mixed NFE (e.g. cosyvoice3 + dots-mf) without falling back to B=1 — recovering A's 1.5–1.8× on the mixed traffic that a single-NFE StepBuckets would drop to B=1. Basis: subbucket.rs:530 t_step_nested MAX-not-Σ pacing (already byte-identical-tested) + admission.rs deadline gate.
designs.tdd_plan: RED-FIRST: (1) `mixed_nfe_flow_cohort_call_set_equals_solo` — a cohort of NFE {1,10} rows through VariableStrideLoop::run produces exactly the solo per-(slot,step) call set (subbucket.rs:251 guarantee) driving a real flow closure — fails until the live driver exists. (2) `flow_cohort_retires_at_own_nfe_masked_not_absent` — a retired NFE=1 row takes zero further inner steps while an NFE=10 neighbor keeps stepping. (3) `flow_cohort_admission_respects_frame_deadline` — a cohort whose t_step_nested exceeds frame_deadline_ms is shed/split, not admitted (deadline safety). (4) accuracy: each row's output matches its Design-A WER gate or Design-B maxΔ==0 stamp. PERF gate: mixed-NFE cohort achieves ≥1.4× vs per-slot on the batchable subset.
designs.coverage: UNIVERSAL across flow/diffusion families and NFE regimes (10-step CFM, 1-step meanflow, 32-step masked-diffusion structurally, though omnivoice's discrete backbone still can't fold its GEMM — it can still ride the driver at B=1 with only its non-reducing per-position work batched per cfg_batch.rs PerRowHidden). Wires admission.rs (currently unwired, live gate is CodecArAdmission). All CUDA backends. This is the layer that closes the 'heterogeneous stage-DAG has zero live driver' adjacent gap too.
designs.risks_conflicts: RISK: complexity — this touches the admission path (admission.rs) which currently is NOT the live gate (CodecArAdmission is); mis-wiring could regress AR admission. Mitigate: additive, behind the same WAAV_FLOW_BATCH gate, AR admission untouched. CONFLICT with lockstep 1-stride/tick: the nested inner solve must run WITHIN an outer tick budget (subbucket.rs t_step_nested) — if the flow cohort is large it can violate the AR frame deadline; the admission gate (test 3) is mandatory, not optional. cfg_batch refusal: unchanged (omnivoice stays two-batch-1). DESIGN-VS-WIRED: this is the design MOST at risk of staying dormant — it only earns its keep once A or B is shipped as a concrete caller; recommend building C's driver ONLY after A proves the seam, else it repeats the exact G2 trap.

dossiers.recommended: Design A (FlowDecodeCoalescer, WER/MOS-gated CFG-fold) is the clear #1: it delivers the biggest concrete, roofline-grounded win (flow-tail 1.5–1.8×, cosyvoice3 RTF 0.67→~0.55), it wires into a REAL live seam (the mux decode stage, codec_ar_batcher.rs:591, mirroring the already-shipped tts_coalescer/ring gating), and it resolves the cfg_batch.rs:177 conflict CORRECTLY by regime — continuous flow output makes the batch-N reassociation quality-invisible, so WER/MOS (not byte-identity) is the right gate per the precision-accuracy-bar. Ship A first. Layer Design B on top as the ADDITIVE byte-identical subset (exact-T, oracle-stamped, TF32-off, B=1 fallback) for the no-MOS-relaxation default path — it respects the cfg_batch refusal rather than relaxing it, at the cost of lower fill. Build Design C (SubBuckets/VariableStrideLoop live driver + admission) ONLY after A proves the seam has a live caller, otherwise it re-creates the exact dormant-machinery trap this gap is about. Explicitly DEFER omnivoice's discrete backbone (keep two-batch-1 per cfg_batch/omnivoice.rs:69) — its only foldable work is the cheap non-reducing per-position ops, not worth the byte-identity risk.
dossiers.other_gaps_found: (1) The flow-batch win is a THROUGHPUT lever that mildly HURTS TTFA (adds a coalescing window) and cannot coexist with an early-emit streaming path — it collides head-on with the #1 realized-latency gap (no model emits audio early; engine.rs:2331 drops codec deltas; decode_committed_prefix arstep.rs:615 is dead code). Any flow-batch must be disabled under future streaming. (2) irodori.rs:1196 CLAIMS byte-identity (maxΔ=0) for equal-shape batched flow, while cfg_batch.rs:177 proves batch-N GEMMs reassociate (nonzero even f32) — these two invariants are in tension; the truth is shape/TF32-dependent and must be empirically stamped per Design B, not assumed. (3) admission.rs (DutyLedger/DriftDetector/Criticality/KvFirewall/LayeredAdmit) and the heterogeneous stage-DAG (dag/stage.rs) are ALSO built-but-unwired — same design-vs-wired trap as G2; Design C would close the admission half. (4) cosyvoice3's estimator is ONNX-on-ORT (Path-A) while dots' DiT is tch (Path-B) — a universal flow-batch seam must batch BOTH the OrtModel StaticGraph::run and the tch forward, i.e. the co-batch must live at the cfm:: FlowField/DiffusionStepper trait boundary, not in one backend. (5) The launch-bound "Kernel2"/BinaryElementWise tail (record.json, compute 0.0103) also implies a CUDA-graph opportunity on the batched flow estimator (cosyvoice3 is not currently in the 4 graphable models), which could compound Design A's win but is out of this gap's scope.

per_design.design_name: Design A — FlowDecodeCoalescer (WER/MOS-gated, CFG folds into the batch)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The core REGIME argument is SOUND and I could not kill it: the AR backbone commits discrete speech_tokens BEFORE the flow decode (cosyvoice3.rs:690), so the flow input is fixed and its output is continuous mel/velocity — the cfg_batch.rs:177 refusal exists solely to protect DISCRETE argmax codes, so folding CFG into a [2B] continuous estimator does NOT flip codes and WER/MOS is the correctly-scoped gate (consistent with the precision-accuracy-bar memory). BUT four real accuracy/invariant flaws: (1) LOCKSTEP/FRAME-DEADLINE VIOLATION — the co-batched solve is a long GPU-monopolizing op ([2B,80,T] × 20 estimator forwards + vocoder). While it runs, concurrently-DECODING streams' AR lockstep ticks (1-stride/tick within frame_deadline_ms, verified real in cohort.rs:101) are stalled; if the solve wall exceeds an active stream's frame budget it underruns/glitches. Design A bounds only the COLLECTION window, never the SOLVE duration vs the AR frame budget — this is a genuine invariant break with no gate. (2) RTF MISLABEL — 'RTF 0.67→~0.55' is wrong for a single stream: batching CONCURRENT streams' tails does not shorten any one stream's wall time; it is a THROUGHPUT/per-GPU-capacity lever (they admit this elsewhere, but the headline number conflates the two). (3) WIN FRACTION OVERSTATED — the 42% tail is not uniformly batchable: '_BinaryElementWise' (11.5%) and any activation-memory-bound portion scale with B (bytes ∝ B, no amortization); only the WEIGHT-bandwidth-bound Kernel2 GEMM amortizes → realistic tail speedup is materially below 1.7×, and occ headroom 1/0.566=1.77× means SMs saturate near B≈2, not B=4–8. (4) RAGGED-T CONTAMINATION — cosyvoice3's estimator is a non-causal U-Net/DiT; padding shorter rows to max-T and masking does NOT prevent conv receptive-field bleed from padded positions into real positions unless the mask is applied pre-every-conv, so padded buckets can perturb the real row beyond ORT-EP noise (a WER regression the 3-clip gate may miss). Also test (2) asserts maxΔ ≤ ~5e-3 with no reject clause, but if ORT leaves TF32 ON the [2B] reassociation compounds over 10 ODE steps and may exceed it.
per_design.required_fixes: (a) Add a frame-deadline cohort cap: bound B (and/or run flow on a lower-priority CUDA stream) so one co-batched solve ≤ the slack of the tightest co-resident decoding stream's frame_deadline_ms — this is the ONE genuinely necessary piece of Design C, extracted as a simple bound WITHOUT wiring admission.rs. (b) Relabel the headline as throughput/concurrent-capacity (~1.7× flow-stage at saturation); do not claim single-stream RTF 0.67→0.55. (c) Make MOS mandatory, not WER-only — WER is insensitive to prosody/timbre artifacts that a continuous-mel reassociation can introduce. (d) Restrict to EXACT-T buckets by default; only enable padded-mask buckets after proving the estimator applies the mask pre-conv (else it silently contaminates). (e) Explicitly disable TF32 on the estimator or characterize the compounded 10-step delta; expand the WER/MOS corpus well beyond 3 clips. (f) Scope coverage honestly to the fleet: the same P1-PARTIAL per-slot flow exists in indextts2/vibevoice/pocket_tts/voxtral_tts — each needs its own MOS stamp, not a blanket cfm:: claim.

per_design.design_name: Design B — Byte-identical exact-T co-batch with per-shape oracle + B=1 fallback
