per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The oracle MECHANISM is valid: cuBLAS/ORT kernel selection is SHAPE-keyed and value-independent, so an identical-row stamp at shape (M=B*T) that passes maxΔ==0 vs solo (M=T) genuinely certifies heterogeneous rows at that shape — the oracle correctly tests the cross-M reassociation, not a trivial duplicate. And it RESPECTS cfg_batch.rs:177 (fail-closed refusal) rather than relaxing it — invariant-faithful. The KILL-adjacent flaw is that the byte-identical promise is likely VACUOUS for the actual production estimators: cosyvoice3's ONNX estimator and dots' tch DiT fold Linear over [2B,T]→a single [2B*T,C] GEMM, and the cfg_batch scar MEASURES batch-2 f32 TF32-off at 9.5e-7 (NON-zero) — so batch-2B will almost never hit maxΔ==0 on these M-folding GEMMs. The oracle will therefore stamp ~ZERO production shapes → the machinery ships LIVE-BUT-IDLE, i.e. the EXACT G2 dormancy trap Design B claims to close. (irodori.rs:1196 does pass maxΔ==0, but that is an f32 architecture whose batch axis is preserved as a true per-batch/bmm dimension — NOT the M-folding DiT class of cosyvoice3/dots; extrapolating irodori's pass to the fleet is unwarranted.) Secondary risk: if cuBLAS uses atomic split-K at the stamped shape, maxΔ==0 is run-to-run flaky, invalidating a one-time stamp.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) MUST ship Design A (WER/MOS) as the guaranteed fallback caller so the coalescer seam is never dormant when the oracle admits nothing — otherwise B is the G2 trap. (2) Rescope the claim: expect near-zero admission on cosyvoice3/dots M-folding estimators; position B as an ADDITIVE fast-path only for irodori-class per-batch (bmm, non-M-folding) architectures, measured per-model, never assumed. (3) Assert cuBLAS determinism (no atomic split-K / CUBLAS_PEDANTIC or workspace-pinned) at the stamped shape, and tie every stamp to the driver+calibration fingerprint (already proposed) so a driver bump invalidates it. (4) Enforce TF32-off is actually honored by ORT (ORT may re-enable TF32 per-session) — test flow_batch_tf32_off_enforced must probe the ORT session flag, not just the tch global.

per_design.design_name: Design C — SubBuckets/VariableStrideLoop heterogeneous-NFE driver + admission.rs wiring
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: As a now-build it fails on both value and safety. (1) DEGENERATE for the real traffic: same-model cohorts all share NFE (every cosyvoice3 row = NFE=10, cosyvoice3.rs:62), so SubBucketByNfe collapses to plain StepBuckets — it adds nothing over Design A for the dominant case. (2) The mixed-NFE win number is WRONG: subbucket.rs:270 EXCLUDES retired slots from the active bucket (masked≠absent = the co-batch rectangle SHRINKS at each retirement). So for a mixed NFE{1,10} cohort, only the ONE overlapping inner step co-batches; the remaining 9 steps run at reduced B — the 'recovers A's 1.5–1.8× on mixed traffic' claim is unsupported (co-batch benefit ≈ min-NFE overlap, not the full solve). Worse, for Design B's byte-identical path every shrink is a NEW shape M=B'*T needing its OWN oracle stamp → almost all fall to B=1. (3) SAFETY REGRESSION RISK with no compensating accuracy benefit: it wires the currently-UNWIRED admission.rs (DutyLedger/KvFirewall/risk-EDF) adjacent to the LIVE CodecArAdmission gate; mis-wiring can regress AR lockstep admission — a correctness hazard on the hot path — to solve a mixed-NFE-concurrent-completion scenario that rarely occurs. (4) It self-admits it is 'MOST at risk of staying dormant' and should be built 'ONLY after A proves the seam' — i.e. it is itself a candidate G2 trap. The only genuinely useful element is the frame-deadline gate (test 3), which Design A actually NEEDS — but that belongs in A as a simple bounded-B cap, not as a promotion of the entire SubBuckets + admission.rs stack.
per_design.required_fixes: Do NOT build C's full stack now. Extract ONLY the frame_deadline_ms cohort-admission gate and fold it into Design A as a bounded cohort-size cap that keeps a single flow solve within co-resident AR streams' frame budgets — WITHOUT touching the live CodecArAdmission path or promoting admission.rs. Defer SubBuckets-by-NFE until heterogeneous-NFE concurrent traffic is actually observed on a replica; if/when built, resolve the masked-vs-shrink tension explicitly (either pad-and-mask retired rows to hold B constant — wasting compute but shape-stable — or accept shape-thrash and B=1 fallback for the byte-identical path) and re-baseline the win, since the current 1.5–1.8× carryover claim is invalid.

verdicts.better_alternative: Ship ONE composite, not three: Design A (WER/MOS-gated FlowDecodeCoalescer) is the correct spine because the regime argument (discrete tokens committed pre-flow → continuous mel out → cfg_batch refusal does not apply → WER/MOS is the right gate) is sound and verified against ode.rs:71 and cosyvoice3.rs:690. Harden it with the ONE necessary piece extracted from C — a frame_deadline_ms-bounded cohort cap so the co-batched solve cannot starve co-resident AR lockstep ticks (the invariant Design A silently breaks) — implemented as a plain B cap, NOT by wiring admission.rs. Keep Design B's oracle as an OPTIONAL additive byte-identical fast-path that only ever engages for irodori-class bmm/non-M-folding estimators (expect ~zero admission on cosyvoice3/dots per the cfg_batch 9.5e-7 evidence), and only atop A so the seam is never dormant. Correct A's headline to a throughput/per-GPU-capacity lever (realistic ~1.3–1.5× flow-stage, since BinaryEW and activation-bound kernels do not amortize and SMs saturate near B≈2 given occ 0.566), make MOS mandatory, default to exact-T buckets, and prove the estimator masks pre-conv before enabling any padded-T bucket. Do NOT build the SubBuckets/admission.rs stack until heterogeneous-NFE traffic is measured — building it now repeats the exact G2 dormancy trap.

per_design.design_name: Design A — FlowDecodeCoalescer (WER/MOS-gated, CFG folds into batch)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: (1) CATEGORY ERROR in the headline number. 'RTF 0.67->~0.55' is a THROUGHPUT/capacity number stated as single-stream RTF. Cross-CONCURRENT-request batching cannot reduce a lone stream's wall time — an isolated stream has no co-resident to batch with, so its flow tail runs solo and RTF stays 0.6703 (measured record.json). Under the realtime-voice regime (one call, low concurrency — the point of this engine) the win is ZERO, and the coalescing window ADDS TTFA latency. Only under high concurrent completion does the 1.7x capacity win exist. The design sells a throughput lever as a latency win. (2) WIRING SEAM IS A TEST DOUBLE. codec_ar_batcher.rs:591 (the cited seam) is inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (boundary at line 515) — CohortRecordingTts is a fake. The real production decode_audio mux call site is never identified; the design-vs-wired trap is not actually closed. (3) 'CFG folds into the batch 2->2B' is the WRONG, DANGEROUS lever and conflates two independent things. The physics win is CROSS-REQUEST row co-batching (B rows share the 20 forwards), NOT folding CFG. Folding CFG 2->2B is exactly the batch-axis GEMM reassociation cfg_batch.rs:177 warns of; dots.rs:8 already runs CFG as a batch-2 stack matching its golden, so there is nothing to 'fold'. Batching across requests while keeping CFG as-is gets the same win without the hazard. (4) FILL-STARVED: the estimator forward is `[2B,80,T]` and REQUIRES equal T (irodori.rs:1189 confirms unequal latent length changes rotary+attention length -> separate buckets). Free-form TTS mel length T=f(speech_token count) rarely coincides across concurrent utterances -> realized B approaches 1 in production; the >=1.4x perf gate is only satisfiable under a SYNTHETIC equal-T corpus. Natural bucket-fill is never measured. (5) OVER-RELAXATION: cuda_torch_irodori.rs:275 proves md==0.0 at B>=5 on CUDA for f32 continuous flow, so A's WER relaxation needlessly abandons byte-identical-by-default where it is FREE.
per_design.required_fixes: Reframe the win as pure throughput/per-GPU-concurrent-capacity (never single-stream RTF); disable on any low-concurrency/early-emit path. Cite the REAL production decode_audio mux seam, not the cfg(test) double. Drop 'CFG folds 2->2B' — batch across REQUESTS while keeping each model's existing CFG discipline. Measure natural bucket-fill on real ragged-T traffic and gate ship on it, not on synthetic equal-T. Subordinate A to B: use the WER path ONLY for oracle-FAIL shapes and bf16/fp16 continuous models; default to byte-identical (B) where the oracle passes.

per_design.design_name: Design B — Byte-identical exact-T co-batch with per-shape oracle + B=1 fallback
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Strongest of the three; its central premise is CODE-VERIFIED not assumed: cuda_torch_irodori.rs:223 asserts `md == 0.0` on the WAVEFORM at B>=5 on Device::Cuda(0) (completed task #128) — byte-identical cross-row flow batching on GB10 is REAL for f32 continuous flow, refuting the naive 'cfg_batch means nothing can pass' objection. The per-shape fail-closed oracle + B=1 fallback is invariant-faithful and RESPECTS cfg_batch.rs:177 rather than relaxing it. Non-fatal flaws: (1) COVERAGE UNPROVEN FOR THE FLAGSHIP — the oracle is demonstrated only for irodori (tch DiT). cosyvoice3's estimator is fp32 ONNX on ORT-CUDA (cosyvoice3.rs:620 OnnxFlowField), a DIFFERENT runtime whose kernel selection for `[2B,80,T]` vs `[2,80,T]` is not guaranteed shape-stable; the cfg_batch 9.5e-7 (TF32-off, Qwen3-H1024) scar shows some f32 CUDA GEMM shapes DO drift, so ORT admission may be sparse. It must MEASURE the ORT oracle pass rate before claiming cosyvoice3. (2) Same exact-T FILL limitation as A, tightened by the oracle-pass filter -> low realized B; the honest 1.2-1.4x holds only on fixed/chunked-T eval, not free-form concurrent traffic. (3) Same low-concurrency-no-win framing as A. (4) STAMP STALENESS: a PASS stamp can flip on driver/cuBLAS-heuristic change; it MUST key to the calibration/driver fingerprint (design says this — enforce as a test).
per_design.required_fixes: Before claiming cosyvoice3 coverage, run and record the ORT-CUDA fp32 estimator oracle at real T/B shapes; report pass rate honestly and route fails to A. Tie every PASS stamp to the calibration+driver fingerprint with a test that a fingerprint change invalidates stamps. Ship A as the WER fallback caller so the live seam is never idle-live. State the win as throughput-only and measure natural exact-T coincidence on production traffic.

per_design.design_name: Design C — SubBuckets/VariableStrideLoop heterogeneous-NFE driver + advanced admission
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: (1) TARGETS A WORKLOAD THAT LARGELY DOES NOT EXIST. Its value is co-batching MIXED flow families / mixed NFE (cosyvoice3 NFE=10 + dots-mf NFE=1 + a 32-step) on ONE replica. Production replicas overwhelmingly serve a SINGLE model, so mixed-NFE co-residency is rare-to-nil; realized win over A/B on real traffic is near zero. The fill problem COMPOUNDS: now you need concurrent completion AND cross-model co-residency AND deadline slack. (2) LIVE-ADMISSION REGRESSION RISK. It wires admission.rs (DutyLedger/KvFirewall/risk-EDF) which is NOT the live gate — CodecArAdmission is. Mis-wiring t_step_nested pacing into the admission path can starve/regress AR lockstep ticks (the design itself flags test 3 as mandatory). (3) MOST-DORMANT-AT-RISK, self-admitted: it only earns its keep once A or B ships a concrete caller — building the full SubBuckets/VariableStrideLoop/compose_nested stack now REPEATS the exact G2 design-vs-wired trap it claims to close. (4) No new per-forward speedup — inherits A/B physics and A/B fill ceiling, so all their throughput-vs-RTF and fill caveats apply unchanged.
per_design.required_fixes: Do NOT build until A or B shows >=1.4x on REAL (not synthetic equal-T) traffic AND a measured mixed-model/mixed-NFE co-residency workload is shown to exist on target deployments. Keep the whole path behind WAAV_FLOW_BATCH; NEVER touch the live CodecArAdmission path — add the deadline gate as an additive SHADOW check first, verified not to alter live AR admission. Scope down to homogeneous-NFE (the only regime with a real caller today); defer the heterogeneous SubBucketByNfe generality as explicitly out-of-scope until traffic justifies it.

verdicts.better_alternative: All three optimize THROUGHPUT under high concurrent, equal-T flow completion — fill-starved in realtime voice (one call) and rare in free-form TTS (ragged mel T) — and none helps the MEASURED single-stream cosyvoice3 bottleneck. Better layered plan: (TIER 0, do first, helps the B=1 realtime path where batching physically cannot) attack the measured per-frame sync + launch-bound tail directly: replace cosyvoice3.rs:331's ~6761-wide Vec<f64> host nucleus-sampling D2H every AR step with the existing on-device sample_token_on_device (nn/sampling.rs, already used by dia2) — a per-frame pipeline-flush elimination, byte-identical if the on-device top-p/top-k matches the stable-sort; and CUDA-graph/capture the tch integrator+vocoder tail (the record.json 343ms @30us x11192-inst, compute_pct 0.0103, launch/memory-bound), exactly what omnivoice.rs:89 and dots already do (the ORT estimator stays outside the capture; the tch wrapper around it is graphable). These lift the low-concurrency RTF that flow-batching structurally cannot. (TIER 1, throughput) ship Design B as the DEFAULT — byte-identical cross-request row batching is already PROVEN on GB10 (cuda_torch_irodori.rs:275, md==0.0 at B>=5 Cuda), so relax NOTHING; the per-shape oracle + B=1 fallback is the invariant-faithful lever. Do NOT fold CFG (drop A's 2->2B); keep each model's existing CFG discipline and batch only across requests. (TIER 2, fallback) Design A's WER/MOS path ONLY for oracle-FAIL shapes and bf16/fp16 continuous models — never the headline. (TIER 3, deferred) Design C's heterogeneous-NFE driver only after Tier-1 shows >=1.4x on real ragged-T traffic AND mixed-model co-residency is measured to exist. Across all tiers: report the number as per-GPU concurrent-flow-stage CAPACITY (throughput), never single-stream RTF, and gate ship on MEASURED natural bucket-fill (the equal-T coincidence rate) on production traffic — not a synthetic corpus — since fill, not kernel physics, is the true limiter."

dossiers.current_state:
VERIFIED against current code. The shared on-device primitive exists and is LIVE only in dia2: `nn/sampling.rs:53 sample_token_on_device` (softmax→topk-select→renorm→multinomial→gather, returns [1] Int64 device tensor) + `:79 broadcast_to` (device-resident CFG fan-out). dia2.rs:1837-1888/2089-2114 run the full 31-stage depformer chain with ZERO per-stage D2H/H2D and ONE bulk `Vec::<i64>::try_from(Tensor::cat(frame_codes).to_device(Cpu))` per frame (dia2.rs:1892). Its module doc + test `on_device_sample_equals_host_sample_seeded` (sampling.rs:88) prove byte-identity (multinomial advances Philox at *enqueue*, so dropping `.int64_value()` changes NO RNG). MEASURED archetype (perf/path-b/dia2/default_graph-off_trt-off_b1/record.json): RTF 2.23, occ 0.37, ~12300ms GPU-IDLE launch gaps over ~380K tiny launches (~32us/launch-gap floor).

The 12 round-trippers still call HOST-returning samplers on the production generate loops (all live via engine.rs):
- cosyvoice3.rs:328 `nucleus_sampling`: `let sv: Vec<f64> = Vec::<f64>::try_from(sorted_val...)` copies the FULL ~6761-wide sorted dist to host EVERY step + a 6761-iteration host cumsum loop, per-step, in the live `generate_bounded` (cosyvoice3.rs:253/288). Plus RAS (`ras_sampling`:309) conditionally draws a 2nd multinomial. MEASURED: RTF 0.67, occ 0.57, top kernel launch-bound (compute 0.010/mem 0.601).
- s2_pro.rs:1353/1372 `argmax(-1).int64_value()` for the semantic token + each of 9 codebooks, then re-uploads `Tensor::from_slice(&[cb_tok]).to(dev).index_select(...)` → 10 D2H + 10 H2D/frame, GREEDY (no RNG).
- csm.rs:564 `sample_token`→`.int64_value(&[0,0])` ×32/frame (cb0 + 31 depth) + re-upload csm.rs:388; occ 0.86.
- misotts.rs:370 Gumbel-max `(&probs/&q).argmax().int64_value()` ×32/frame + re-upload misotts.rs:339.
- qwen3_tts.rs:855/859/869/872 ×16/frame + re-uploads qwen3_tts.rs:1856/1882/1913; occ 0.82. cb0 needs host `cb0_history` (rep-pen) + `if cb0==CODEC_EOS_ID break` (stop).
- zonos2.rs:454 `let choice_v: Vec<i64> = ...try_from(choice...)` = MoE expert-routing host read (~23/frame) — NOT a sampler; separate class (see adjacent gaps).
NO on-device stop/history primitive exists (grep for StopFlag/DeviceHistory/deferred_stop = empty). Basis: dia2 numbers MEASURED; cosyvoice3/csm/qwen3 occ MEASURED; per-model sync counts from code; per-sync stall from dia2's ~32us/launch-gap floor + queue-drain semantics (a `.item()` blocks the CPU until the whole enqueued frame drains → serializes launch-bound frames).
dossiers.root_cause: The proven sync-free primitive covers exactly ONE sampler spelling (temperature→topk-SELECT→renorm→multinomial-over-k→gather = dia2's). The 12 laggards each use a DIFFERENT byte-exact spelling — cosyvoice3 top-p nucleus + repetition-aware resample, csm topk-MASK→softmax-over-full-vocab→multinomial, misotts Gumbel-max, qwen3 rep-pen+min-new+suppress+topk-mask, s2_pro pure argmax — none of which the single primitive reproduces bit-for-bit. There is also no on-device equivalent for the OTHER two per-frame syncs: the stop condition (`cb0==EOS`) and the sampler's host-state dependencies (rep-pen history, RAS window). So each model keeps round-tripping. The fix is a SHARED on-device logits-warp + sample + stop + history LIBRARY (mirroring HF's warper composition) where every op is device-resident and byte-identical to its current host spelling, so any model composes its exact sampler on-device and a new model gets it for free.

designs.name: D1: nn/sampling on-device warper+sampler+stop+history library (universal, byte-identical)
designs.mechanism: Extend nn/sampling.rs into a composable device-resident toolkit, each op bit-matching the CURRENT host spelling and returning device tensors: (a) `top_p_nucleus_on_device(logp, top_p, top_k)` — softmax→`sort_stable(desc)`→exclusive-cumsum→`keep = min(top_k, 1 + (cumsum_excl < top_p).sum())` (reproduces cosyvoice3.rs:334-345's `cum<TOP_P && keep<TOP_K` accumulate-then-break, min 1) → narrow(keep)→multinomial→gather, returns [1] dev tensor, KILLING the 6761-wide `Vec<f64>` D2H + host loop at cosyvoice3.rs:331; (b) `topk_mask_multinomial_on_device` (csm.rs:564/569 spelling: scores/temp→topk-mask-to-−inf→softmax-over-FULL-vocab→multinomial); (c) `gumbel_max_on_device` (misotts.rs:383: `argmax(probs / Exponential(1))` — the Exp draw stays on the same global generator, byte-identical); (d) `repetition_penalty_on_device(scores, hist_dev, penalty)` + `suppress_on_device` + `min_new_eos_mask` (qwen3_tts.rs:824-855, deterministic scatter — no conditional RNG → fully on-device with a DeviceHistory ring tensor replacing `cb0_history`); (e) `argmax_gather_on_device` for s2_pro.rs:1353/1372 greedy + carry the `-SEMANTIC_START/clamp` offset math on-device; (f) `StopFlag` = device Bool accumulator (`stop |= tok.eq(EOS)`), ONE [1] D2H/frame replaces the 16-32 per-codebook stop/int64 reads. Each model's production sampler call site (csm.rs:1003/1029/1042, misotts.rs:851/868/876, qwen3_tts.rs:1841/1873/1911, s2_pro.rs:1353/1372, cosyvoice3.rs:288) is rewritten to compose these ops + `broadcast_to`/on-device index_select for the re-upload, landing ONE bulk frame D2H like dia2.rs:1892.
designs.projected_win: s2_pro (greedy, no RNG): removes 20 round-trips/frame (10 D2H+10 H2D) → at the measured ~32us/launch-gap floor ≥640us/frame recovered, more under full-queue-drain; cleanest byte-identical win. cosyvoice3: eliminates per-step 54KB D2H + ~6761-iter host cumsum loop that sits on the CPU critical path BETWEEN AR steps on a 0.57-occ launch-bound loop → RTF projected 0.67→~0.60-0.64 (basis: remove the inter-step host-CPU gap on a launch-bound stride; roofline says a 6761-elem top-p is <<1us on-GPU). csm/qwen3 (occ 0.86/0.82, well-occupied): direct sync win modest, BUT sync-elimination is the PREREQUISITE that legalizes depth-chain CUDA-graph capture (host copy is illegal in capture) → unlocks the dia2-proven -13.6% RTF (2.23→1.93) compounding win on the 32/16-deep chains. Fleet basis anchored to dia2's MEASURED sync-free+graph result.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST, per new op: a seeded CPU test asserting device-path == the exact current host spelling bit-for-bit (clone of sampling.rs:88 `on_device_sample_equals_host_sample_seeded`) — one each for top_p_nucleus, topk_mask_multinomial, gumbel_max, repetition_penalty (assert scores tensor max|Δ|=0), argmax_gather. Then REUSE each model's existing force-solo CODES oracle (tasks #99/#105/#111 misotts/dia2/s2_pro …): assert decoded codes max|Δ|=0 vs the pre-change host-sampler golden on real weights. StopFlag test: deferred device-stop yields the SAME truncation frame/code-length as per-frame host stop. ACCURACY GATE = byte-identical (max|Δ|=0 on codes) for s2_pro/csm/misotts/qwen3/cosyvoice3-nucleus. PERF GATE = nsys re-capture asserting syncs/frame drops (csm 32→1, s2_pro 20→1) + cuda_api dispatch time down + RTF non-regression.
designs.coverage: UNIVERSAL across ALL Path-B (tch/CUDA) codec-AR TTS: dia2(done), csm, misotts, qwen3_tts, s2_pro, cosyvoice3, higgs/higgs_v2, neutts, vibevoice, dots, voxtral_tts, indextts2 — each composes its exact sampler from the shared ops so a NEW model gets it for free (the reuse thesis of nn/sampling.rs). Dtype/quant-agnostic (ops cast to f32 internally exactly as host does; bf16/fp16/q4f16 logits handled identically). Hardware: on CUDA the id stays on-GPU (the win); on CPU (Path-A/portable) the tensor is a CPU tensor → still correct, zero regression. Argmax-on-device also applies to Path-A ORT STT decoders. SCOPED OUT (honest): zonos2 MoE choice read (not a sampler — separate design).
designs.risks_conflicts: byte-identity LAW: cosyvoice3 RAS (ras_sampling.rs:309) is the ONE genuine blocker — the rep-fire (`rep>=1`) CONDITIONALLY draws a 2nd multinomial, so unconditionally computing both on-device would advance Philox differently. Byte-identical answer: keep a MINIMAL 1-element rep-fire Bool D2H/step (still kills the 54KB Vec + host loop) OR expose a WER/MOS-gated fully-speculative variant — must NOT silently relax. lockstep 1-stride/tick: UNAFFECTED (intra-stride depth-loop data path). ring-KV/ChannelId/MaskedCell: UNAFFECTED (post-logits). cfg_batch batch-2 refusal (cfg_batch.rs:177): SAFE — introduces no new batch-2 GEMM; broadcast_to feeds the same code to cond/uncond rows exactly as dia2 already does. DESIGN-VS-WIRED: LOW risk — swaps land directly in the LIVE generate loops engine.rs calls (unlike the dead step-bucket/DAG machinery); the trap to avoid is adding ops to nn/ but only calling them from a test/probe — the acceptance requires replacing the PRODUCTION call sites.

designs.name: D2: Fish graph-capture-safe deferred-stop protocol (removes the LAST per-frame sync → full-utterance graph replay)
designs.mechanism: Steal vLLM-Omni Fish's no-`.item()` protocol to kill even D1's residual 1-stop-D2H/frame. Run a CPU-precomputed worst-case MAX_FRAMES; accumulate the EOS-hit frame index as a device Int64 (`eos_idx = where(stop & eos_idx<0, t, eos_idx)`); do the crop/align (dia2.rs:1918-1937 style delay-align) with on-device narrow/gather driven by the device eos_idx; ONE D2H at utterance END lands the cropped codes. With NO per-frame host read, the entire frame step (backbone+depth+sample+embed) becomes a single CUDA-graph replay slot (extends nn/cuda_graph.rs capture_preserving_rng, RNG-buffer-refill-before-replay per the Fish stealable). Applies on top of D1 for the bounded models.
designs.projected_win: Removes the final serialization point: on csm/qwen3 (occ 0.82-0.86) the direct D1 win is small BUT this unlocks graphing the whole step like dia2's MEASURED -13.6% (2.23→1.93); compounding across the 32/16-deep chains. On cosyvoice3, removing the per-step stop+RAS sync closes the launch-bound gap toward the roofline (top kernel compute 0.010 → the stride is bandwidth/launch-bound, so a graphed sync-free stride approaches occupancy-limited throughput). Basis: dia2 is the only MEASURED graph datapoint; projection is the same mechanism applied to same-shaped chains.
designs.tdd_plan: RED: `deferred_stop_matches_host_truncation` — on real weights, the device eos_idx crop yields byte-identical code length AND codes vs the per-frame-host-stop golden (max|Δ|=0). RED: `graph_replay_bit_identical` — captured full-step replay == eager step, max|Δ|=0 on codes over N seeds (extends the dia2 608/608 gate). PERF GATE: nsys shows 0 per-frame D2H + RTF improvement ≥ dia2's -13.6% band. ACCURACY GATE: byte-identical (deterministic — no new RNG).
designs.coverage: Bounded-generation codec-AR models with a stable per-step shape: csm, qwen3_tts, misotts, cosyvoice3, dia2. Requires a real MAX_FRAMES cap (over-generation cost if EOS is early — the honest tradeoff; cap tuned per model). SCOPED OUT: models with genuinely unbounded/variable inner shape or not-yet-graphable seams (qwen3/misotts have no graph seam today → blocked on the separate graph-capture gap). Quant/hardware coverage inherits D1.
designs.risks_conflicts: byte-identity: deterministic (crop/align is arithmetic) so max|Δ|=0 holds. RISK: over-generation to MAX_FRAMES wastes compute when EOS fires early (Fish's own tradeoff) — bound it. cuda_graph.rs currently has NO shape bucketing (exact-shape B=1) and batched serve DISABLES the backbone graph (dia2.rs:1146) — so D2's full-step graph is B=1/per-slot only until the separate graph-bucketing gap lands; do NOT couple it to cross-request flow batching (cfg_batch.rs:177 batch-2 reduction refusal still applies). DESIGN-VS-WIRED: must wire into the live generate loop, not a probe; higher integration risk than D1.

designs.name: D3: Minimal scoped adoption — swap only the RNG-free inner sub-chains to the EXISTING primitive (Wave-0, lowest risk)
designs.mechanism: Without building the full library, immediately replace the sub-chains that ALREADY match `sample_token_on_device`/`broadcast_to`: qwen3 sub-talker cb1..15 (qwen3_tts.rs:1873/1911 `sample_subtalker` = temp→topk-mask→softmax→multinomial — the same family) and s2_pro codebooks 1..9 (pure argmax → `argmax_gather_on_device`). Leave cb0 (rep-pen/stop) and cosyvoice3 nucleus/RAS on host for now. Feed device tokens straight into the next embed index_select (kill the `Tensor::from_slice(&[prev]).to(dev)` re-uploads at qwen3_tts.rs:1882/1913, s2_pro.rs:1372).
designs.projected_win: qwen3: 16 syncs/frame → ~2 (cb0 sample + cb0 stop) — removes 14 D2H+14 H2D/frame. s2_pro: 20 round-trips/frame → ~2. On occ-0.82 qwen3 the per-frame serialization drop is modest in isolation but is a strict, zero-risk improvement and de-risks D1. Basis: same launch-gap arithmetic as dia2 (~32us/gap floor × ~28 removed round-trips/frame).
designs.tdd_plan: RED: reuse the existing qwen3/s2_pro force-solo CODES oracles (tasks #93/#111) — assert codes max|Δ|=0 after the sub-chain swap (the spelling is already provably equal via sampling.rs:88, so this is a wiring gate). PERF GATE: nsys syncs/frame qwen3 16→~2. ACCURACY: byte-identical.
designs.coverage: Only the sub-chains whose spelling ALREADY equals the shared primitive: qwen3 sub-talker, s2_pro codebooks 1..9, and any other model's inner topk-select depth loop. Does NOT cover cosyvoice3 nucleus/RAS, csm topk-MASK-full-vocab (different spelling), misotts Gumbel-max, or the cb0/stop/rep-pen host deps — those NEED D1. Explicitly a partial stepping-stone.
designs.risks_conflicts: byte-identity: SAFE (identical spelling, proven). No lockstep/ring-KV/ChannelId/cfg_batch interaction. DESIGN-VS-WIRED: lands in live loops. RISK: leaves cosyvoice3 (the #1 named hotspot) and csm/misotts largely untouched → does NOT close the gap alone; must be sequenced INTO D1, not shipped as the answer.

dossiers.recommended: D1 is the foundation and the correct universal answer — it is the SHARED, reusable on-device warp+sample+stop+history library the gap asks for, byte-identical per model, so every current and future codec-AR model gets sync-free sampling for free. Sequence: land D3 first as a zero-risk wiring proof of the sub-chains that already match, build out D1's per-spelling ops (top_p_nucleus for the #1 cosyvoice3 hotspot, topk-mask-full-vocab for csm, gumbel_max for misotts, rep-pen+DeviceHistory+StopFlag for qwen3, argmax_gather for s2_pro), then layer D2 (Fish deferred-stop) ONLY on the bounded+graphable models to convert the freed syncs into full-step CUDA-graph replay (the dia2-proven -13.6% compounding win). The one honest caveat carried through: cosyvoice3 RAS's conditional 2nd-draw keeps a minimal 1-bit rep-fire sync under strict byte-identity, or moves fully on-device only behind an explicit WER/MOS gate.
dossiers.other_gaps_found: (1) zonos2.rs:454 `choice_v: Vec<i64>` is NOT a sampling sync — it is data-dependent MoE expert routing driving a Python-style per-token loop with `index_copy` (zonos2.rs:445-458). The sampling library does NOT cover it; it needs a distinct on-device grouped-expert dispatch (one-hot batched GEMM or masked expert matmul) — a separate sub-gap the gap statement conflates into the '23 host reads/frame'. (2) csm/qwen3 already have HIGH occupancy (0.86/0.82) — the direct sync-elimination win on them is modest; their real value is UNLOCKING depth-chain CUDA-graph capture, but qwen3/misotts have NO graph seam today (only dia2/csm/omnivoice/dots are graphable per nn/cuda_graph.rs) → the compounding win is partially blocked by the separate graph-capture/bucketing gap, and batched serve still DISABLES the backbone graph (dia2.rs:1146). (3) The streaming-TTFP dead code (arstep.rs:615 decode_committed_prefix, engine.rs:2331 dropped deltas) is an adjacent but distinct realized-latency gap — sync-elimination lowers per-frame wall but does NOT emit audio early. (4) s2_pro carries `SEMANTIC_START`/clamp offset math and the `sem_token==IM_END` stop on host (s2_pro.rs:1353-1358) — both can move on-device with StopFlag, else they re-introduce a per-frame sync that would negate the codebook-loop win.

verdicts.lens: accuracy/correctness/invariants — byte-identity of each device-resident sampler to its CURRENT host spelling (same Philox consumption), no AR-trajectory fork, no cfg_batch batch-2 GEMM introduced, lockstep/ring-KV/ChannelId untouched, and — critically — whether the proposed accuracy GATE actually exercises the RNG path it claims to protect.

per_design.design_name: D1: nn/sampling on-device warper+sampler+stop+history library (universal, byte-identical)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Core is sound and honest — each proposed op mirrors a REAL current host spelling I verified (csm.rs:564 MASK→softmax-full→multinomial(1,false); misotts.rs:370 Gumbel-max argmax(probs/Exp(1)); qwen3_tts.rs:824-863 rep-pen→min-new→suppress→temp→topk-mask→softmax→multinomial; s2_pro argmax; cosyvoice3 nucleus). None of these ops exist yet (grep for argmax_gather_on_device/topk_mask_multinomial/gumbel_max_on_device/top_p_nucleus/StopFlag/DeviceHistory = EMPTY), so this is genuine build, not wiring. No invariant broken: no batch-2 CFG GEMM (cfg_batch refusal SAFE), post-logits so ring-KV/ChannelId/lockstep untouched. THREE flaws. (1) Nucleus keep-formula mis-specified: cosyvoice3.rs:328 uses a check-BEFORE-add host loop `while cum<TOP_P && keep<TOP_K { cum+=p; keep+=1 }` = `min(TOP_K, count(exclusive_cumsum<TOP_P))`, but D1 writes `min(top_k, 1 + (cumsum_excl<top_p).sum())` — the `1 +` is off-by-one vs the actual host predicate. (2) Graph-compounding overclaim: D1 says sync-removal 'unlocks the dia2-proven -13.6% RTF' on csm AND qwen3, but only 4 models are graphable (dia2/csm/omnivoice/dots); qwen3/misotts have NO graph seam, so sync-removal is necessary-not-sufficient — they get only the direct occ-0.82 sync win. (3) cosyvoice3 RTF 0.67→~0.60-0.64 is shaky: D1 honestly keeps a residual 1-element rep-fire Bool D2H/step for RAS's conditional 2nd multinomial, but the doc's own physics says each per-frame D2H is a pipeline FLUSH not bytes — a 1-element .item() flushes the launch-bound queue every step just like the 54KB one, so the per-step flush persists; only the host cumsum LOOP work is removed.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Port cosyvoice3's exact host predicate (drop the `1 +`). 2) Per op, PIN the multinomial replacement flag to the host site (dia2/csm replacement=false; cosyvoice nucleus/random replacement=true — different Philox consumption; mismatch silently forks the trajectory). 3) Scope the -13.6% graph-compounding claim to graphable models (dia2/csm) only; label qwen3/misotts/s2_pro/cosyvoice3 direct-sync-win-only. 4) State cosyvoice3 honestly: under byte-identity RAS is stuck at 1-flush/step (flush removal needs D2's deferred-stop, forbidden by RAS conditional RNG). 5) MANDATE a seeded STOCHASTIC byte-identity oracle per op (clone of sampling.rs:88), NOT only the greedy force-solo CODES oracle — the fleet codes-gates run GREEDY (qwen3_tts.rs:37-38) and cannot exercise the multinomial path.

per_design.design_name: D2: Fish graph-capture-safe deferred-stop protocol (full-utterance graph replay)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The deterministic-crop core (device eos_idx accumulator + on-device narrow/gather, ONE D2H at end) IS byte-identical for DETERMINISTIC-control-flow samplers, and graph_replay_bit_identical is writable. But D2 has a byte-identity CONTRADICTION in coverage: it lists cosyvoice3 while promising 'NO per-frame host read.' cosyvoice3's stop is `if tid>=SOS break` where tid=ras_sampling, which CONDITIONALLY draws a 2nd multinomial off a host repetition-window (cosyvoice3.rs:309-323). Computing both branches unconditionally on-device to avoid the read advances Philox differently → forks trajectory → NOT byte-identical; this contradicts D1's own RAS finding. Second flaw: D2 claims to graph 'the whole step (backbone+depth+sample+embed)', but the backbone attends a GROWING per-slot ring-KV — dia2 keeps the backbone EAGER and graphs only the 31 fixed-shape depformer stages; cuda_graph.rs has NO shape bucketing (exact-shape B=1) and batched serve DISABLES the backbone graph (dia2.rs:1146). D2's full-step graph depends on a static-worst-case-grid ring backbone that does NOT exist (a separate gap). Third (perf-adjacent): over-generating to MAX_FRAMES (cosy mx=20·tts_len) when TTS typically stops at ~2-4·tts_len is +400-900% compute that dwarfs the -13.6% graph win — likely NET NEGATIVE for early-EOS utterances.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) REMOVE cosyvoice3 and every conditional-RNG sampler from D2 coverage — deferred zero-sync stop is byte-identical ONLY for deterministic-control-flow samplers (s2_pro greedy; qwen3/csm/misotts where stop is the sole host dep and composition is fixed). 2) Gate D2 behind the static-grid graphable-backbone gap; keep B=1/per-slot, never couple to cross-request flow batching (cfg_batch.rs:177 refuses batch-2). 3) Bound MAX_FRAMES per model and report expected-vs-worst frame ratio; MOS/perf-gate the over-generation tradeoff. 4) Keep D2 strictly on-top-of-D1.

per_design.design_name: D3: Minimal scoped adoption — swap RNG-free sub-chains to the EXISTING primitive (Wave-0)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The s2_pro cb1..9 half is a genuine zero-risk byte-identical win: s2_pro.rs:1353/1372 is pure `argmax(-1).int64_value()` — argmax is deterministic and already device-resident, so keeping it on-device is trivially bit-exact (greedy #111 oracle suffices). BUT the qwen3 sub-talker half rests on a FALSE premise. D3 claims sample_subtalker (qwen3_tts.rs:863) 'ALREADY match[es] sample_token_on_device ... provably equal via sampling.rs:88.' It does NOT: I verified sample_subtalker = `temp → top_k_mask(→−inf) → softmax over FULL vocab → multinomial(1,false)` (csm-family MASK spelling), while the existing primitive is `softmax → topk-SELECT k → renorm → multinomial OVER k → gather`. Same support distribution but multinomial over length-k vs length-V masked vector → different Philox consumption → different id → forks the AR trajectory. sampling.rs:88 only proves equality to dia2's SELECT-renorm spelling. Worse, D3's cited gate (#93/#111) runs GREEDY (qwen3_tts.rs:37-38 'the deterministic LAW is the greedy codes, argmax, RNG-free') — in greedy mode sample_subtalker degenerates to argmax and the wrong-primitive routing PASSES the gate, hiding the stochastic divergence. The test D3 proposes CANNOT detect the bug D3 introduces.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Restrict D3 to GENUINE argmax/greedy sub-chains only (s2_pro cb1..9; qwen3/misotts/csm in greedy LAW mode) via a plain device argmax — NOT via sample_token_on_device, and stop citing sampling.rs:88 (wrong equivalence). 2) For the STOCHASTIC qwen3 sub-talker, use D1 op (b) topk_mask_multinomial_on_device — not the existing primitive. 3) Add a seeded STOCHASTIC byte-identity oracle before any stochastic swap; the greedy CODES oracle is insufficient. Net: D3's stochastic scope collapses INTO D1 — ship only the argmax/greedy subset as an independent Wave-0.

verdicts.better_alternative: The three are not equally weak: D1 is the correct spine, D3 collapses into D1 for anything stochastic (its 'reuse the existing primitive' premise is byte-identity-false for the MASK-family and Gumbel samplers), and D2's headline (full-step graph) depends on an unbuilt static-grid ring backbone and its over-generation likely nets negative. Sequence: (Wave-0) ship ONLY the deterministic-argmax swaps as D3's safe subset — s2_pro cb1..9 and greedy-mode sub-chains — via a plain device argmax gated by the existing greedy codes oracles; true zero-risk, de-risks D1. (Wave-1) build D1 as the universal library, but add two hard gates the current plans lack: (a) a SEEDED STOCHASTIC byte-identity test per op (clone of sampling.rs:88), because every fleet codes-gate is greedy/RNG-free and structurally blind to a wrong multinomial; (b) pin each op's multinomial replacement flag and full predicate to the exact host site (fix the nucleus off-by-one). Scope every graph-compounding claim to the 4 graphable models only. Keep cosyvoice3 RAS at its honest 1-bool-flush/step under byte-identity, and route any fully-speculative RAS variant onto an explicit WER/MOS-gated path, never silent. (Wave-2, deferred) D2 only after the static-grid graphable-backbone gap lands, permanently excluding conditional-RNG samplers (cosyvoice3 RAS) and bounding MAX_FRAMES with a measured expected-vs-worst frame ratio so over-generation cannot silently exceed the graph win.

per_design.design_name: D1: nn/sampling on-device warper+sampler+stop+history library (universal, byte-identical)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Core is sound and I verified every spelling: csm.rs:565 IS topk-MASK->softmax-full-vocab->multinomial (distinct from dia2's select-k, so op (b) is genuinely needed); misotts.rs:369 IS Gumbel-max argmax(probs/Exp(1)) with the Exp draw already device-resident (op (c) is a clean drop-the-read win); qwen3_tts.rs:828 sample_talker_cb0 IS rep-pen->min-new->suppress->temp->topk-mask->softmax->multinomial over an OWNED f32 copy (comment at :2810 warns the in-place scatter must NOT alias the caller's logits); s2_pro.rs:1354/1370 IS pure argmax greedy with re-uploads at :1372. cfg_batch.rs:177 refuses only a batch-axis-in-GEMM reduction, and broadcast_to fans out a SAMPLED INDEX (no GEMM) exactly as dia2 does, so D1 is safe there. HOWEVER three claims are wrong/overstated: (1) FALSE 'ONE bulk frame D2H like dia2' for cosyvoice3 - nucleus_sampling (cosyvoice3.rs:337) has a DATA-DEPENDENT keep width; D1's own mechanism (a) says narrow(keep), and narrow needs keep on the host = a scalar D2H per step. The only escape (mask-to-full-vocab + multinomial over the padded dist) is byte-identical ONLY IF torch multinomial's Philox-offset advance is independent of category count (k vs 6761) - that is UNPROVEN and is exactly a byte-identity-LAW question, not an assumption. (2) qwen3/misotts graph-compounding overclaim: D1 leans on 'unlocks the dia2-proven -13.6% RTF' for the occ-0.82/0.86 models, but per the roofline notes qwen3/misotts HAVE NO GRAPH SEAM today - that -13.6% is contingent on a SEPARATE graph-capture gap D1 does not own, so those two models get only the (admittedly modest) direct sync win. csm is fine here because csm.rs:1040 single_step already has a per-stage CUDA-graph fast-path, so de-serializing its 32 drains genuinely pipelines like dia2. (3) RAS (ras_sampling, cosyvoice3.rs:309) conditionally draws a 2nd multinomial keyed on a host history-window count, so it retains >=1 scalar rep-fire D2H/step (D1 acknowledges this). Net: cosyvoice3 - the #1 MEASURED hotspot - keeps ~2 scalar syncs/step, not zero. Not a kill: the actual measured cost (54KB Vec<f64> D2H + 6761-iter host cumsum on the inter-step CPU critical path) IS eliminated, so RTF direction holds; the 0.60-0.64 figure is an unmeasured projection guarded by the PERF gate. TDD is real (clone of the live sampling.rs:88 seeded equality test + the already-shipped force-solo CODES oracles tasks #93/#99/#111 asserting max|delta|=0 on real weights), and swaps land in the LIVE engine.rs generate loops, not a probe.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Add an explicit RED test 'multinomial_philox_advance_is_category_count_invariant' that DECIDES the cosyvoice3 nucleus path: if it fails, the design must retain a 1-element keep-D2H (still kills the hotspot) rather than silently masking. 2) Publish honest per-model RESIDUAL-sync accounting (cosyvoice3 ~2 scalar/step; csm/s2_pro/qwen3 ~1 stop D2H + 1 bulk frame D2H) - drop the blanket 'ONE bulk D2H'. 3) Re-scope the qwen3/misotts projected win to direct sync-elimination only; move the graph-compounding claim under the graph-capture gap. 4) Add a duplicate-index scatter test for the DeviceHistory rep-pen (torch scatter_ duplicate-index ordering) against sample_talker_cb0's owned-copy semantics. 5) Keep any fully-speculative RAS variant strictly WER/MOS-gated and opt-in.

per_design.design_name: D2: Fish graph-capture-safe deferred-stop protocol (full-utterance graph replay)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The projected win rides on a MISATTRIBUTED number. dia2 already achieves its -13.6% (2.23->1.93) with PER-STAGE depformer graphs + eager backbone + sync-free depth - NOT with whole-step single-graph replay. D2 cites that same -13.6% as evidence that its NEW whole-step-graph mechanism will pay off; there is zero measured basis that a whole-step single graph beats the current per-stage-graph state on ANY model. Coverage is silently tiny: cuda_graph.rs is explicitly EDGE-ONLY, fixed-B, exact-shape single-slot (verified in the module header) and batched serve DISABLES the backbone graph (dia2.rs:1146), so D2 can only run at B=1/per-slot on the already-graphable set {dia2,csm} - and both ALREADY graph per-stage. cosyvoice3 is not in the graphable-4; qwen3/misotts have no graph seam. So on the only two models D2 can touch, it removes D1's LAST 1 stop-D2H/frame - roughly 1/32 of D1's own sync benefit on a loop dominated by ~380K tiny launches - in exchange for a large integration lift (deferred-stop protocol + full-step capture + RNG-buffer-refill) plus MAX_FRAMES over-generation cost. That is marginal-on-marginal work with an unquantified upside and high design-vs-wired (dead-machinery) risk. TDD (deferred_stop_matches_host_truncation, graph_replay_bit_identical) is writable and deterministic, but a green identity test on a near-zero-delta feature does not justify the build.
per_design.required_fixes: Demote from a design to a MEASUREMENT SPIKE gated on evidence: first prove on dia2 (already graphable) that a whole-step single-graph beats the committed per-stage-graph 1.93 by a real, repeated margin using profiling/perf_equations.py; only if that delta materializes, build it, scoped explicitly to {dia2,csm} at B=1/per-slot and decoupled from the batched-serve backbone-graph-disable (dia2.rs:1146) and the cfg_batch.rs:177 batch-2 refusal. Absent that measured delta, do not build - it is dormant machinery.

per_design.design_name: D3: Minimal scoped adoption - swap only RNG-free inner sub-chains to the EXISTING primitive
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The safety premise is partly FALSE. D3 claims qwen3 sub-talker cb1..15 'ALREADY match sample_token_on_device' and calls the swap a mere 'wiring gate ... provably equal via sampling.rs:88'. But I verified sample_subtalker (qwen3_tts.rs:864) is temp->topk-MASK(set to -inf)->softmax over FULL vocab->multinomial over FULL vocab, whereas the existing primitive sample_token_on_device (sampling.rs:53) is softmax->topk-SELECT[1,k]->RENORM->multinomial over K->gather. Same normalized distribution on the kept set, but DIFFERENT multinomial cardinality (k vs V) - so byte-identity again hinges on the unproven category-count-invariance of the multinomial Philox advance. sampling.rs:88 proves the SELECT-k spelling equals a SELECT-k reference; it does NOT prove the MASK-full subtalker spelling equals it. So D3 mislabels a genuine ACCURACY risk as a wiring gate. Second, argmax_gather_on_device (needed for s2_pro cb1..9) does NOT exist in sampling.rs yet (only sample_token_on_device + broadcast_to are present) - so D3's 'without building the full library, use the EXISTING primitive' is incorrect: it must write op (e) and effectively op (b) first. The s2_pro half is genuinely safe (argmax is exact/deterministic, no RNG, trivially byte-identical), lands in the live s2_pro.rs:1354/1370 loop, and reuses the shipped force-solo oracle (#111). D3 is honest that it is partial and leaves the cosyvoice3/csm/misotts hotspots for D1.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Correct the premise: qwen3 sub-talker needs the MASK-full-vocab op (D1's (b)), NOT the existing select-k primitive - gate it on the category-count-invariance test (same as D1 fix 1) before asserting byte-identity. 2) Acknowledge argmax_gather_on_device must be written (D1's (e)); ship it for s2_pro cb1..9 (the truly zero-risk, no-RNG win) as the real Wave-0. 3) Reframe D3 as 'land D1 ops (e) and (b) for the greedy/RNG-free sub-chains first', explicitly sequenced INTO D1 - do not present it as a no-new-code swap or ship it as the answer (it leaves cosyvoice3, the #1 measured hotspot, untouched).

verdicts.better_alternative: Sequence, don't pick one. (A) Wave-0 = the genuinely zero-risk slice of D3: write argmax_gather_on_device (D1 op e) and wire s2_pro cb1..9 + the greedy semantic argmax on-device (deterministic, no RNG, byte-identical by construction), reusing oracle #111. (B) FIRST-CLASS gate that unblocks everything: a single RED test proving whether torch multinomial's Philox-offset advance is invariant to input cardinality (k vs full-vocab-masked). Its outcome decides, for ALL of cosyvoice3-nucleus, csm-mask-full, and qwen3-subtalker, whether the sync can go fully on-device or must retain a 1-element scalar D2H - this is the true root question and must be settled empirically, never assumed. (C) Then D1's full library, but LED BY cosyvoice3 (RTF 0.67, occ 0.57 - the ONLY laggard with a measured sub-1.0 launch-bound hotspot and the 54KB Vec + 6761-iter host cumsum on the inter-step CPU path), because that is where the measured win lives; publish honest per-model residual-sync counts and a PERF gate (RTF non-regression + nsys syncs/frame drop) rather than the speculative 0.60-0.64. (D) Drop D2 as a design; convert it to a measurement spike gated on a proven whole-step-vs-per-stage-graph delta on dia2. Throughout, treat byte-identity of every new op as decided by the existing force-solo CODES oracles (max|delta|=0 on real weights), and keep any speculative RAS/nucleus relaxation strictly WER/MOS-gated and opt-in - never silently relaxed.

dossiers.current_state:
VERIFIED against code, not summary. THREE facts establish the gap:

(1) The heterogeneous stage-DAG is NOT on the live serve path — it is CLI/test-only. `CascadeDag::spawn` (crates/waav-infer-dag/src/cascade.rs:179) has exactly two callers: `run_dag_once` (crates/waav-infer-server/src/bin/waav_infer.rs:480-542, the `run-dag` CLI) and the `cascade_live.rs:154` integration test. The LIVE WS path (crates/waav-infer-server/src/ws.rs:377/568/627/679) admits via `s.try_admit()` → codec_ar_batcher.rs:234 → CodecArAdmission — a SINGLE-model codec-AR loop. No heterogeneous DAG, no GPU-resident handoff, ever runs for a real request.

(2) The DAG does NOT do independent per-stage BATCHING. `CascadeDag::spawn` (cascade.rs:207-222) creates ONE OS thread per stage (`thread::spawn`), each a `StageWorker` (worker.rs) that pulls ONE item, applies its step, pushes ONE item. `BatchWidth`/`batch_size` (stage.rs:56,87) is used ONLY as the inter-stage edge channel CAPACITY (cascade.rs:200-203) — never as a co-step batch. `run_cascade` (server/cascade.rs:96-190) feeds ONE item and recvs ONE. So `StageNode::ar_llm(8)`'s "lockstep B≥4" is dead metadata: the AR spine runs B=1. The lockstep `Driver::tick` (runtime/driver.rs:229) and the RaggedSlotRing/forward_ring fleet (qwen3 etc.) are wired to the codec_ar_batcher, NOT to the DAG's AR stage.

(3) Advanced admission has ZERO live callers. `Scheduler::admit_layered` (scheduler/admission.rs:2532), `shed_victim` (1851), `KvFirewall::admit` (1982), `DriftDetector`/`Criticality`/`TierArbiter` appear only inside admission.rs + its tests (grep confirmed). The live gate is the flat CodecArAdmission (concurrency count + fixed DEFAULT_BYTES_PER_STREAM=256MB @ codec_ar_admission.rs:52 + 28GiB free-mem floor @:75 + priority band + tenant fairness). The ONE wired roofline gate, `engine.admit_bandwidth()` (server/lib.rs:350, DutyLedger), is a no-op on GB10: it needs a DCGM bandwidth profile, but GB10 "exposes NO dram counters" so the profile stays None → engine.rs:2682 confirms "no measured profile ⇒ admit_bandwidth is a no-op Ok". So on the target box the sophisticated duty ledger is inert.

MEMORY: no multi-stage co-located accounting exists. CodecArAdmission is single-model (one VramAccountant, one flat per-stream footprint); run_cascade takes no admission gate at all. For a 3-model co-located cascade (STT+LLM+TTS) nothing sums the three stages' weights+KV+transients against one budget. The GB10 unified-pool OOM scar (170GB mapped, crashed the box twice per MEMORY) is defended ONLY for the single-model codec-AR path.

QUANTIFIED WIN BASIS (calibration profiling/gb10_calibration.json: 130.6GB unified, 198.5 GB/s, 86.04 TFLOP/s bf16, ridge 433.5 FLOP/byte): vLLM-Omni #2318 = 22GB for a 0.6B model = 2 engines × 0.90 mem-fraction (per-process CUDA context ~0.3-0.6GB + per-process arena over-reservation, duplicated per stage). WaaV in-process = ONE CUDA context + ONE arena: 3-stage cascade weights ≈ STT(~0.5-1.5GB)+LLM(0.6B bf16=1.2GB)+TTS(~0.5-1.5GB) ≈ 3GB resident + shared arena. The naive process-per-stage port on GB10's SHARED pool is not just wasteful, it is FATAL: 3 stages × 0.90×130.6GB = 3×117GB requested against one 130.6GB pool = the exact unbounded-arena crash pattern. In-process with one capped arena is the only correct design. Latency win: AR→vocoder codec-token handoff (~25Hz × ~8 codebooks × 2B ≈ 400 B/frame) is bandwidth-trivial, but process-per-stage forces D2H + IPC-serialize + H2D + a cross-process pipeline sync per chunk (a per-frame pipeline flush, same class as the dia2 D2H stall = ~hundreds of µs); in-process it is a device-tensor pointer handoff (0-copy).
dossiers.root_cause: The DAG machinery (StageNode/Paradigm/CascadeDag/StageWorker), the lockstep Driver, the RaggedSlotRing per-model batchers, and the advanced admission (admit_layered/DutyLedger/KvFirewall/DriftDetector/shed_victim/TierArbiter) were each built and byte-identical/unit-tested in ISOLATION, but three integration seams were never wired: (a) no live DAG driver — the WS handler branches only to the single-model codec_ar_batcher, so CascadeDag is a CLI demo; (b) the DAG's AR stage is a per-item StageWorker, never bound to the lockstep Driver+ring, so per-stage batching is metadata not behavior; (c) the live admission gate is the flat CodecArAdmission, and the roofline duty gate (admit_bandwidth) is inert on GB10 for lack of a DCGM profile — so admit_layered/KvFirewall/shed_victim have no caller. There is no process-wide multi-stage VramAccountant, so co-located stages cannot be admitted against one budget (the OOM scar). This is the classic design-vs-wired trap at three layers.

designs.name: D1: Live in-process DagSession with GPU-resident handoff + process-wide multi-stage VramAccountant (the beats-vLLM-process-per-stage core)
designs.mechanism: Add a live `DagSession` serve path parallel to codec_ar_batcher: when the loaded config declares a cascade (Paradigm chain, e.g. Feedforward-STT -> Ar-LLM -> CodecStream-TTS or Talker->vocoder), ws.rs (crates/waav-infer-server/src/ws.rs:377) branches to it instead of the single-model path. Reuse CascadeDag::spawn (dag/cascade.rs:179) UNCHANGED for topology/park-wake/backpressure, but (i) change the inter-stage payload from host `Vec<f32>`/`String` (server/cascade.rs:130-159 copies to host) to a device-resident handle (a tch `Tensor` on CUDA for Path-B / a Latent CodecTokens tensor) so the AR->vocoder edge is a 0-copy pointer handoff, never D2H+H2D; keep a host-Vec handoff for Path-A/CPU (still one process, no OOM). (ii) Introduce ONE process-wide VramAccountant (runtime/watchdog.rs:811, the reserve/commit RAII ledger) shared by the DAG path AND the codec_ar_batcher, and generalize CodecArAdmission's flat DEFAULT_BYTES_PER_STREAM (codec_ar_admission.rs:52) to a cascade-SUMMED footprint = Σ(per-stage weights already committed once) + Σ(per-stage per-slot KV) so the whole cascade admits as ONE reservation; a second cascade over the summed budget sheds typed AdmissionRejected. (iii) Wire the L2 DagSlotReset (dag/reset.rs) into the DagSession's slot-recycle so a recycled slot bumps ChannelId first then fans reset_slot to every stage (the cross-user-contamination guard, currently unwired to any live DAG).
designs.projected_win: Memory: eliminates the per-stage CUDA-context (~0.3-0.6GB each) + per-stage arena-fraction duplication. vs vLLM 22GB (2×0.90 fractions) a 3-stage 0.6B-class cascade lands ONE context ~3GB weights + one capped arena. On GB10's shared 130.6GB pool this is the ONLY non-crashing design (naive 3×0.90×130.6=351GB request → the 170GB-scar crash). Latency: removes one D2H+IPC+H2D+cross-proc-sync per inter-stage chunk (per-frame pipeline flush, ~hundreds of µs class per dia2 D2H) → replaced by 0-copy device handoff. Basis: calibration 198.5 GB/s makes the ~400B/frame token payload bandwidth-free; the win is pure launch/sync-stall elimination + arena de-duplication.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `dag_runs_on_live_ws_serve_path` — a WS session with a cascade config returns real PCM AND a spy proves codec_ar_batcher's single-model path was NOT taken (fails today: ws.rs has no cascade branch). (2) `interstage_handoff_is_device_resident_zero_d2h` — instrument the AR->vocoder edge; assert 0 host copies of the token tensor (fails today: cascade.rs:130-159 copies to host). (3) `colocated_cascade_admits_summed_footprint_or_sheds` — VramAccountant just under Σ(stage weights+KV); admitting one cascade reserves the SUM, a second sheds typed AdmissionRejected (fails today: run_cascade takes no gate). (4) `recycled_dag_slot_is_reset_across_every_stage` — reused slot shows no prev-occupant state on any stage (fails: reset.rs unwired). ACCURACY GATE (byte-identical, deterministic): live DagSession egress PCM == run_cascade CLI egress over the same input+seed, maxΔ=0 (staging is control-plane, numerics untouched). PERF GATE: end-to-end RTF<1 (existing G11 accept) AND peak-resident-bytes(in-process) < 1/2 peak-resident-bytes(3× naive process-per-stage baseline), measured via /proc/meminfo + torch memory_allocated.
designs.coverage: UNIVERSAL over the DAG driver (not per-model): all heterogeneous cascades (STT->LLM->TTS, Talker->vocoder), all paradigms (Feedforward/Ar/CodecStream/Flow/Diffusion, and Remote which stays off-box). Path-B(tch,CUDA) gets device-resident handoff; Path-A(ORT)/CPU falls back to in-process host-Vec handoff (still one process, no per-stage OOM). Quant-agnostic (control-plane; the summed footprint just reads each stage's actual bytes). Hardware-agnostic: the VramAccountant is a byte ledger; on a discrete-VRAM box it uses total VRAM×safety instead of the unified pool.
designs.risks_conflicts: Byte-identity: PRESERVED (control-plane staging; each stage's kernels unchanged) — gated by test 3-ACCURACY. Lockstep 1-stride/tick: D1 alone keeps each stage micro-batch (AR spine still B=1) — it does NOT yet realize per-stage batching (that is D2); honest scope. Ring-KV/ChannelId/MaskedCell: reset.rs already bumps ChannelId-first (reset.rs:25) — must fan to every stage's reset_slot. cfg_batch batch-2 refusal: not touched (no cross-request GEMM batching in D1). DESIGN-VS-WIRED: this is THE fix for half the gap — it moves CascadeDag from CLI-only onto the live WS path; without it the DAG stays a demo. RISK: co-locating DAG threads with the codec_ar_batcher can contend the tch caching allocator/CUDA stream — the VramAccountant MUST be process-wide (one ledger), not per-path, or the two paths double-count and OOM.

designs.name: D2: Independent per-stage lockstep batching — bind the DAG's Ar stage to Driver::tick + the RaggedSlotRing (the throughput multiplier)
designs.mechanism: Replace the Ar-paradigm stage's per-item StageWorker with a batching adapter: instead of `step(one_item)`, the AR stage accumulates up to `StageNode::batch_size()` (stage.rs:126, currently dead metadata) items arriving on its input edge within a bounded coalescing window (reuse the tts_coalescer fan-in pattern, server/tts_coalescer.rs), then drives ONE `Driver::tick` (runtime/driver.rs:229) over an `ActiveSet` of B slots advancing all B in lockstep, and scatters B outputs to the output edge. The AR model is a `forward_ring` ArStepModel over the RaggedSlotRing (per-slot B=1 dispatch, GQA-native ring-KV) — reuse the fleet template already built for qwen3/dia2/csm (tasks #92/#104/#108). Feedforward-STT and CodecStream-TTS stages stay per-item StageWorkers (RFC#2568 micro-batch of 1). Flow/Diffusion stages route to the step-bucket batcher (scheduler/cohort.rs StepBuckets, currently only wired via tts_coalescer for one-shot arms — adjacent).
designs.projected_win: AR decode is memory-bound (AI ~1-2 FLOP/byte << ridge 433.5 → weight-load bandwidth dominated), so batching amortizes the per-step weight bytes (0.6B×2=1.2GB) across B streams: near-linear until the KV-read term crosses over. MEASURED basis: qwen3 ring 2.61×@B12 default-on (waav-pathb-batch-rollout memory), lockstep 55×@64 upper bound (device-KV matrix). Projection: DAG AR spine at B=8 → ~2-2.6× stage throughput vs the current B=1 StageWorker, pulling end-to-end cascade RTF below the D1 (B=1) baseline. vLLM-Omni cannot match this in-process because its stages are separate processes with separate batchers and cross-process handoff.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `ar_stage_lockstep_batches_B_streams_in_one_tick` — feed B=8 concurrent items to the AR stage edge; a spy on the model asserts ONE tick advanced 8 slots (not 8 sequential single-item steps) (fails today: StageWorker steps one item). (2) `flow_stage_uses_step_bucket_not_per_slot` — a Flow stage coalesces same-NFE solves into one [B,..] forward (fails today: per-slot). ACCURACY GATE (codes-identical-to-solo, maxΔ=0): reuse the force-solo CODES oracle pattern (e.g. qwen3_tch_force_solo_codes_identical_ragged) — each of the B streams' output tokens == that stream run solo, and two identical concurrent requests draw the identical RNG stream (D2 content-keyed rng_base). PERF GATE: AR-stage throughput at B=8 ≥ 2× B=1 on GB10; end-to-end cascade RTF strictly < the D1 B=1 RTF.
designs.coverage: Scoped-but-fleet-universal for the Ar family: reuses the per-model forward_ring already shipped across the fleet (qwen3/dia2/csm/misotts/s2_pro/higgs/higgs_v2/neutts/dots/voxtral_tts/vibevoice/cosyvoice3/indextts2 per the task log), so any AR spine plugs in. Feedforward/CodecStream correctly stay B=1 (RFC#2568). Flow/Diffusion covered via the StepBuckets step-bucket path (needs its own wiring = adjacent gap). Path-B(tch,CUDA) only for the ring; Path-A/CPU keeps the B=1 StageWorker (no regression). Quant-agnostic (ring is byte-identical in any dtype because the batch index never enters a reduction).
designs.risks_conflicts: cfg_batch batch-2 reduction refusal (cfg_batch.rs:177): RECONCILED — the ring uses per-slot B=1 forward_ring dispatch so the batch axis never reassociates a cuBLAS reduction (the exact property that made the fleet codes-identical); and the AR LLM spine has no CFG. Lockstep 1-stride/tick: RESPECTED (Driver::tick is the frame-sync primitive). Ring-KV: this IS the per-slot ring, GQA-native. MaskedCell/ChannelId: masked≠absent handled by ActiveSet (driver.rs:58). RISK: the coalescing window adds a small batching latency to the AR stage — bound it to ≤ one frame so TTFP is not hurt. DESIGN-VS-WIRED: this converts StageNode.batch_size from dead metadata into real behavior — but it DEPENDS on D1 (there must be a live DagSession first).

designs.name: D3: Wire admit_layered + multi-stage StageDuty + KvFirewall + DriftDetector/shed_victim as the live DAG admission gate (the roofline gate that knows co-located duty)
designs.mechanism: At DAG admission, build a Vec<StageDuty> — one per stage — from calibrated compute_secs/bytes_touched via StageDuty::from_calibrated (scheduler/admission.rs:516), sourcing the numbers from the on-box profiler (nn/profiler.rs measured CUDA-event data — NOT the absent DCGM counters that make admit_bandwidth inert on GB10). Call Scheduler::admit_layered(ledger,arbiter,tier,&stages,nested,masked,thermal,c) (admission.rs:2532): it AND-reduces every co-located stage's per-substrate compute duty PLUS the shared-bus bandwidth duty PLUS the masked-slot term against the tier-effective, thermally-derated bound, naming the argmax Saturated resource on reject — the true roofline gate for a co-located cascade. On Admit, DutyLedger::add all stages; RAII removes on session end. Add KvFirewall::admit(context) (admission.rs:1982) to cap per-stage KV-length against a KvLengthBudget (closes the flat-256MB gap: a long-context stream can't blow the ring). Under sustained overload, DriftDetector::observe(step_time) (admission.rs:1633) trips is_shedding, and shed_victim (admission.rs:1851) evicts the Criticality-Lo, newest, least-progress stream (deadline-graded degradation vLLM lacks). Layer this on top of CodecArAdmission (keep it for concurrency-count + the 28GiB free-mem floor); admit_layered becomes the compute/bandwidth authority.
designs.projected_win: Admits to the MEASURED roofline (198.5 GB/s bus, 86.04 TFLOP/s bf16) instead of a hardcoded concurrency count: a co-located 3-stage cascade whose Σ bandwidth_duty>1.0 at N streams is refused at N+1 rather than admitted-and-glitched. Prevents p99 blowup — DriftDetector sheds BEFORE saturation, and under a 400-stream spike the box admits exactly to Σduty≤1.0. KvFirewall bounds KV growth, closing the 'ledger shows headroom while unified pool near-empty' gap for the co-located case (the 170GB scar's true cause). Basis: DutyLedger::admit is a pure roofline projection over calibrated scalars; the win is correctness+bounded-p99, not raw throughput.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `dag_admission_uses_layered_duty_not_flat_count` — 3 StageDuty for a cascade whose Σ bandwidth_duty exceeds 1.0 at N concurrent; the (N+1)-th is refused by admit_layered naming SharedBandwidth as Saturated (fails today: no live admit_layered caller). (2) `kv_firewall_refuses_overlong_context` — projected_kv_bytes(context)>budget → typed refuse (fails: KvFirewall unwired). (3) `drift_sheds_lowest_criticality_newest_victim_under_sustained_breach` — step-times past p99 sustain → shed_victim evicts Criticality-Lo newest, Hi retained (fails: unwired). (4) `admit_bandwidth_uses_profiler_not_dcgm_on_gb10` — with no DCGM but a live profiler StageDuty, the duty gate is ACTIVE (fails today: engine.rs:2682 no-op). ACCURACY GATE: admitted streams byte-identical (admission is control-plane); an evicted stream gets a typed error, never a corrupt/partial output. PERF GATE: under a 400-stream spike admit exactly to Σduty≤1.0 and p99 step-time ≤ budget (DriftDetector never trips in steady state), vs CodecArAdmission which admits a flat count and lets p99 blow.
designs.coverage: UNIVERSAL: StageDuty/DutyLedger/KvFirewall/DriftDetector/shed_victim/TierArbiter are backend/model/quant/hardware-agnostic pure scalars (compute_secs, bytes_touched, KV bytes, step_time). Applies to every stage on every substrate (per-substrate SubstrateId keys the ledger), every paradigm (Remote stages excluded from local duty via Paradigm::is_local, cascade.rs:96). Needs a per-model calibration; absent → conservative roofline fallback (never fail-closed).
designs.risks_conflicts: RISK: admit_layered needs MEASURED StageDuty; if the profiler is cold it MUST fall back to the conservative roofline (design/L4), not refuse everything. Must NOT double-gate with CodecArAdmission — assign authorities cleanly (CodecArAdmission=concurrency+VRAM-count+free-mem floor; admit_layered=compute+bandwidth duty; KvFirewall=KV length) so a stream isn't rejected twice with conflicting reasons. Byte-identity/lockstep/ring-KV: untouched (control-plane). cfg_batch refusal: N/A (admission doesn't batch). DESIGN-VS-WIRED: this is the whole point — admit_layered/shed_victim/KvFirewall currently have zero callers; the risk is it stays test-only. It also revives the inert admit_bandwidth by feeding it profiler data instead of the missing DCGM counters.

dossiers.recommended: Sequence D1 → D3 → D2 (D1+D3 is the MVP that closes the gap; D2 is the throughput extension). D1 is the foundational must-do and the single best design: without a live DagSession the entire gap is moot (CascadeDag stays a CLI demo), and D1 alone delivers the headline 'beats vLLM process-per-stage' claim — one CUDA context + one process-wide VramAccountant summing co-located stages is the ONLY non-crashing design on GB10's shared 130.6GB pool, plus 0-copy GPU-resident handoff. D3 folds directly into D1's admission seam (build Vec<StageDuty> at DagSession admit, call admit_layered) and is what makes the co-located memory/bandwidth accounting correct and p99-bounded — critically it also revives the otherwise-inert admit_bandwidth by sourcing StageDuty from the on-box profiler instead of GB10's absent DCGM counters. D2 (per-stage lockstep batching via the existing forward_ring fleet) is the throughput multiplier that makes it SOTA (~2-2.6× on the AR spine, measured basis qwen3 2.61×@B12) but strictly depends on D1 existing first. All three are byte-identical/codes-identical gated, so accuracy is never traded.
dossiers.other_gaps_found: (1) StageNode.batch_size is DEAD metadata: used only as edge channel capacity (cascade.rs:200-203), never as a co-step batch — mislabeled as the throughput lever it is not (D2 fixes). (2) The ONE wired roofline gate, engine.admit_bandwidth() (lib.rs:350), is INERT on GB10: it needs a DCGM bandwidth profile but GB10 exposes no dram counters, so it is a no-op Ok (engine.rs:2682) — the sophisticated DutyLedger never bites on the target box (D3 revives via profiler). (3) The L2 DagSlotReset (dag/reset.rs, the DAG-wide cross-user-contamination guard, FEAT-55) has NO live DAG driver calling it — a privacy gap the moment the DAG goes live with slot recycling (the runtime reset_slot callers in dynamic_fr.rs/harness.rs are the per-model L1 wipe, a different verb). (4) The step-bucket flow batcher (scheduler/cohort.rs StepBuckets / subbucket.rs VariableStrideLoop) is byte-identical-tested but only wired via tts_coalescer for one-shot arms; the 12 streaming hybrid models keep the flow head PER-SLOT (engine.rs:407 self-labeled 'P1-PARTIAL') — a Flow/Diffusion DAG stage would inherit this gap. (5) The DAG emits WHOLE-utterance (run_cascade recvs one item) — it intersects the TTFP/streaming-egress gap: early per-stage emit is not wired, so a live cascade would have TTFA==whole-utterance latency until the streaming seam (decode_committed_prefix, arstep.rs:615, currently dead code) is also wired. (6) Co-locating DAG stage threads with the codec_ar_batcher risks tch caching-allocator/CUDA-stream contention unless the VramAccountant is made strictly process-wide (one ledger for both paths) — currently each path would allocate independently.

per_design.design_name: D1: Live in-process DagSession with GPU-resident handoff + process-wide multi-stage VramAccountant
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: On the pure numerics axis D1 is control-plane and its byte-identity claim mostly holds (integer codec tokens and String text edges survive a host<->device round-trip bit-exact; wiring reset.rs IMPROVES state-safety since DagSlotReset is confirmed unwired to any live path). But two real correctness hazards break the accuracy claim as stated. (1) STREAM-ORDERING RACE = byte-identity violation. cascade.rs:207-222 runs each stage on its OWN OS thread (thread::spawn). A '0-copy device-resident pointer handoff' of a tch CUDA Tensor across those threads ignores CUDA stream ordering: the consumer stage can dereference the tensor before the producer's kernel has completed (read-before-write) unless an explicit cross-stream CUDA event synchronizes the edge. That is non-deterministic corruption -> the maxDelta=0 gate (test 3-ACCURACY) is not just unmet, it is FLAKY, and the flakiness only appears under concurrent overlap, which the single-item run_cascade oracle never exercises. (2) MECHANISM INCONSISTENCY: 'reuse CascadeDag::spawn UNCHANGED' for a device CodecTokens/Latent tensor is impossible — spawn's signature hardcodes String for both middle edges (StageStep<A,String>+StageStep<String,String>+StageStep<String,A2>). The device-tensor handoff, which is the ONLY claimed accuracy-neutral latency win, cannot ride the cited seam. Byte-identity is preserved in principle but not deliverable via the named code path.
per_design.required_fixes: (a) Record a CUDA event on the producer stream and wait on it on the consumer stream for EVERY device-resident edge (or keep device tensors on ONE stream); the design must state this or drop 'pointer handoff' to a stream-synchronized handoff. (b) Generalize spawn's payload beyond String (generic PayloadKind or a dedicated 2-stage codec/Talker->vocoder spawn) — cite the real edge, do not claim UNCHANGED. (c) Run the byte-identity DagSession==CLI gate under >=4 concurrent overlapping streams, not the single-item run_cascade, so the race is actually caught. (d) The process-wide VramAccountant must be the single ledger for BOTH paths (already noted) — verify it, since double-counting is an OOM/ correctness risk not a numeric one.

per_design.design_name: D2: Independent per-stage lockstep batching — bind the DAG Ar stage to Driver::tick + RaggedSlotRing
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The AR-family core is genuinely correct on this axis: per-slot B=1 forward_ring dispatch keeps the batch index OUT of every cuBLAS reduction, which is the exact property that made the fleet codes-identical-to-solo (verified: cfg_batch.rs two_pass refuses BatchAxisReducedInGemm as a hard typed error; the ring sidesteps it entirely, and the AR LLM spine has no CFG). Content-keyed rng_base for identical concurrent requests is a real, correct invariant. The accuracy hole is the FLOW/DIFFUSION coverage claim: D2 asserts 'Flow/Diffusion covered via StepBuckets step-bucket path' and routes same-NFE solves into ONE [B,..] forward — but that is NOT reconciled with the cfg_batch batch-2 reduction refusal. If a flow/diffusion head runs CFG (cond+uncond) or any matmul where stacking streams on the batch axis reassociates the cuBLAS reduction, cross-request batching flips emitted codes at maxDelta ~3.9e-4 — the exact documented trap. StepBuckets is byte-identical-TESTED only for one-shot arms (per the wiring-gap note); it has never been stamped byte-identical for a streaming CFG flow head. So D2's Flow coverage ships an unproven byte-identity claim. Also honestly depends on D1.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Restrict D2's live batching claim to the AR ring family (qwen3/dia2/csm/... forward_ring), which is proven. (2) Keep Flow/Diffusion PER-SLOT (as engine.rs:407 already labels P1-PARTIAL) until step-bucket flow batching passes a force-solo CODES oracle EXTENDED to the CFG case; specifically prove the [B] flow forward does not reassociate the CFG reduction, or dispatch each in-batch flow row as its own forward (per-slot-in-batch). (3) Add test: a 2-stream Flow-stage batch must be codes-identical to each stream solo AND must reconcile with cfg_batch (assert no BatchStackedGemm on the CFG axis). (4) Bound the AR coalescing window to <= one frame so TTFP is not regressed (already noted).

per_design.design_name: D3: Wire admit_layered + StageDuty + KvFirewall + DriftDetector/shed_victim as the live DAG admission gate
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The machinery is sound and control-plane (numerics untouched), but the HEADLINE accuracy claim — 'admits to the MEASURED roofline (198.5 GB/s) ... admit exactly to Sigma duty<=1.0, no glitch' — is FALSE on the target box because of a wrong hardcoded number. engine.rs:1291 defines GB10_PEAK_DRAM_BYTES_PER_S = 273e9 (the LPDDR5X datasheet 273 GB/s), but the calibration triad is 198.5 GB/s. The duty ledger's Ceilings peak-DRAM is built from that constant, so Sigma duty<=1.0 admits ~37.5% MORE bandwidth than physically exists -> over-admit past real saturation -> the exact p99 blowup D3 exists to prevent, and it violates the owner's rule 'MEASURED not datasheet, never hardcode elsewhere'. Second correctness flaw (interaction with D2): DriftDetector::observe(step_time) trips on RAW tick time, but D2's lockstep batching makes step-time grow with B legitimately, so a raw-tick DriftDetector false-positive-sheds valid streams and can evict a live Criticality stream — it fights batching. Third: shed_victim evicting a SERVING slot must emit a DISTINCT typed terminal; today only barge-in has a Cancelled terminal wired, so an evicted mid-synthesis slot risks presenting truncated PCM as a complete utterance (silent correctness bug). The accuracy-gate assertion 'evicted stream gets a typed error, never a corrupt/partial output' is unbacked by any live eviction terminal.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Source the DRAM ceiling from profiling/gb10_calibration.json (198.5 GB/s), NOT the 273e9 constant; delete/deprecate GB10_PEAK_DRAM_BYTES_PER_S or set it to the measured value and add a test that the admit ceiling == calibration bandwidth. (2) Make DriftDetector batch-aware: observe per-active-slot-normalized step time, not raw tick time, so lockstep batch growth is not misread as drift; add a test that a B=8 lockstep tick does NOT trip is_shedding. (3) Wire shed_victim to the existing Cancelled/AdmissionRejected distinct terminal so an evicted serving slot NEVER emits truncated-as-complete PCM; test the terminal frame. (4) bytes_touched for StageDuty must be an explicit analytic (weights+KV+transients) or the L2-proxy, documented — do not imply real DRAM counters exist (GB10 has none). (5) Assign gate authorities cleanly (CodecArAdmission=concurrency+free-mem floor; admit_layered=compute+bandwidth; KvFirewall=KV length) so no stream is double-rejected with conflicting Saturated reasons.

verdicts.better_alternative: No wholesale replacement needed — the three designs are the right decomposition (D1 live path + accountant, D2 batching, D3 duty gate). But sequence and gate them: (i) D1 first, with the CUDA-event stream-ordering fix and a generic (non-String) edge payload, gated by a >=4-concurrent byte-identity oracle (the single-item run_cascade oracle cannot catch the cross-thread device race). (ii) D3's ONE-LINE prerequisite (source the 198.5 GB/s ceiling from gb10_calibration.json, killing the 273e9 datasheet constant) should land BEFORE D3's machinery, since every duty projection is wrong until then. (iii) D2 and D3 have a hidden coupling the plan misses: batch-induced step-time growth (D2) vs raw-tick DriftDetector shedding (D3) — they must be co-designed with per-slot-normalized drift, or D3 will evict the streams D2 is legitimately batching. Restrict D2's live byte-identity claim to the AR ring family and keep Flow/Diffusion per-slot until step-bucket flow batching is separately cfg_batch-reconciled with a CODES oracle.

dossiers.current_state: MACHINERY EXISTS, GATE IS UNWIRED (the central G6 finding). (1) Graph-driven dtype seam is REAL but scoped: `empty_kv_dtype_for`/`feed_float` (crates/waav-infer-runtime/src/precision.rs:45-90) read `StaticGraph::input_types()` per-input-name so a q4f16 export's F16 KV / F32 features are graph-driven — but only TWO arms call it: voxtral.rs and tts/chatterbox.rs (grep confirmed). `input_types()` default is EMPTY (backend-api/src/lib.rs:539) and only `OrtModel` populates it (ort/src/lib.rs:378,731); parakeet.rs and the other enc-dec/AR arms still build empty state hardcoded-f32, so a zero-code `_q4f16` manifest swap crashes them exactly like the original voxtral bug. (2) The quant-admission gate is DESIGN-NOT-WIRED: `admit_quant_variant` (model.rs:357), `resolve_precision` (backend-api:987), `QuantStamp` (model.rs:253) are fully unit-tested but have ZERO live callers (all call sites are `#[test]`, model.rs:1567-1661 / backend-api:3929-4005). The LIVE load path `load_model(dir, loader)` (model.rs:642) takes NO EpCaps/ActiveEp/stamps; it picks a weight file purely by string suffix via `weight_path`→`graph_precision_token` (model.rs:211-220) with NO stamp interposed. `QuantStamp` is never deserialized (Manifest::from_json at model.rs:60/117 reads no stamp field). So the ONLY live precision guard is the ORT-load-time int8-on-CUDA typed *reject* (ep.rs:184 BackendError::Precision) — a hard error, NOT the designed degrade-to-fp32. (3) Path-B native precision: `PrecisionMode::resolve` (backend-torch/nn/precision.rs:68) is per-model wired via `WAAV_<M>_PRECISION`→`WAAV_PRECISION`→manifest, default = byte-identical Sandwich for dia2/s2_pro, Native for csm/qwen3/misotts/higgs; but nothing auto-flips it from a WER stamp. MEASURED basis: dia2 native-bf16 WER 0.0129 vs f32-sandwich 0.0337 (equivalent) at 1.25× backbone GEMM; voxtral q4f16 KV byte-identical int8==plain-onnxruntime. ROOFLINE (perf_equations.py decode_step_bytes:190 + ar_decode_ai:218, calib 198.5 GB/s / ridge 433.5): B=1 decode weight-read floor = N·dtype_bytes/BW. fp16→q4f16 cuts weight bytes ~3.9× (2.0→~0.516 byte/param incl group-128 fp16 scales); e.g. a 2B backbone: fp16 4.0GB→20.2ms/step floor, q4f16 ~1.03GB→5.2ms floor (−15ms). AI rises 1.0→4.0 FLOP/byte, still ≪433.5 ⇒ still deeply memory-bound ⇒ the byte cut converts ~linearly to time IN the memory-bound regime. HONEST CAVEAT: measured Path-B AR is LAUNCH-bound (dia2 gpu_busy 0.06, ~380K tiny launches, perf/path-b/dia2), so quant cuts bytes not launches — the weight-byte win is masked on the launch-bound tail; the clean wins are (a) Path-A ORT dense/one-shot graphs and (b) 4× residency headroom on GB10's 130GB unified pool (admission/batch capacity).
dossiers.root_cause: Two independent roots.
