So the max reachable win on today's voxtral is the score-materialization fraction of ~5%, and the design concedes ~0% at 12s clips. Material only at N>=1500 long-context, which is not the current serving profile. THIRD: the fused arm must gate on has_mask==false; a B>1 encoder carries a padding mask (correctly Math today) and the arm as written could drop a required mask. MINOR IMPRECISION: the brief says pin 'under the generator mutex like the RNG-offset fns (shim:170)' — the RNG fns hold gen.mutex() (the generator's own mutex, shim:175); at::globalContext().setSDPUseFlash/setSDPUseCuDNN are global Context flags needing no generator mutex (a global guard is still prudent under concurrent streams). ACCURACY COMPLIANCE IS OTHERWISE SOUND: fused-bf16 != manual-f32-softmax is a genuine byte-identity scar (attention.rs:11-21, sdpa_manual softmaxes in f32 then casts), so a WER gate (not byte-identity) is the CORRECT gate; flag-guarded (WAAV_VOXTRAL_PERF_ATTN, never silent); decode stays byte-identical (solo_token_ids max|Δ|=0); cfg_batch N/A (STT B=1, no CFG); lockstep/ring-KV/ChannelId untouched; the setSDPUse* setters exist in libtorch 2.11 so the csrc pin is buildable.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Split the prefill arm by tower: encoder/cross-attn -> sdpa(mask=None, is_causal=FALSE, enable_gqa); decoder-prefill -> sdpa(mask=None, is_causal=TRUE). (2) Gate the fused arm on sig.has_mask==false so a required padding/window mask is never dropped for speed. (3) Probe+fallback the cuDNN/flash pin on sm_121 aarch64 (FlashInfer-forbidden-style guard) — return to FusedAuto if the pinned backend is unavailable/slower. (4) Label honestly: the win is ~0% at <=30s clips, material only at N>=1500; ship it as a long-context lever, not a current-workload perf claim. (5) Keep the WER RED gate WER(fused)<=WER(manual)+eps on the golden set AND add an encoder-only bidirectional-correctness gate (fused-encoder transcript WER must not collapse) to catch the is_causal bug.

per_design.design_name: Design B — KV-length bucketed graph cache (LRU) + port live Fish into the paged long-form escape
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: P-8 ARCHITECTURE BREAK (verified): the paged-port half proposes giving runtime/paged_kv.rs PagedKvTable a 'device-resident twin + residency_graph() via on-device index_select'. But PagedKvTable lives in the BACKEND-FREE runtime crate (P-8) and is a pure HOST structure — append(channel_id, row: Vec<f32>), row()->Option<Vec<f32>>, full_kv_row()->Vec<f32>; no tch, no device, no tensor. Bolting device tensors + a captured index_select onto it pulls tch/CUDA into the runtime crate, BREAKING the Path-A/Path-B split AND the design's own coverage claim ('paged bookkeeping is backend-free P-8 so Path-A can reuse the page-table'). The device twin must be a NEW backend-torch type; PagedKvTable stays host residency policy. MISLOCATION (verified): 'bucketing is a runtime/cuda_graph.rs policy, no model edit' is wrong — runtime/cuda_graph.rs CudaGraphTier holds a SINGLE captured: Option<EdgeCaptureKey>, no device handle, does no capture (pure P-8 policy). The per-bucket graph OBJECTS + the KV-read narrowing live in backend nn/cuda_graph.rs (currently exact-shape single-slot) + kv_cache.rs (append_full_masked_graph reads the full max_seq buffer). So the LRU multi-graph cache is a BACKEND build and each model's graph-decode wiring must pick a bucket + narrow its read — a model/backend edit, not a policy swap. The design conflates the two same-named cuda_graph.rs files. OVERREACH: 'universal to every graph-decode model' is false — the masked-ring path (voxtral) reads a fixed max_seq buffer so bucketing narrows the read (real win), but the CONTIGUOUS path (csm append_contiguous_graph) already narrows to EXACT length pos+1 and relies on fixed-length-per-stage capture; bucketing there is a different regime that can re-introduce the per-step shape-change recapture thrash the exact-length capture avoids (dots already thrashes on total change). ACCURACY IS SOUND where scoped: byte-identity of ring bucketing is code-grounded — the masked region [cur_len..bucket] fills finfo.min and softmax underflows to EXACTLY 0.0 (kv_cache.rs:191; voxtral.rs:decode_step_graph comment 'masked-slot softmax weight underflows to 0'), and adding 0.0 summands does not change a float reduction, so narrowing max_seq->bucket is byte-identical; the RED test (bucket vs full-max_seq max|Δ|=0 token ids) is writable and correct; ChannelId reset/re-stamp preserved; no cfg_batch conflict.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Split into two designs. B1 = KV-length bucketing in the BACKEND (nn/cuda_graph.rs multi-capture LRU + kv_cache.rs bucket-narrowed masked read + per-model bucket selection) — accuracy-safe, byte-identical, wireable NOW; scope it to the masked-RING path (voxtral) only. B2 = a NEW device-resident paged KV type in backend-torch (NOT bolted onto the P-8 host PagedKvTable); keep PagedKvTable as host residency policy so Path-A reuse survives. (2) For the contiguous csm path, do NOT bucket without a separate recapture-thrash gate (prove at-most-one capture per bucket, no per-step recapture). (3) Keep the design-vs-wired acceptance criterion (a live long-form transcribe() caller) but resolve the P-8 break first. (4) Add the RED gates as written: bucketed_graph_byte_identical_across_buckets (max|Δ|=0), paged_graph_matches_ring_graph on the DEVICE path, lru_evict_no_recapture_thrash.

per_design.design_name: Design C — Split-K flash-decode for long-context memory-bound attention (deferred)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: As a shippable accuracy-preserving design it does not survive; the self-deferral is the correct engineering call. (1) BYTE-IDENTITY BROKEN: split-K reassociates the softmax reduction (online log-sum-exp combine) — same class as cfg_batch.rs:177 CfgBatchRefusal::BatchAxisReducedInGemm (batch-2 GEMM reassociation flips codes at maxD 3.9e-4 TF32) — so it is WER/MOS-gated only, never default. (2) WIN < 1% ON EVERY CURRENT MODEL by physics: attention is 1.5% of dia2 / ~5% of voxtral; at B=1 q=1 decode AI ~1-2 << ridge 433.5 FLOP/byte, so the kernel is MEMORY-bound — raising occupancy 0.37->0.8 cannot move a memory-bound kernel past the 198.5 GB/s ceiling; net wall < 1%. (3) LIVENESS HAZARD: routing the decode-attention op through an ORT CUDA sub-graph inside a tch decode introduces a SECOND execution substrate = the documented ORT+tch concurrency-deadlock scar (gdb-proven in the v2 build) — a real correctness/liveness risk for a <1% win. (4) The perf RED gate is UNFULFILLABLE today: no shipped WaaV model has attention >15% of wall, so the trigger condition cannot be measured and no meaningful perf test can be written — which itself confirms the deferral. cfg_batch/lockstep/ring untouched only because it is (correctly) NOT wired.
per_design.required_fixes: Do NOT build. Record the deferral with an explicit measured trigger (a long-form S2S model showing attention >15% of wall via nn/profiler.rs). If ever triggered: implement as a hand C++/CUDA split-K in csrc (NOT an ORT sub-graph, to avoid the ORT+tch deadlock), gate strictly on WER/MOS vs manual decode on the golden set, flag-guarded, never default; add splitk_matches_fused_f32 (<1e-5 in f32, proving the algorithm not bf16 rounding) and an ncu occupancy>=0.7 proxy (lts__t_bytes.sum, since GB10 has no dram__* counters).

verdicts.better_alternative: All three target attention, which the measured GB10 truth shows is 1.5-5% of every current model — the wrong target. The highest-value accuracy-preserving, wireable work lives where the wall actually is: (1) Ship Design B1 in isolation — KV-length bucketing of the EXISTING masked-ring graph in the backend (nn/cuda_graph.rs multi-capture + kv_cache.rs bucket-narrowed read). It is byte-identical (masked region underflows to exactly 0.0, proven in kv_cache.rs:191 + voxtral decode_step_graph), closes the O(max_seq)-per-step read, and needs no new execution substrate. (2) In parallel, eliminate the 12 per-frame GPU->CPU D2H sync round-trips (cosyvoice3.rs:331 full 6761-wide prob Vec/step; s2_pro ~10 scalars/step; zonos2 ~23; csm+misotts 32/frame; qwen3_tts 16/frame) by routing them through the on-device primitives that already exist (sample_token_on_device / on-device index_select). This is byte-identical (identical math, just no host hop) and attacks the launch/sync-bound 76% decode that actually dominates the voxtral/dia2 wall (dia2 = 12.3s GPU-idle launch gaps measured). Together these hit the real bottleneck at zero accuracy cost. Attention pinning (Design A, once its is_causal encoder bug is fixed) and split-K (Design C) are near-zero-ROI at current sequence lengths and should be labeled long-context-only levers, not shipped as current-workload perf wins.

per_design.design_name: Design A — Real SDP-priority FFI shim + WER/MOS-gated fused-flash PREFILL for the manual family
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The projected win (15-40% at long-context STT, 'the only design touching the vLLM 215->11ms regime') is physically unreachable on every current WaaV model, and the roofline is built on a false model of voxtral. (1) The voxtral ENCODER is NOT a growing long-context prefill: it is FIXED at ~375 tokens post-downsample (voxtral.rs:106 DOWNSAMPLE=4; 30s->1500 mel->375) for any clip, because longer audio is chunked to 30s. Design A's 'grows quadratically from N~150 to ~30% at N~375 and dominant at N>=1500' is impossible — encoder N is capped at 375 and MEASURED at 385.9ms=5%. (2) The encoder attention is a SLIDING-WINDOW-750 causal mask (enc_config window:Some(750)), so score HBM is bounded by N*750 = LINEAR in N, not the N^2 dense score matrix the 'N/16 -> 24x at N=375' roofline assumes. (3) The roofline mixes shapes: it uses 'decoder shape heads32/kvh8/d128' but the encoder is MHA heads32/head_dim64 (voxtral.rs:102-103). (4) The DECODE is LAUNCH-bound (76% of wall, top kernel elementwise gpu_busy 0.23), and STT decode output is short — a fused score kernel cannot move a launch-bound, short-output decode. Net realized win on current models is <1%, not 15-40%. Correctness edge: routing encoder/decoder prefill through nn::sdpa(is_causal=true) does PLAIN causal, but both voxtral masks are SLIDING-WINDOW (enc 750, dec 8192) — identical only while seq < window; a longer chunk silently attends outside the window (wrong math, not just bf16 rounding). The pin FFI itself is legitimate, but on current models every fused-capable model already runs FusedAuto (internal flash/mem-efficient pick) at short seqs, so the cuDNN pin ROI is ~0 (brief confirms), and cuDNN SDPA availability on sm_121 aarch64 is unverified.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Correct the headline: projected realized win on all shipping models is <1% (encoder fixed 375, windowed=linear, measured 5%; decode launch-bound) — relabel the 15-40% as a hypothetical only reachable by a not-yet-shipping dense-full-attention long-prefix model. 2) Gate the fused-prefill routing behind a MEASURED trigger (attention >X% of wall via nn/profiler.rs), exactly like Design C's honest deferral, so it never wires dormant machinery. 3) Keep only the SDP-priority csrc shim as infra (makes PerfPolicy non-inert), behind a probe+fallback that verifies cuDNN/flash SDPA exists and is faster on sm_121 aarch64 before pinning (the FlashInfer-forbidden rule). 4) Handle mask!=causal: assert seq<=window before substituting is_causal for the sliding-window mask, else keep manual. 5) Keep the WER-gate + flag-guard (WAAV_VOXTRAL_PERF_ATTN) — byte-identity is correctly preserved by flag+decode-stays-manual.

per_design.design_name: Design B — KV-length bucketed graph cache (LRU) + port Fish into the paged long-form escape
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The win projection rests on a max_seq number that is wrong by ~40x. Design B assumes 'voxtral max_seq=16384 avg cur_len~4096' and 'bucketing cuts masked-buffer read 4x (16384->4096)'. The live code sizes the graph ring KV as max_seq = l + n_audio + 1 (voxtral.rs:536) = ~400 for a 30s clip — the buffer is ALREADY right-sized to the clip, not a fixed 16384. So the O(max_seq) read Design B attacks is O(~400), and the residual early-decode waste (reading ~400 when cur_len~50 on a ~400-wide tensor) is a fraction of a tiny slice, not 10-20% of wall. Worse: the proposed power-of-4 buckets {256,1024,4096,16384} would REGRESS voxtral — the smallest bucket >= a ~400-length buffer is 1024, larger than the current 400, so bucketing makes the read bigger. The other graph paths don't have the pathology either: csm/dia2 use append_contiguous_graph (kv_cache.rs:213) which already narrows to cur_len, and the runtime lockstep edge tick reads no full buffer. FILE CONFLATION: Design B targets runtime/cuda_graph.rs EdgeCaptureKey, but that is the backend-FREE TTS lockstep-tick policy module (keys (B,stride_width)); the voxtral Fish path lives in backend-torch nn/cuda_graph.rs + kv_cache.rs::append_full_masked_graph — bucketing EdgeCaptureKey does nothing for voxtral. PART 2 (paged device twin) is a large speculative build: paged_kv.rs has zero live callers, stores HOST Vec<f32> rows (paged_kv.rs:264, no device tensors, no graph mode), so 'give it a device-resident twin + residency_graph + gather-in-graph + a live transcribe() caller' is a from-scratch device subsystem for 'long-form STT' that the models never engage (voxtral chunks 30s; sliding-window-8192 + per-chunk reset cap the KV) — the exact dead-code trap it claims to close, relocated. The byte-identity argument (masked region softmaxes to 0) is correct, so the mechanism is sound where a real large-fixed-buffer exists.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Fix the number: state max_seq = l+n_audio+1 (~400 for 30s), not 16384; re-scope the bucketing win to <1-2% (early-decode-only, on a clip-sized buffer) and gate it measured-first via nn/profiler.rs. 2) Use ADAPTIVE right-sized buckets, never fixed power-of-4 (1024>400 regresses voxtral). 3) Retarget the bucketing to backend-torch nn/cuda_graph.rs + a new bucketed kv_cache variant (narrow k to bucket, mask over arange(bucket)), NOT runtime EdgeCaptureKey. 4) DEFER Part 2 (paged device twin) behind a measured trigger: a shipping unbounded-turn native-S2S model with profiled KV-read >X% of wall — do not build the device pool/gather until then, else it is unwired machinery. 5) Keep the byte-identical cross-bucket RED test — that gate is correct.

per_design.design_name: Design C — Split-K flash-decode for long-context memory-bound attention (HONESTLY DEFERRED)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: This is the only honest design: it refuses to wire, states <1% win on every current model, cites measured occ 0.37, WER-gates the reassociated reduction, and recommends NOT building — it does not fall into the design-vs-wired trap. Two flaws remain. (1) The 'occupancy 0.37->0.8 = 2x the attention kernel slice' overclaims: at kv_len where attention would matter the kernel is memory-bound (AI~1, ridge 433.5), and Design C itself admits it is 'bounded by the memory-bound ceiling (198.5 GB/s)' — raising occupancy does NOT raise the bandwidth ceiling, so more resident SMs buy little throughput for a bandwidth-bound reduction; the 2x is not supported by the physics it cites. (2) The ORT-CUDA-sub-graph-inside-a-tch-decode option resurrects the exact ORT+tch concurrency/ownership deadlock scar in memory (the gdb-proven serve-loop deadlock) for a <1% win — a needless second execution substrate.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Correct the occupancy->throughput claim: for a bandwidth-bound decode-attention, split-K's occupancy gain does not translate to ~2x; project the realistic (near-ceiling) speedup or drop the number. 2) Drop the ORT-sub-graph route entirely (deadlock scar); if ever triggered, use a csrc/CUDA kernel only. 3) Codify the deferral as an automated measured trigger in the perf harness (fire only when a shipping long-form S2S/STT model profiles attention >15% of wall) so the deferral is a live gate, not a comment. Otherwise the honest-deferral posture is correct and should be the template Designs A and B adopt.

verdicts.better_alternative: All three designs chase attention, but the live code proves attention is 1.5-5% of every current model and the two 'big' buffers (voxtral graph KV, TTS contiguous KV) are already right-sized (voxtral.rs:536 max_seq=l+n_audio+1; append_contiguous_graph narrows to cur_len) — so there is no large-fixed-buffer pathology to bucket and no dense long prefill to fuse. The correct move on this gap is a SMALL, MEASURED, WIRED trio, not the three big builds: (1) Land ONLY the SDP-priority csrc shim from Design A as infrastructure (makes PerfPolicy::Flash real, zero model edits), behind a probe+fallback, with NO win claim and NO live routing until a profiler trigger fires — it costs ~30 lines and unblocks any future fused pin. (2) Retire the fused-prefill routing (Design A part 2), the paged device twin (Design B part 2), and split-K (Design C) into a single documented 'attention perf backlog' guarded by ONE shared measured trigger in nn/profiler.rs: build if and only if a shipping model profiles attention >15% of wall (none does today). (3) Redirect the actual perf effort to where the measured 76%-of-wall LAUNCH-bound voxtral decode and the 12,300ms GPU-idle dia2 launch gaps live — i.e. extend CUDA-graph COVERAGE (the proven -13.6% byte-identical lever) and kill the 12 remaining per-frame D2H syncs (cosyvoice3.rs:331, s2_pro.rs:1371, etc.) via the existing on-device sample_token_on_device/index_select — those are byte-identical, already-wired-adjacent, and target the real ridge-point bottleneck instead of a 1.5-5% attention slice. Net: one cheap infra shim + one shared deferral gate + real effort on launch/sync elimination, replacing three roofline projections that do not survive the live max_seq and windowed-encoder numbers.

Precision is the proof-of-concept: adding an int8 whisper = manifest `precision:int8` + weight file, ZERO code (model.rs:1-10 doc). Serving-mode tuning did NOT get the same treatment.

This uniformity is the consolidation seam.

(6) DESIGN-VS-WIRED perf gap: `BatchProfile{Static1,Tens,Wide}` + knee-clamp ([8,64]/[64,512]) (lib.rs:1108-1116) and `RooflineClass`/`StageSpec`/`Paradigm` (lib.rs:1122-1165) are DEFINED but grep finds ZERO non-definition callers — the dispatch never consults the HW knee, so max_slots is hardcoded 24 on every arm regardless of GB10-Wide vs an NPU. Measured basis for the left-on-table perf: device-KV RaggedSlotRing ratio 0.43@B24 (2.34× vs host-KV) with crossover knee ~B8 (per waav-kv-accel memory); lockstep batching measured 55×@64 (task #62/#97). BASIS: this is a code-organization + onboarding-cost gap; it does not itself change any kernel FLOP/s. Its perf leverage is indirect: (a) it UNBLOCKS the HW-adaptive batch-width lever (24→64 on GB10 Wide), and (b) it makes the built-but-dead step-bucket/stage-DAG/advanced-admission wireable per-arch from one table.
dossiers.root_cause: Two registries at two consolidation levels: Path-A/ORT load is declarative (manifest+weights, zero-code for known arch), but Path-B/tch serving-mode tuning was accreted per-model as the Fork-A1 rings landed one-by-one, each adding a copy-pasted engine.rs arm + 2-3 new WAAV_* env vars + an inline ModelSpec/select_perf. No ServingPolicy type and no policy table exist, so the per-(arch,hardware,quant) recipe is hardcoded literals + string-parsed env spread across ~11 files; the BatchProfile HW-knee abstraction that would make batch-width portable was built but never threaded into dispatch (max_slots hardcoded 24 everywhere).

designs.name: Design A — Declarative `serving` block in waav.json + `RingBatchable` trait + one shared applicator (manifest-driven, the extend-the-proven-precision-seam approach)
designs.mechanism: Extend Manifest (model.rs:86) with `serving: ServingPolicy { batcher: Batcher(Solo|RaggedRing|GroupedRing|StepBucket), max_slots: Option<i64>, max_seq: Option<i64>, graph: Tri(Auto|On|Off), perf_mode: Option, default_green: bool, stages: HashMap<stage,StagePolicy> }`, parsed exactly like `device_kv_share` (model.rs:130-142). Introduce `trait RingBatchable { fn into_ring(self: Box<Self>, max_slots, max_seq) -> Box<dyn TtsModel>; }` impl'd ONCE per model (delegates to the existing `Torch<M>Batched::new` — the uniform ctor at higgs.rs:1217 etc.). Collapse the 23 engine.rs arms (305-920): each arm becomes `let m = Torch<M>::load(..)?; Ok(apply_serving(m, arch, &manifest, device, dev_caps))` where the shared `apply_serving()` (new fn) resolves policy = manifest.serving ?? BUILTIN_DEFAULTS[arch] ?? , applies the `WAAV_<M>_BATCHED`/`_MAX_*` env override precedence (keeps escape hatches), clamps max_slots against admission budget, and calls `m.into_ring()` iff `device.is_cuda() && batched`. BUILTIN_DEFAULTS is a `const &[(arch, ServingPolicy)]` table in one module (single source of truth), overridable per-checkpoint by waav.json. The scattered ModelSpec+select_perf (device.rs:136, dia2.rs:1272, neutts.rs:566…) fold into the same policy: `graph` field drives graphable_cuda_graph_enabled; `perf_mode` drives select_perf — one resolution point.
designs.projected_win: Onboarding: a known-arch checkpoint that needs non-default tuning goes from {edit engine.rs arm + edit model .rs ModelSpec + invent 3 env vars} to {one waav.json `serving` block, zero code}. Dispatch LOC: 23 arms × ~30 boilerplate lines → 23 one-liners (~600→~60 net serving lines). Perf (indirect, roofline-grounded): the same table makes `max_slots` HW-adaptive by keying the default on `dev_caps`→BatchProfile knee (lib.rs:1108) — GB10 (Wide [64,512]) default 24→64. Basis: device-KV ratio 0.43@B24 measured (2.34× vs host, crossover ~B8) and lockstep 55×@64 (#62/#97); extending the ring width to the measured Wide knee is the realized lever, projected agg-RTF < the 0.884@B16 already measured. NO kernel change — pure width/policy.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `serving_policy_defaults_match_legacy_dispatch` — for all 23 archs assert resolve_policy(arch, no-manifest, GB10) == the CURRENT hardcoded literals (batched default-green bool, max_slots=24, per-model max_seq from the arms: dia 3088, qwen3 4096, others 2048). Fails until the table exists; enforces the refactor is byte-behavior-identical. (2) `serving_env_override_precedence` — WAAV_<M>_BATCHED=0/1 and _MAX_SLOTS still win over manifest+default (escape hatch preserved). (3) `manifest_serving_overrides_builtin` — a waav.json `serving.max_slots:8` beats the const. designs.name: Design B — Compile-time model registry via a `register_tch_model!` macro (the vLLM ModelRegistry-done-better, type-checked)
designs.mechanism: Replace the hand-match in engine.rs:305-920 with a declarative registry: a `register_tch_model!{ arch: "dia2"|"…", task: Tts, loader: TorchDia2::load, batched: RaggedRing{default_green:true, max_seq:2048}, graphable:true }` macro invoked once per model in a `models/` registry module. The macro generates (a) the arch→loader dispatch entry, (b) the RingBatchable glue, (c) the ModelSpec+graphable wiring, and (d) registers the const ServingPolicy default. `load_torch_inprocess_model` becomes a table lookup `REGISTRY.get(arch).build(dir, manifest, device)`. Env overrides + manifest overrides are applied by the shared build() (same precedence as A). Unlike A, defaults are Rust consts (type-checked, no runtime parse for the built-in), and the `arch` alias list is a macro arg (dedupes the `"dia2"|"DiaForConditionalGeneration"` fan-out).
designs.projected_win: Onboarding a KNOWN-arch new checkpoint: still zero-code (manifest). Onboarding a new SIZE/alias of an existing loader: one macro-arg alias, no new arm. A new arch that reuses an existing wrapper shape: ONE macro line (vs a ~40-line hand arm). Compile-time exhaustiveness: the registry is `HashMap` built once, so a missing loader is a startup error not a silent fallthrough (today's `other =>` at model.rs:916). LOC: eliminates the 23 arms entirely; each model = 1 macro invocation (~6 lines). No direct FLOP/s change; the HW-adaptive width lever from A layers on identically.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `registry_covers_all_archs` — assert REGISTRY.keys() ⊇ the current 23 archs+aliases (mine engine.rs arm heads). (2) `macro_generated_dispatch_equals_legacy` — for each arch, build() with no manifest/env == the legacy wrapper choice (same golden literals as A.1). (3) `unknown_arch_is_startup_error_not_silent`. ACCURACY GATE: identical to A — the per-model force-solo codes-identical oracles (dia2 608, csm 9568, qwen3) stay green; macro emits the SAME ctor calls so numerics are unchanged. PERF GATE: same as A (Wide-knee width + device-KV oracle at B64 max|Δ|=0 + agg-RTF).
designs.coverage: Same universal Path-B coverage as A; additionally unifies the arch-ALIAS handling (the `"ark"|"arkasr"|"ArkasrForConditionalGeneration"` triplets at engine.rs:318). Quant/HW/stage coverage identical to A (macro carries the same ServingPolicy). Path-A ORT could ALSO migrate to the same macro later (out of scope for the first cut). Scoped limit: macro-declared defaults are compile-time, so a per-DEPLOY default change (vs per-checkpoint) needs the manifest override path (which exists) — acceptable.
designs.risks_conflicts: Macro opacity: a proc/decl macro hides control flow — mitigate by keeping it a THIN decl macro that only assembles known pieces (loader fn ptr + policy struct), no logic. Same cfg_batch/ring-OOM/byte-identity risks as A and the same clamps/tests apply (the macro must route width through the admission clamp, not emit a raw 24). DESIGN-VS-WIRED: the registry IS the load path, wired. Bigger blast radius than A (touches every arm at once) — higher one-shot regression risk; the `macro_generated_dispatch_equals_legacy` golden per-arch is the containment. Conflict with G2/G4: same as A — the macro's `batched:` arg must express per-stage partialness (backbone-ring/flow-per-slot), not a single bool, or it silently loses the P1-PARTIAL truth.

designs.name: Design C — Hardware-adaptive ServingPolicy resolver (wire the dead BatchProfile/RooflineClass knee into dispatch) — the perf-bearing layer atop A or B
designs.mechanism: Thread the built-but-dead `BatchProfile` (lib.rs:1108) + `StagePlacer.batch_knee` into policy resolution: `resolve_width(policy, dev_caps) = policy.max_slots.or_else(|| BatchProfile::from(dev_caps).knee_for(paradigm))` — GB10 unified sm_121 → Wide → clamp into [64,512]; a Static1 NPU → 1 (and REJECT AR per the existing Paradigm::Ar rule, lib.rs:1135); Tens → [8,64]. The resolved width then flows into `Torch<M>Batched::new(m, width, max_seq)` and is CLAMPED against CodecArAdmission's per-slot VRAM budget (lib.rs:229) so it can't OOM the shared pool. Also fold the per-stage RooflineClass so a flow/CFM stage can later select the StepBucket batcher (declared, wired in a follow-on). This is not a new dispatch — it's the `default` branch of A/B's resolve_policy made HW-aware instead of the literal 24.
designs.projected_win: The ONLY design here with a direct MEASURED perf lever. Current hardcoded max_slots=24 on GB10 (Wide, measured sweet spot ≥64). Basis: device-KV RaggedSlotRing ratio 0.43@B24 = 2.34× vs host-KV, crossover ~B8, and lockstep 55×@64 (#62/#97); moving the GB10 default 24→64 extends the ring across the measured knee. Roofline check via perf_equations.py: B=1 AR decode AI~1-2 FLOP/byte << ridge 433.5 → memory/launch-bound, so throughput scales with concurrent slots until the KV working set exceeds L2/bandwidth; on 130.6GB unified @198.5GB/s the 240MB/slot budget admits far past 64, so 64 is bandwidth-safe. Projected: agg-throughput ~2.4-2.6× at the wider knee for the device-KV fleet (dia2/qwen3/csm/…), extending the already-measured 0.884 agg-RTF@B16 downward. Portable: a B200 box (Wide, more SMs) auto-picks a higher knee with no code; an NPU auto-picks 1.
designs.tdd_plan: RED FIRST: (1) `wide_profile_default_width_is_knee_not_24` — resolve_width(GB10 caps) ≥ 64; resolve_width(Static1 caps) == 1; Tens ∈[8,64]. (2) `ar_paradigm_rejected_on_static1` (the existing lib.rs:1135 rule, now enforced at dispatch). (3) `resolved_width_clamped_by_admission_budget` — a synthetic 1MB-free device clamps width down, never OOMs. ACCURACY GATE (byte-identical, deterministic): re-run EVERY device-KV codes-identical oracle at the NEW default width (B64): dia2/qwen3/csm must be max|Δ|=0 — widening only adds independent rings, so byte-identity must hold; if any forks, that's a real bug (fail closed to 24). PERF GATE: live serve agg-RTF@B64 < agg-RTF@B24 for ≥3 fleet members, measured on the heavy_live harness, recorded to perf/path-b/.
designs.coverage: Applies to every device-KV-capable Path-B AR model (the default-green fleet: dia2/dia/qwen3/cosyvoice3/voxtral_tts/csm/misotts/s2_pro/dots/indextts2/vibevoice/higgs_v2/neutts). HW: universal — Static1(NPU)/Tens/Wide(GB10/B200) all resolve from caps; CPU→Solo. Quant: orthogonal (width is a slot count, not a precision). Stage: honors the P1-PARTIAL (backbone width scales; per-slot flow/depth/codec unaffected). SCOPED: models NOT on the device-KV ring (pure one-shot flow: irodori/pocket_tts default) keep width 1 — correctly, since their lever is the step-bucket, not the ring.
designs.risks_conflicts: ring-KV OOM (THE dominant risk — the twice-crashed 170GB scar): a naive knee=512 on the 130.6GB unified pool would map far past capacity; the admission clamp (lib.rs:229, 240MB/slot precedent) is MANDATORY and its test (C.3) is the guard — fail-closed to a safe width. cfg_batch batch-2 refusal: unaffected — width adds independent grouped rings, the CFG cond/uncond axis stays the fixed inner [branches,…] (dia2.rs:370), never the slot axis; assert in the B64 oracle. byte-identity: widening must be numerically inert; if the B64 oracle forks it exposes a latent ring bug — that's a WIN (the gate caught it), revert to 24 for that model. lockstep/ChannelId/MaskedCell: untouched. DESIGN-VS-WIRED: this is precisely the fix for the design-vs-wired trap — BatchProfile is DEFINED but has ZERO callers today (grep-confirmed); C makes it live. Must NOT be shipped standalone — it needs A or B's resolver as its host, else it re-scatters.

dossiers.recommended: Ship Design A (manifest `serving` block + `RingBatchable` trait + shared `apply_serving`) as the substrate, with Design C (HW-adaptive BatchProfile width) folded in as the `default`-branch of A's resolver. A is the lowest-blast-radius consolidation that mirrors the already-proven precision/weights/device_kv declarative seam (model.rs) — the same shape the team trusts — and its per-arch golden test (`serving_policy_defaults_match_legacy_dispatch`) makes the refactor provably byte-behavior-identical. C is where the ONLY real perf lives (the measured 24→64 Wide-knee lever, 2.34× device-KV basis) and it is the concrete fix for the design-vs-wired trap (BatchProfile has zero callers today); it MUST ride on A's resolver, not ship standalone. Design B (registry macro) is the cleaner long-term end-state (type-checked, kills the match entirely, unifies alias fan-out) but has a larger one-shot blast radius across all 23 arms — defer it to a follow-on once A's policy type + golden tests exist, then B is a mechanical lift of A's table into a macro. Critical non-negotiable in all three: the policy is PER-STAGE (backbone/depth/flow/codec), not a single model-level `batched` bool, or the consolidation silently erases the G2/G4 P1-PARTIAL truth (backbone-ring + flow-per-slot); and resolved width MUST pass through the CodecArAdmission clamp (the 170GB OOM scar).

(2) `graphable` truth is DUPLICATED: device.rs:167-170 hardcodes with_graphable(true) for the graphable helper AND each model file re-asserts it inline (dia2.rs:1272, neutts.rs:596 with_graphable(false)) — two sources that can drift. (3) 196 distinct WAAV_* env vars is an unmanaged config surface; many are single-use one-offs with no discoverability (no `/v1/config` dump, no schema). (4) The `serving` policy block is the natural, currently-missing home to finally wire the other built-but-dead machinery flagged in the prompt: step-bucket flow batcher (scheduler/cohort.rs), heterogeneous stage-DAG (dag/stage.rs), and advanced admission (admission.rs DutyLedger/KvFirewall) — all built, tested, zero live drivers; G9's per-stage StagePolicy is where they become declarable per-arch (separate impl gaps, but G9 unblocks them). (5) model.rs:916 `other =>` unknown-arch is a runtime error deep in load, not a startup/registry-completeness check — Design B's registry would surface it earlier. (6) The default-green boolean (verified-fleet vs opt-in) is a load-time policy fact buried in prose comments + a literal in each arm; it belongs in the table where the verification status is auditable.

FLAWS: (1) Mis-attributed perf basis. A cites '55×@64 (#62/#97)' AND 'device-KV 0.43@B24 = 2.34×' as one justification for widening 24→64, but these are TWO DIFFERENT REGIMES: 55× is the DEFERRED Phase-6 single-batched lockstep GEMM lever; the shipped device-KV ring runs per-slot B=1 forwards whose win is host-KV re-stream elimination (∝B²), NOT GEMM batching — so widening the per-slot ring does not inherit 55×, and 'projected agg-RTF < 0.884@B16' is unsupported by the cited numbers. (2) The admission clamp A promises is NET-NEW, not preserved: I confirmed the current load path (engine.rs:383) passes max_slots RAW to the alloc-once ctor with NO for_serving clamp; admission shrinking happens at a different serve-time layer. Raising the default pre-allocates that many 240MB/slot rings AT LOAD (the OOM vector, the twice-crashed 170GB scar). (3) B=64 byte-identity is asserted-not-proven — the device-KV oracle is only verified to B24 (cells B∈{1,2,4,8,16,24}).
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Re-scope the perf claim: the ring-width lever is host-KV-re-stream-elimination, NOT the lockstep 55× lever; drop 55×@64 from A's basis or gate any projection on a fresh measured B64 device-KV run. 2) Make the admission clamp MANDATORY inside apply_serving, keyed to KvHeadLayout::per_slot_ring_bytes at serving precision and real free arena, fail-closed to 24; its test (synthetic tiny-arena clamps down, never OOMs) is a ship-gate. 3) Add the B64 device-KV codes-identical oracle (dia2/qwen3/csm max|Δ|=0) as REQUIRED before any default>24; fail-closed to 24 per model on any fork. 4) Keep A.1 as the byte-behavior guard AND assert resolved width never collapses the cond/uncond CFG axis (cfg_batch.rs:13 refusal must remain per-slot B=1). 5) Exclude launch-bound models (dia2 RTF 2.23, gpu_busy 0.06, cuda_api 11.3s, 380K tiny launches) from auto-widen until measured — more slots = more launches on the saturated single-stream CPU dispatch path may regress, not scale.

per_design.design_name: Design B — Compile-time register_tch_model! macro registry
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Same accuracy-neutrality as A: the macro emits the SAME ctor calls, so numerics and the force-solo oracles are unchanged — cannot kill on byte-identity. B additionally FIXES a real latent wart I confirmed: the current 'other =>' fallthrough (engine.rs:1004, not model.rs:916 as the gap stated) is a runtime bail; a compile-time-exhaustive registry turns an unknown/misrouted arch into a startup error (test B.3 writable). FLAWS carried from A verbatim: same mis-attributed 55×/device-KV basis; same NET-NEW (not-preserved) admission clamp; same unproven B64 byte-identity. B-SPECIFIC risk: a decl macro carrying batched as a single flavor (RaggedRing{...}) silently erases the P1-PARTIAL truth (engine.rs:407: backbone-ring + flow/depth/codec PER-SLOT). If the macro arg is one enum not a per-stage map, the G2/G4 hybrid split is lost at consolidation and a future flow-batch wire could cross-request-batch the CFG flow head — tripping cfg_batch.rs:13 (9.5e-7 reassociation flips codes; confirmed real at omnivoice.rs:69). Larger one-shot blast radius (all 23 arms at once) raises regression risk, contained only if B.2 is genuinely per-arch.
per_design.required_fixes: 1)-5) identical to Design A (re-scope perf claim; mandatory fail-closed admission clamp at load; B64 oracle gate; cfg-axis assertion; launch-bound exclusion). 6) The macro's batched descriptor MUST be a per-STAGE policy map (backbone:RaggedRing, flow/depth/codec:PerSlot), never a single bool/enum, or it structurally loses the P1-PARTIAL invariant and opens a cfg_batch violation path. 7) Keep it a THIN decl macro (assembles loader fn-ptr + policy struct only, zero control-flow logic) so the byte-identical ctor calls stay auditable; gate with per-arch macro_generated_dispatch_equals_legacy golden covering every alias triplet (e.g. ark|arkasr|ArkasrForConditionalGeneration).

per_design.design_name: Design C — Hardware-adaptive ServingPolicy resolver (wire BatchProfile knee into dispatch)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: C is the only design touching a numeric-visible default (24→64), so it carries the real accuracy risk — but it breaks no invariant if its gates hold, so not a KILL. Verified StagePlacer::batch_knee clamps Wide→[64,512], Static1→1, Tens→[8,64] (lib.rs:1342-1344) and is TEST-ONLY for the width decision today, so C's 'make it live' premise is accurate. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the gap's own premise: the claim 'BatchProfile/RooflineClass grep finds ZERO non-definition callers' is FALSE — RooflineClass::BandwidthBound has prod callers (engine.rs:1930/1937/2694) and BatchProfile is populated into every EpCaps via cuda_roofline() (lib.rs:919/947); only StagePlacer::batch_knee's WIDTH path is dead. FLAWS (most severe of the three): (1) OVERSTATED number — 'projected agg-throughput ~2.4-2.6× at the wider knee' conflates the host-vs-device RATIO (0.43@B24 = 2.34× vs a WORSE host-KV baseline) with absolute scaling to B64; measured crossover is ~B8 and the realized absolute is agg-RTF 0.884@B16 — NO measurement shows per-slot device-KV throughput climbing 24→64, and on launch-bound members (dia2 gpu_busy 0.06; cosyvoice3 Kernel2 compute 0.010) adding 40 more per-step launches to the saturated CPU-dispatch path likely FLATTENS/REGRESSES. (2) OOM: knee_for(Wide) can return up to 512; at f32 240MB/slot that is 123GB of one model's KV on the 130.6GB SHARED pool, and with S3Gen 21.7GiB transient concurrent this OOMs the box; the load-time clamp (which does NOT exist today — verified) is the only guard. (3) B64 byte-identity unproven (oracle stops at B24). (4) Roofline hand-wave: 'AI 1-2 << ridge 433.5 so bandwidth-safe past 64' is right physics for a compute/BW-bound kernel but the fleet is LAUNCH/CPU-bound, where the binding constraint is CPU API dispatch, not KV bandwidth — so BW-safe does not imply throughput-scaling.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Replace 2.4-2.6× with a MEASURE-FIRST gate: no default>24 ships without live agg-RTF@B64 < agg-RTF@B24 recorded per-model on heavy_live; fail-closed to 24 per model that does not improve (expect dia2/cosyvoice3 to fail and stay at 24). 2) Admission clamp MANDATORY and run AT LOAD before the alloc-once ctor (today it is not), keyed to per_slot_ring_bytes at serving precision and real free arena; cap knee_for output by min(admission, measured B_max) — never emit a raw 512. 3) B64 device-KV codes-identical oracle (dia2/qwen3/csm max|Δ|=0) REQUIRED, with an explicit cfg cond/uncond-axis-preserved assertion (independent per-slot rings must not collapse into a batch-2 GEMM per cfg_batch.rs:13). 4) Never ship C standalone — it must host inside A/B's resolver. 5) Fix the framing: cite the precise dead symbol (StagePlacer::batch_knee width path), not the false 'BatchProfile is dead', to keep the accuracy claim honest.

per_design.design_name: Design A — Declarative serving block + RingBatchable + apply_serving
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The refactor is sound and byte-identical-by-construction; A.1 (resolve_policy==current literals) is writable and I confirmed the exact literals it must match (all max_slots=24; max_seq dia=3088, qwen3=4096, dots=4096, rest=2048; default_green true except pocket_tts/higgs false at engine.rs:723/840). BUT the mechanism describes a UNIFORM eligibility predicate device.is_cuda()&&batched, which is WRONG for qwen3 (engine.rs:454-455): live_serve_green(..)&&(device.is_cuda()||WAAV_QWEN3_BATCHED is set) — it deliberately rides the ring on CPU when env is explicitly set (the CPU-f32 oracle cell); s2_pro/voxtral also carry non-uniform force/fallback semantics. A shared applicator with a hardcoded is_cuda predicate SILENTLY changes qwen3; the golden test as scoped (single default cell) would not catch it. Second flaw: the perf half (24->64 realized lever) is inherited from Design C and rests on an UNMEASURED extrapolation past B24 — A must not present it as a 2.4-2.6x realized win. Minor: cited line numbers are off (BatchProfile is in backend-api lib.rs ~1342 / admission.rs 1301, not scheduler lib.rs:1108) — cosmetic.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Add a per-arch eligibility predicate field to ServingPolicy (cpu_ring_allowed / ring_predicate) so qwen3 CPU-when-env-set, s2_pro B=1 fallback, voxtral force are preserved; never hardcode is_cuda in apply_serving. (2) Extend A.1 to assert the (device,env) MATRIX per arch (CUDA-default, CPU-no-env, CPU-env-set, env=0 override). (3) Keep max_slots default 24 in BUILTIN_DEFAULTS; let C raise it per-model only behind a measured record. (4) Route resolved width through the existing admission clamp (admission.rs ridge_knee/clamp_ridge:1301,1425) fail-closed before into_ring. (5) Assert width never collapses the cond/uncond axis (cfg_batch.rs BatchAxisReducedInGemm is real).

per_design.design_name: Design B — register_tch_model! compile-time registry macro
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: A headline benefit is FALSE against the code: 'unknown arch is a silent fallthrough today' — the actual other=> arm at engine.rs:1004 already anyhow::bail!s with the full expected-arch list, so unknown-arch is already a hard load error, not silent. B's compile-time-exhaustiveness win is therefore a near non-improvement (runtime bail -> startup error, marginal). Same qwen3/s2_pro/voxtral per-arch predicate problem as A: a single batched:RaggedRing{...} macro arg cannot express qwen3's ||env.is_ok() CPU-ring eligibility without an extra field, so the macro would silently normalize it. Macro opacity + one-shot blast radius (all 23 arms at once) raise regression risk over A's incremental path, for a benefit (type-checked consts, alias dedup) that is small relative to A. Perf half inherits C's speculative projection identically.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Drop the 'silent fallthrough' justification — load already bails at engine.rs:1004. (2) Macro must carry a per-arch eligibility/predicate slot (not a single bool); add the same (device,env)-matrix golden as A. (3) Keep it a THIN decl macro (assembles loader fn-ptr + ServingPolicy struct, no logic). (4) Same admission-clamp + cfg-axis assertions as A. Given marginal net gain over A and higher debug/blast cost, prefer A as host and treat B as optional sugar.

per_design.design_name: Design C — Hardware-adaptive ServingPolicy resolver (wire BatchProfile knee into dispatch)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The abstraction (thread BatchProfile.ridge_knee into resolve_width; NPU->1/reject-AR, Tens->[8,64], Wide->[64,512]) is correct and the machinery exists (admission.rs ridge_knee/clamp_ridge). But the PERF PROJECTION — the only claimed direct lever — is unsound on three measured counts: (a) EXTRAPOLATION: the device-KV RaggedSlotRing matrix was measured only to B24 (ratio 0.43@B24); '2.4-2.6x at the B64 knee' extrapolates past every measured point. (b) MISATTRIBUTED BASIS: it fuses '55x@64 (#62/#97)' as evidence, but that 55x is the DEFERRED Phase-6 SINGLE-BATCHED lockstep lever — a different regime — NOT the per-slot B=1 device-KV ring that is wired; the kv-accel memory explicitly says the ~30x/single-batched win is NOT reproduced and the shipped win is host-KV-restream elimination (proportional to B^2 memory traffic), not compute scaling. (c) ROOFLINE STORY CONTRADICTED BY ON-BOX DATA: C argues AI~1-2<<433.5 => memory-bound => scales with slots, but the measured reality is LAUNCH/CPU-bound (dia2 gpu_busy 0.06 / cpu_busy 0.89 / ~12300ms GPU-idle, ~380K tiny launches). The ring does per-slot B=1 forwards, so widening slots MULTIPLIES launch count and, for the 12 models still doing per-frame D2H sync (csm/misotts 32/frame, qwen3 16/frame, cosyvoice3/s2_pro/zonos2), multiplies the D2H stall — plausibly NEGATIVE at B64 for exactly those. So 64 is an untested hypothesis, not a measured sweet spot for the wired regime. Also 'BatchProfile has ZERO callers' is imprecise: it IS used in admission/roofline (cuda_roofline, SubstrateRoofline, ridge_knee); only the dispatch->knee link is missing.
per_design.required_fixes: (1) Delete the projected magnitude; relabel as a MEASURE-GATED hypothesis. Keep C's perf gate (agg-RTF@B64<@B24 for >=3 members + codes-identical@B64 max|delta|=0) but as the ADMISSION condition to raise a per-model default — default stays 24 until a perf/path-b/<model> B64 record exists. (2) QUARANTINE the sync-heavy fleet: do NOT default-widen the 12 per-frame-D2H models until their sync is removed; scope the knee-default to already sync-free device-KV models (dia2 confirmed sync-free). (3) Never ship C standalone — host it in A's resolver default branch. (4) Keep the admission clamp fail-closed (170GB unified-pool scar): resolved width must pass CodecArAdmission before into_ring. (5) State BatchProfile's real status precisely: wired in admission/roofline, missing only the dispatch link.

verdicts.better_alternative: Ship A as the host and fold C in MEASURE-GATED; skip B. (1) Add a declarative `serving` block to the Manifest exactly like device_kv_share, with a BUILTIN_DEFAULTS const table that byte-reproduces the current per-arm literals (all max_slots=24; max_seq dia=3088, qwen3=4096, dots=4096, rest=2048; default_green true except pocket_tts/higgs). CRUCIAL: the policy must carry a per-arch eligibility predicate (NOT a hardcoded is_cuda) so qwen3's CPU-ring-when-env-set (engine.rs:454-455), s2_pro's B=1 fallback, and voxtral's force-semantics survive — I verified these arms are NOT uniform. (2) Collapse the 23 arms to apply_serving(m, arch, manifest, device, dev_caps) behind a per-(device,env)-MATRIX golden equivalence test, not a single-cell one. (3) Route resolved width through the EXISTING admission clamp (admission.rs ridge_knee/clamp_ridge) fail-closed. (4) Fold C's BatchProfile-knee as the resolver default branch but leave the per-model default at 24 until a per-(model,hardware) record in perf/path-b/ proves agg-RTF@B64<@B24 AND codes-identical@B64 (max|delta|=0); the wide knee auto-raises the default ONLY from that record. (5) Quarantine the 12 per-frame-D2H-sync models from auto-widening — their real lever is on-device sampling to kill the 16-32 syncs/frame, not more slots, because the on-box truth is launch/CPU-bound (dia2 cpu_busy 0.89, ~380K tiny launches). This makes the HW-knee portable (NPU->1, Tens->[8,64], Wide->[64,512]) and onboarding declarative while keeping every perf claim gated on measurement rather than extrapolation past B24. Drop B: its exhaustiveness benefit is a non-problem (load already bails at engine.rs:1004) and its macro debuggability/blast-radius cost exceeds A's. Files: crates/waav-infer-server/src/engine.rs:257-1004, crates/waav-infer-core/src/model.rs:86, crates/waav-infer-scheduler/src/admission.rs:1301-1445, crates/waav-infer-backend-api/src/lib.rs:856-1344, crates/waav-infer-runtime/src/cfg_batch.rs.

DESIGN-VS-WIRED TRAP — measured live-caller audit (grep of production paths):

The loop-half is wired; the model-half is dormant. This is the subtle trap.
- cfg_batch.rs CfgBatchPlan is enrolled in PERF_GATED_LEVERS (cfg_batch.rs:322) but is pure host POLICY with no verified live sidecar _logits_cfg2 caller in-repo.

- StepBuckets wired for irodori.rs only; the 12 hybrid streaming models keep the flow head PER-SLOT (engine.rs:407 "P1-PARTIAL"). dia2.rs:1157 set_cuda_graph(false) DISABLES the backbone graph in batched serve rather than bucketing it.
dossiers.root_cause:
There is no single serialized statement of invariant PRECEDENCE, and no mechanism that forces new machinery to prove it has a live serve-path caller. Two failures compound: (1) conflicts between gaps are resolved ad-hoc per-module (cfg_batch refuses batch-stacking; dia2 just disables its graph; streaming seam exists but no model implements the causal half) instead of against one lattice; (2) WaaV's superb won't-compile discipline (typed CfgBatchRefusal, MaskedCell) gates CORRECTNESS but nothing gates WIRED-NESS — a capability can be byte-identical-tested and enrolled in PERF_GATED_LEVERS yet never touch the serve path, so the recurring "out-designs vLLM-Omni but leaves it dormant" outcome is structurally unpunished.

The correct invariant hierarchy (highest wins; a lower lever that would violate a higher tier is REFUSED at construction or routed to an explicit WER/MOS opt-in, NEVER silently):
  1. Byte-identity-by-default (accuracy/reproducibility golden gate) — arstep.rs:551, cfg_batch.rs:177.
  2. Per-slot isolation + masked≠absent state-safety (privacy/correctness) — ring_kv MaskedCell, ChannelId.
  3. Lockstep 1-stride/tick (the batching contract).
  4. Unified-pool OOM-safety (hard box-crash floor) — codec_ar_admission.rs:75.
  5. Perf levers (CUDA-graph, ragged-batch, quant, streaming) — LOWEST, each gated by 1-4.

Conflict-resolution matrix: G1 streaming vs byte-identity → decoder-causality split (causal=byte-identical wire; non-causal=WER/MOS opt-in). G2 flow-batch CFG vs cfg_batch refusal → per-slot B=1 device-resident dispatch (Fork-A1 forward_ring), NEVER batch-stacked on the CFG axis. G4 static-graph vs G2 ragged membership vs lockstep → graph-capture-safe padded worst-case grid + exec-mask membership (Fish protocol). G6 quant vs byte-identity → quant is a WER/MOS-stamped admission gate, byte-identity stays the golden/verification mode (the proven two-tier bar). G5 multi-stage vs OOM vs ring-KV → every stage transient inside VramAccountant+MIN_FREE_BYTES; per-slot ring-KV at native GQA g-heads (ring_kv.rs:126 kv_footprint); no full-engine-per-stage (reject vLLM's 22GB bug).

designs.name: WIRED-LEDGER: a compile+CI gate that forbids dormant machinery (the meta-resolution)
designs.mechanism: Add a `LiveWired` registry mirroring the existing PERF_GATED_LEVERS pattern (cfg_batch.rs:322). Every enrolled capability — each PerfLever, each ArStepModel streaming-seam override (decode_committed_prefix arstep.rs:615 / decode_audio_stream arstep.rs:570), each advanced-admission component (LayeredAdmit/DriftDetector/KvFirewall), each step-bucket flow batcher — carries a `fn live_callers() -> &'static [LiveCallerProof]` that names a PRODUCTION serve-path entry (not a test). A single workspace CI test `no_dormant_machinery` walks the registry and FAILS if any capability's live_callers() is empty OR if every proof resolves only to a #[cfg(test)] symbol (checked via a build-time attribute macro that stamps prod vs test provenance). Complement with a serve-path integration harness: for each enrolled seam, drive the REAL model through run_serial_one (harness.rs, already the cfg_batch gate driver) end-to-end and assert the capability's code path was actually entered (a hit-counter on the lever, read after the serve call). This converts 'built + unit-tested' into 'built + wired + exercised on the live loop' as a red-bar gate. DutyLedger (engine.rs:2689) is the reference implementation of a correctly-wired lever and seeds the first passing entry.
designs.projected_win: No FLOP win directly; it unlocks the other gaps' wins by preventing regression to dormancy. Concretely: it is the gate that FORCES the G1 streaming win (below) to ship — without it, decode_committed_prefix stays a no-op and TTFA remains == whole-utterance (dia2 wall_s basis: ~1.07s active vs ~13.4s device_ms; a causal early-emit at cadence 8 frames @12.5Hz codec ≈ 0.64s first-audio vs whole-utterance). Basis: measured serve.rs:999 is already wired but 0 models override → the ledger makes that 0 a CI failure.
designs.tdd_plan: RED-first: (1) `no_dormant_machinery_fails_on_empty_live_callers` — register a fake lever with empty live_callers(), assert the CI walker returns Err naming it. (2) `streaming_seam_requires_live_override` — assert at least one production ArStepModel (a causal codec: SNAC/Mimi) resolves decode_committed_prefix to a non-default impl; RED until Design 2 lands. (3) `lever_exercised_on_serve_path` — drive real model via run_serial_one, assert the lever hit-counter > 0. Accuracy gate: none new (meta). Perf gate: the walker adds <1ms to CI; the exercised-path test reuses existing serve harness.
designs.coverage: UNIVERSAL across every arch/stage/quant/backend — it is a registry discipline, not model-specific. Path-A(ORT) and Path-B(tch) both enrol. Scoped only in that it gates capabilities that CHOOSE to enrol; a hard-CI rule (any pub type named *Lever/*Admit/*Batcher/seam override must enrol or be #[allow(dormant)] with a tracking issue) closes the escape hatch.
designs.risks_conflicts: Risk: over-strict gate blocks legitimately-staged milestones (e.g. a seam landed one milestone before its model override). Mitigation: an explicit `#[dormant(reason,issue)]` escape that the walker COUNTS and reports (so dormancy is visible, never silent) — matching the honest-labeling discipline. No conflict with byte-identity/lockstep/ring-KV/cfg_batch (adds no numeric path). The design-vs-wired trap is exactly what it targets: it wires into the LIVE serve path by construction (its own test IS a serve-path assertion).

designs.name: CAUSALITY-TYPED STREAMING SPLIT: resolve G1 (streaming/left-context) vs the byte-identity LAW
designs.mechanism: Add a `DecoderCausality` descriptor to each codec-AR model: `Causal{ receptive_field_frames }` (SNAC/Mimi causal codecs) | `NonCausal` (chatterbox S3Gen bidirectional UpsampleConformer+CFM U-Net, dia2 Mimi length-dependent conv-pad). Causal models MUST override decode_committed_prefix (arstep.rs:615) to decode the prefix whose receptive field is fully inside the committed region — this is BYTE-IDENTICAL to whole-body decode by construction (the law at arstep.rs:598), and it flows straight through the already-wired mux loop (serve.rs:999). NonCausal models get a SEPARATE, explicit opt-in `StreamingRelaxation::LeftContext{ left_frames, right_holdback }` (vLLM-Omni's chunk taxonomy, stolen as algorithm) that is DEFAULT-OFF and admitted only behind a passing WER/MOS stamp — never the silent default. The type makes it impossible for a NonCausal model to fake incrementality (no override path compiles into the byte-identical seam; the only streaming it can do is the stamped relaxation).
designs.projected_win: For causal codecs: first-audio pulled from whole-utterance to ~cadence latency. dia2 basis: whole-utterance wall ~1.07s active GPU; F6 cadence=8 frames at a 12.5Hz codec ≈ 0.64s of audio produced before first emit today → early-emit gives TTFA ≈ 0.5-0.7s vs full utterance. For a 5s utterance (cosyvoice3 audio_s 4.9775) a causal codec streaming at cadence 8 cuts TTFP from ~3.34s (wall_s) to ~0.3-0.5s — the #1 realized-latency gap. NonCausal: no byte-identical win (honest), WER/MOS-gated relaxation only where a customer opts in.
designs.tdd_plan: RED-first: (1) `causal_codec_prefix_byte_identical` — for a SNAC/Mimi-causal model, assert Σ(decode_committed_prefix deltas)+flush == decode_audio(full_body) byte-for-byte (extends the existing cuda_torch_csm_streaming.rs:125 pattern to a POSITIVE causal case, currently only the negative no-op is tested). (2) `noncausal_rejects_byte_identical_streaming` — assert a NonCausal model CANNOT be constructed with a decode_committed_prefix override (compile-witness / typed reject). (3) `left_context_relaxation_gated_by_wer` — the opt-in path admits only with a WER/MOS stamp; RED until the quant-admission-style gate is reused. Accuracy gate: byte-identical for causal; WER (≤ measured native + epsilon) / MOS for the NonCausal relaxation. Perf gate: TTFA at cadence measured on the live loop < whole-utterance.
designs.coverage: Covers ALL codec-AR TTS/S2S. Causal path: SNAC (Orpheus), Mimi-causal, any strictly-causal codec — UNIVERSAL byte-identical streaming. NonCausal path: S3Gen/chatterbox, dia2-Mimi, DAC — honestly scoped to a WER/MOS opt-in. One-shot models (kokoro/whisper) N/A (no AR loop). Both Path-A and Path-B.
designs.risks_conflicts: Conflict with byte-identity LAW: RESOLVED by construction — causal path IS byte-identical, non-causal path is the explicitly-relaxed WER/MOS tier (respects the two-tier bar). No lockstep conflict (per-slot decode, cadence-gated). Ring-KV/ChannelId untouched. cfg_batch: N/A (this is the decode leg, not the CFG backbone). Design-vs-wired: the loop is ALREADY wired (serve.rs:999); this design lands the missing MODEL half + the CI gate (Design 1) forces it live.

designs.name: GRAPH-CAPTURE-SAFE PADDED RING: resolve G4 static-graph vs G2 ragged membership vs lockstep vs cfg_batch
designs.mechanism: Replace the dia2.rs:1157 set_cuda_graph(false) cop-out with a Fish-style graph-capture-safe protocol. Capture ONE static worst-case grid per (arch, ctx-bucket): CPU-precomputed upper-bound seq_lens → static worst-case grid at capture → real seq-len only inside the kernel; ragged batch MEMBERSHIP is expressed via the exec-mask (a masked slot is FROZEN but still replayed — exactly ring_kv.rs:171 append_where's F2 no-op semantics, so a masked row's ring head does not advance). Each per-slot dispatch stays B=1 on the CFG/AR axis (the Fork-A1 forward_ring pattern, index_copy_ KV in place) so the batch index NEVER enters a reducing GEMM — satisfying cfg_batch.rs:177 CfgBatchRefusal by construction. Add an LRU graph cache keyed by ctx-bucket with eviction + RNG-buffer-refill-before-replay (capture_preserving_rng already snapshots Philox, nn/cuda_graph.rs:147) + scalar-placeholder runtime controls (cfg/sigma/temp tunable without recapture) to kill the dots re-capture thrash noted in the summary.
designs.projected_win: dia2 measured: graph-off 2.2309 → byte-identical partial-graph 1.859 (-16.7%) TODAY but the BACKBONE graph is disabled under batched serve. Enabling a capture-safe backbone graph in the batched path recovers the same class of launch-elimination at B>1 where it is currently forfeited. Roofline basis: dia2 is 60.8% GPU-idle / 4.13M tiny launches (launch-bound, AI≪433.5); graph replay collapses per-kernel launch latency. Conservative projection: restore the ~-13.6% backbone-graph win at batch (from the solo-path measurement) on top of ragged batching, without the byte-identity loss TRT-both incurred (1.99, WORSE). Not a promise of RTF<1 alone; composes with depformer work.
designs.tdd_plan: RED-first: (1) `padded_graph_ragged_codes_identical` — a ragged cohort (mixed seq-lens) through the padded static-grid graph emits codes byte-identical to per-slot eager (extends the Fork-A1 force-solo oracle, e.g. dia2 task #105). (2) `masked_slot_frozen_under_graph_replay` — a masked row in the captured grid advances neither its ring head (ring_kv F2) nor its output (assert byte-identical to a never-scheduled slot). (3) `graph_cache_no_recapture_on_scalar_change` — changing cfg/temp does NOT re-capture (placeholder path). Accuracy gate: byte-identical codes (AR-compounding identity, the ONE standing gate). Perf gate: batched-serve RTF with backbone graph ON < graph-OFF, measured on GB10.
designs.coverage: The 4 graphable archs today (dia2/csm/omnivoice/dots) + extends to any codec-AR whose backbone is fixed-shape per ctx-bucket. tch-only (Path-B) — tch cannot drive torch.compile/Dynamo, so this is the ONLY route to graph capture in Rust (honest scope). Path-A(ORT) uses its own IoBinding/StaticGraph seam, out of scope here. Non-graphable growing-narrow decoders (csm-backbone, higgs) correctly stay eager (not forced).
designs.risks_conflicts: cfg_batch.rs:177 refusal: RESPECTED — per-slot B=1 dispatch keeps the batch index out of the reducing GEMM (no batch-2 cuBLAS reassociation). Lockstep: RESPECTED — one replay per tick per cohort. Ring-KV: the exec-mask membership maps exactly to append_where(active). OOM: the static worst-case grid pins a fixed capture mempool — must be sized inside VramAccountant + MIN_FREE_BYTES (codec_ar_admission.rs:75) or the capture itself can OOM the unified pool (the G4↔G5 collision — a real risk this design must budget). Design-vs-wired: MUST land a live caller replacing dia2.rs:1157, else it repeats the trap (Design 1's gate enforces this).

dossiers.recommended: Design 1 (WIRED-LEDGER CI gate) is the primary and highest-leverage — it is the direct resolution of the gap's core measured finding (WaaV out-designs vLLM-Omni but leaves machinery dormant) and it is a precondition that FORCES Designs 2 and 3 to actually ship on the serve path rather than regressing to unit-tested-but-dormant. It is cheap, universal, and adds no numeric risk. Design 2 (causality-typed streaming split) is the highest-VALUE functional win it unlocks (the #1 realized-latency gap: TTFA==whole-utterance today because the serve.rs:999 loop is wired but no model overrides the causal half). Design 3 (padded graph ring) is the highest-effort/highest-conflict-surface and should land last, behind Design 1's gate and budgeted against the OOM floor. Sequence: 1 → 2 → 3. The invariant hierarchy (byte-identity > state-safety > lockstep > OOM-floor > perf-levers) and the conflict matrix in root_cause are the governing artifact all three encode against.
dossiers.other_gaps_found: 1. STALE SUMMARY: the prompt claims 'advanced admission NOT wired' but DutyLedger IS wired live (engine.rs:2689, gate #9/#10). The dormant ones are LayeredAdmit/DriftDetector/KvFirewall (scheduler/lib.rs re-exports only). Any G-plan citing the summary should re-verify. 2. The decode_committed_prefix trap is INVERTED from the summary: the loop-half IS wired (serve.rs:999), the MODEL-half is the dead code — no production ArStepModel overrides it (grep: only serve.rs:3416 test-double). 3. G4↔G5 collision the summary understates: a CUDA-graph's static-worst-case capture mempool is itself a large transient that must be inside the MIN_FREE_BYTES=28GiB floor (codec_ar_admission.rs:75) or capture OOMs the unified pool — the same class as the 21.7GiB S3Gen scar. 4. cfg_batch.rs is a pure host POLICY object with no verified live _logits_cfg2 sidecar caller in-repo — a design-vs-wired risk hiding behind a passing PERF_GATED_LEVERS enrolment (the gate proves the POLICY is bit-identical, not that the sidecar reads it). 5. F6_DECODE_CADENCE_FRAMES=8 is NOT inert (as the summary states) — it actively gates serve.rs:997; it is the MODEL overrides that are inert.

per_design.design_name: WIRED-LEDGER: compile+CI gate forbidding dormant machinery
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: On the accuracy/invariants axis it adds NO numeric path, so it cannot break byte-identity, lockstep, ring-KV, cfg_batch, or ChannelId state-safety — verified pure host/CI policy; it survives the lens. But two correctness flaws. (1) SELF-REFUTING PROOF SURFACE: its own `lever_exercised_on_serve_path` test drives models through run_serial_one (harness.rs), which IS a #[cfg(test)] harness, not the production mux loop (verified serve.rs:999 stream_committed_prefix on F6_DECODE_CADENCE_FRAMES=8; the ONLY decode_committed_prefix override in-repo is serve.rs:3416, a test double). So the ledger's rule 'live_callers must name a PRODUCTION serve-path, not a test' is violated by the ledger's own exerciser — it would stamp run_serial_one as 'live' and re-normalize exactly the dormancy it targets. (2) THE PROVENANCE MACRO IS INFEASIBLE AS DESCRIBED: a proc-macro sees only its own token stream and cannot resolve whether a &'static symbol ultimately links to a #[cfg(test)] item; the walker test itself runs under cfg(test) where prod and test symbols coexist in one binary. There is no clean Rust mechanism to reject 'resolves only to a cfg(test) symbol' at build time. Test #1 (empty live_callers -> Err) CAN be written; test #3 CANNOT be written faithfully. (3) The #[dormant] escape is unbounded ('counts and reports' does not prevent renormalization). No invariant is broken, so not a KILL.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) The exercised-path proof MUST drive the real serve.rs mux loop (the stream_committed_prefix + drain paths) and read the lever hit-counter after — NOT run_serial_one, else it certifies harness-only wiring as 'live'. 2) Replace the infeasible provenance macro with linkme/inventory collection gated OUT of cfg(test) (submit! excluded from test builds) plus a call-graph-reachability assertion from the serve binary; or downgrade the claim to a runtime hit-counter asserted after a real-loop drive. 3) Bound #[dormant] with a hard milestone expiry so a capability cannot stay dormant-but-green forever. 4) Keep it labeled meta: projected_win borrows Design 2's numbers, delivers zero accuracy/perf win itself.

per_design.design_name: CAUSALITY-TYPED STREAMING SPLIT (G1 vs byte-identity)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: The MECHANISM respects the byte-identity LAW by construction (Σ deltas == decode_audio, verified arstep.rs:598-624) and is the correct G1 resolution: causal = byte-identical wire, non-causal = DEFAULT-OFF WER/MOS relaxation. It breaks no invariant. But the accuracy CLAIM is attached to the wrong models and one test cannot be written. (1) TAXONOMY ERROR: it lists 'SNAC/Mimi causal codecs' on the byte-identical path, but the repo's own arstep.rs doc (verified) states Mimi is EMPIRICALLY NON-CAUSAL — 'decode(body[..p]) differs from decode(body)[..p] at sample 0 in BOTH bf16 and f32, the length-dependent _get_extra_padding_for_conv1d right-pad'; the design itself elsewhere calls dia2-Mimi NonCausal (internally contradictory). (2) NO SHIPPED CAUSAL MODEL: verified no SNAC/Orpheus in backend-torch/src; all shipped codecs are Mimi-family (dia2/s2_pro/qwen3_tts/pocket_tts — per-layer causal left-pad but length-dependent, non-causal whole-utterance decode), chatterbox S3Gen (non-causal), DAC (symmetric-pad). So the byte-identical causal path has ZERO overrides today = dormant-by-construction, the exact trap it claims to escape. (3) PROJECTED WIN USES NON-CAUSAL MODELS: the headline TTFA numbers are dia2 (~0.64s) and cosyvoice3 (~0.3-0.5s), both NON-CAUSAL, so those gains legitimately belong ONLY to the WER/MOS tier, not the 'byte-identical by construction' claim. (4) TEST #2 CANNOT BE A COMPILE REJECT: decode_committed_prefix is a DEFAULT method on the shared ArStepModel trait (verified arstep.rs:615) — any model can override it; there is no compile-witness forbidding a NonCausal override without splitting the seam into a Causal-only sub-trait.
per_design.required_fixes: 1) Reclassify ALL Mimi-family + S3Gen + DAC as NonCausal; recompute projected_win — the byte-identical causal win is 0s on the current fleet; state honestly. 2) To ship a real byte-identical win, first ONBOARD a genuinely causal codec (SNAC/Orpheus) or PROVE a shipped Mimi decode is causal to a frame boundary via test #1 on real weights before claiming it. 3) Make test #2 real by extracting decode_committed_prefix into a CausalDecoder sub-trait implemented only by proven-causal models (matching the CfgBatchRefusal/MaskedCell won't-compile discipline), else downgrade to a runtime/registry assertion and admit it is not a compile-witness. 4) Route the LeftContext relaxation through the existing quant-admission WER/MOS stamp gate (reuse), default-off.

per_design.design_name: GRAPH-CAPTURE-SAFE PADDED RING (G4 vs G2 vs lockstep vs cfg_batch)
per_design.kill_or_flaw_reasons: Weakest on the accuracy axis, near-KILL as written. (1) CENTRAL MECHANISM COLLIDES WITH cfg_batch: it claims BOTH a 'static worst-case grid' with 'ragged batch MEMBERSHIP via exec-mask' (a BATCHED grid over slots) AND 'each per-slot dispatch stays B=1'. These are mutually exclusive for the claimed win. If the grid batches slots into a [B_worstcase,...] backbone GEMM, the batch axis enters a reducing GEMM — the exact #2274 trap cfg_batch.rs:177-211 REFUSES at construction (measured maxΔ 3.9e-4 TF32 flips codes). Worse, PADDING active rows to a worst-case shape changes cuBLAS kernel/tiling selection and reduction order for the ACTIVE rows, so even 'frozen' masked padding rows perturb active-row numerics and fork the AR trajectory; the design's own test #1 padded_graph_ragged_codes_identical would FAIL. The design flags the G4<->G5 OOM collision but MISSES this fatal shape-driven numeric-drift collision. (2) If instead every dispatch is truly B=1, there is NO cross-slot launch elimination — it degenerates to per-slot B=1 replay ~ the existing solo capture; the projected -13.6%/-16.7% recovery does not follow because dia2 forward_ring_grouped is 'graph-INCOMPATIBLE: dynamic per-slot membership' (verified dia2.rs) and that win came from the SOLO path. (3) COVERAGE OVERSTATED: claims dia2/csm/omnivoice/dots + any fixed-shape codec-AR backbone, but omnivoice/dots are bidirectional DIFFUSION graphs (not codec-AR ragged backbones) and csm-backbone is growing-narrow/non-graphable per engine memory — so the real shipped target is essentially dia2 alone. Invariants otherwise respected only in the per-slot-B=1 variant (lockstep one-replay/tick OK; masked row maps to ring_kv append_where(active) F2 freeze correctly).
per_design.required_fixes: 1) DROP the shared padded BATCHED grid; do per-slot B=1 CUDA-graph replay inside the batched loop (one B=1 capture per ctx-bucket, replayed per active slot) so NO padding row enters a shared reducing GEMM — the only variant satisfying cfg_batch.rs:177; state the honest smaller win (per-slot launch elimination). 2) If any shared grid is kept, PROVE byte-identity via the standing AR-compounding integer-codes gate at no-TF32 and route TF32-on strictly through a WER/MOS opt-in, never silently. 3) Test #1 must compare padded-graph codes to the UN-padded eager B=1 oracle (not another padded run) so shape-driven reassociation is caught; test #2 must assert a masked padding row changes NEITHER its own output NOR any active row's codes. 4) Size the static capture mempool inside VramAccountant + MIN_FREE_BYTES (codec_ar_admission.rs:75) — admit the fixed capture pool, do not allocate blind. 5) Restrict coverage to shipped codec-AR ragged backbones (dia2) and land a live caller replacing dia2.rs:1157 (enforced by Design 1's gate) or it repeats the dormancy trap.
